translation.quality: The source edition describes its English as machine-assisted and post-edited and cautions that errors may remain. These passages were extracted from the al-Tabari-labeled sections; they have not been independently checked against the Arabic.

x: Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn Jarir said: We have mentioned the differences of opinion among the people of interpretation regarding the interpretation of His statement: “Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Book,” and the statement that we choose regarding the interpretation of that has already been made, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. As for his saying:
h
These are the verses of the clear Book
, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of it.
Some of them said: Its meaning is:
h
These are the verses of the clear Book
, which explains what is permissible and what is forbidden, and what is right and proper.
Who said that?

c: Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me, he said, Al-Walid bin Salamah Al-Filistini told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab bin Mujahid told me, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding the statement of God: “Alif, Lam, Ra.
h
These are the verses of the clear Book
,” he said: between what is permissible and what is forbidden.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “Alif, Lam, Ra.
h
These are the verses of the clear Book
,” yes, by God, clear, God made clear His guidance and right direction.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “Alif, Lam, Ra.
h
These are the verses of the clear Book
,” he said: God made clear his guidance and his direction.

x: Others said about this:

c: Saeed bin Amr Al-Kiswani told me, he said, Al-Walid bin Salamah told us, he said, Thawr bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, on the authority of Muadh: that he said
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: The clear Book, he said: He explained the letters that were dropped from the tongues of the non-Arabs, and they are the sunnah of letters.

x: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is to say: Its meaning is: These are the verses of the Book that make it clear to whoever recites it and ponders what is in it, of what is permissible, what is forbidden, what is prohibited, and all the other types of meanings it contains, because God, may He be glorified and exalted, informed us that it is clear, and He did not specify that it is clear about some of what is in it without all of it. So that applies to all of it, since all of it makes clear what is in it.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is to say: Its meaning is: These are the verses of the Book that make it clear to whoever recites it and ponders what is in it, of what is permissible, what is forbidden, what is prohibited, and all the other types of meanings it contains, because God, may He be glorified and exalted, informed us that it is clear, and He did not specify that it is clear about some of what is in it without all of it.

x: God Almighty says: We have sent down this clear book, an Arabic Qur’an, to the Arabs, because their language and speech are Arabic. So We sent down this book in their language so that they may understand it and comprehend it, and that is His saying:
h
So that you may understand

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: We relate to you, O Muhammad, the best of stories, by revealing to you this Qur’an, so that we inform you in it of past report, and report of previous nations, and the books that we revealed in past ages, and you were, before it, among the unaware, God Almighty says: And you, O Muhammad, before We revealed it to you, were among the unaware of that, not knowing it or anything of it, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: We relate to you the best of stories, from the past books, and the past affairs of God among the nations, and you were, before that, among the unaware. He mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when his companions asked him to tell them a story. The novel mentioned that:

c: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi told me, he said, Hakam Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Amr Al-Mala’i, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: They said, O Messenger of God, why don’t you tell us a story? He said: So this was revealed: We relate to you the best of stories.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Ayoub bin Sayyar Abu Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Amr bin Qais, he said:
m: They said: O Prophet of God, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, my father narrated, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Awn ibn Abdullah, who said: “The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were bored with one religion and said: O Messenger of God, tell us. So God Almighty revealed: God has sent down the best statement. Then they were bored with another religion and said: O Messenger of God, tell us something above the statement and below the Qur’an, meaning stories. So God revealed: (Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book. Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’an that you may understand. We relate to you the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur’an, although you were, before it, among the unaware.) So they wanted the statement, so he guided them to the best statement, and they wanted the stories, so he guided them to the best of stories.” Muhammad ibn Saʿid al-ʿAttar narrated, ʿAmr ibn Muhammad narrated, Khallad al-Saffar informed us, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Qays, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Musʿab ibn Saʿd, on the authority of Saʿd, who said: The Qur’an was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He recited it to them for a period of time, and they said: O Messenger of God, if only you would tell us a story. Then God revealed: “Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book,” to His saying: that you may understand, the verse. He said: Then he recited it to them for a period of time, and they said: O Messenger of God, if only you would tell us a story. Then God revealed: God has sent down the best statement, a consistent Book. Khallad said: Another man added to it. They said: O Messenger of God - or Abu Yahya said: A word has been lost from my book - so God revealed: Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God?

evidence.text: He recited it to them for a period of time, and they said: O Messenger of God, if only you would tell us a story.
He said: Then he recited it to them for a period of time, and they said: O Messenger of God, if only you would tell us a story.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And if you, O Muhammad, are among those who are unaware of the report of Joseph, son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, when he said to his father Jacob, son of Isaac:
h
O my father
h
I saw eleven stars
, meaning:
h
I saw eleven stars
in my dream. It was said: The vision of the prophets was a revelation.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “Indeed,
h
I saw eleven stars
h
and the sun and the moon
. I saw them prostrating to me,” he said: The vision of the prophets was revelation.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
I saw eleven stars
, he said: The vision was a revelation among them. He mentioned that the eleven planets that he saw in his dream prostrating with the sun and the moon, are:

c: Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi told me, he said, Al-Hakam bin Dhahir told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Sabit, on the authority of Jabir, he said:
m: “A Jewish man called Bustanah Al-Yahudi came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: O Muhammad, tell me about the stars that Joseph saw prostrating to him, what are their names? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent and did not answer him with anything, and Gabriel came down to him and told him their names. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for him and said: Are you a believer if I tell you their names? He said: Yes. He said: Jiryan, Al-Kariq, Al-Dhiyal, Dhu Al-Kanafat, Qabis, Wathab, Amudan, Al-Faliq, Al-Misbah, Al-Dharuh, Dhu Al-Fargh, Al-Dhiya, and Al-Nur. The Jew said: By God, these are their names.” And his saying:
h
And the sun and the moon
, I saw them prostrating to me, means:
h
And the sun and the moon

, I saw them prostrating in my dream. He said: Prostrating. The planets, the sun, and the moon are only described by fa’ila and fa’ilat, not by waw and nun, because waw and nun are only a sign of the plural of the names of the males of the sons of Adam, or the jinn, or the angels. And it was said thus because prostration is one of the actions of those who collect the names of their males with ya’ and nun or waw and nun, so the plural of its names is taken out as the plural of the names of those who do that, as it was said: O ants, enter your dwellings. He said, I saw them. It has been said,
h
I saw eleven stars
. So he repeated the verb, and that is in the language of someone who said, I spoke to your brother, to confirm the verb by repetition. It has been said that the eleven planets were his brothers,
h
and the sun and the moon
were his parents.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
When Joseph said to his father
h
O my father
, indeed I have seen eleven stars,’ his brothers, eleven stars,
h
and the sun and the moon
, meaning by that: his parents.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi
m: regarding his statement: Indeed,
h
I saw eleven stars
h
and the sun and the moon
, the verse, he said: He saw his parents and brothers prostrating to him, and when it was said to him: On whose behalf? He said: If it is true, then Ibn Abbas interpreted it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
Eleven stars and the sun and the moon
. I saw them prostrating to me,” he said: The stars are his brothers,
h
and the sun and the moon
are his parents.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: his saying:
h
I saw eleven stars
, his brothers, and the sun, his mother, and the moon, his father.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan said:
m: His parents and brothers.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: Ibn Al-Faraj said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd Ibn Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say:
h
I saw eleven stars
, who were Joseph’s brothers,
h
and the sun and the moon
, who were his parents.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
O my father

, indeed I have seen eleven stars, the verse, he said: His parents and his brothers. He said: So his brothers, and they were prophets, mourned him and said: He was not satisfied for his brothers to prostrate to him until his parents prostrated to him, when he reached them. Surat Yusuf 12:4
h
When Joseph said to his father
h
O my father
, indeed I have seen
h
eleven stars and the sun and the moon
; I saw them prostrating to me."

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said:
m: The planets are his brothers,
h
and the sun and the moon
are his father and his maternal aunt, from an unfavorable perspective, so I disliked mentioning it.

x: God Almighty says: Jacob said to his son Joseph: O my son, do not relate your vision, this, to your brothers, lest they envy you, and plot against you, meaning: they will seek to harm you, and show enmity towards you, and obey Satan in your regard, Indeed, Satan is to man a clear enemy, meaning: Satan is an enemy to Adam and his sons, and he has made his enmity clear to them and manifested it. He says: So beware of Satan tempting your brothers to envy you if you relate your vision to them. Jacob said that because he had previously noticed envy from his brothers, such as: Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi narrated, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said: Jacob settled in Ash-Sham, and his concern was Joseph and his brother. His brothers envied him when they saw his father’s love for him. Joseph saw in a dream that eleven stars, the sun, and the moon were prostrating to him.

He told his father about it, and he said: O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers, lest they plot against you, the verse. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the inclusion of the letter lam in the phrase fikaydaw laka kida.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: Its meaning is: They devise a plan for you, and it is not like: If you interpret dreams, in that he wanted to connect the action to it with the lam, as it is connected with the ba, as you say: I presented food to him, meaning I presented to him, and he said: They eat what you presented to them, and similar to it is his saying: (Say: God guides to the truth). He said: If you wish, They devise a plan for you is in the meaning of: They plot against you, and you make the lam like: They fear their Lord. And he said: They fear their Lord, but it is in place of: Their Lord they fear.

Some of them said: The lam was introduced in that, just as it is introduced in their saying: I praised you and thanked you, and I praised you and thanked you. He said: This is a lam brought by the verb, so is his saying:
h
They plot against you a plot
, you say: They plot against you, or: They plot against you, so they intend you, and they intend for you. He said: And ‘plotting’ is an emphasis.
God Almighty says, informing about what Jacob said to his son Joseph, when he told him his dream: And thus your Lord chooses you, and thus your Lord chooses you.
He says: Just as your Lord showed you the planets, the sun, and the moon prostrating to you, so your Lord chooses you, just as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr Al-Anqazi told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: And thus your Lord chooses you, he said: He selects you.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And thus your Lord chooses you and teaches you the interpretation of dreams
, so He chose him and selected him and taught him the interpretation of dreams, which is the interpretation of dreams. And His statement:
h
And He teaches you the interpretation of dreams
, means: And your Lord teaches you the knowledge of what people’s dreams are interpreted to mean, about what they see in their dreams. And that is the interpretation of dreams.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And He teaches you the interpretation of dreams
, he said the expression of the vision.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And He teaches you the interpretation of dreams

, he said: The interpretation of speech, knowledge and speech. And Joseph was the most eloquent of people, and he recited: And when he reached his full strength, We gave him wisdom and knowledge. And His saying:
h
And He will complete His favor upon you

, by choosing you, selecting you, and teaching you the interpretation of hadiths, and upon the family of Jacob, meaning: and upon the people of Jacob’s religion and his faith from his descendants and others, as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham and Isaac, by taking this one as a friend and saving him from the Fire, and the ransom of this one with a great sacrifice, like the one:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told us, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He will complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob as He completed it upon your two fathers before

, Abraham and Isaac, he said: So His favor upon Abraham was that He saved him from the Fire, and upon Isaac was that He saved him from being slaughtered. And His saying: Indeed, your Lord is All-Knowing, All-Wise, means: Indeed, your Lord is All-Knowing, in better places, and who is worthy of being chosen and blessed, Wise, in His management of His creation.

x: God Almighty says: There were certainly in Joseph and his brothers, the eleven, signs, meaning: he explained and mentioned them, for those who ask, meaning: those who ask about their report and stories. And God Almighty meant by that His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is said that God Almighty revealed this Surah to His Prophet, to teach him what Joseph had suffered from his relatives and brothers of envy, while God honored him, as a consolation for him from what he suffered from his relatives and friends from the polytheists of Quraysh.
Ibn Ishaq also used to say:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: God Almighty told Muhammad the story of Joseph, and the oppression and envy of his brothers towards him, when he mentioned his dream, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw the oppression and envy of his people when God Almighty honored him with his prophethood, so that he would follow his example. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: Signs for those who ask. So I read it as most countries read: verses on intercourse.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid and Ibn Kathir
m: that they read that on monotheism. Which is the more correct of the two readings, is the reading of the one who reads it as intercourse, because the evidence from the readings agrees on it.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: Signs for those who ask.
So I read it as most countries read: verses on intercourse.
It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid and Ibn Kathir that they read that on monotheism.
Which is the more correct of the two readings, is the reading of the one who reads it as intercourse, because the evidence from the readings agrees on it.

x: God Almighty says: There were signs in Joseph and his brothers for those who asked about their situation, when Joseph’s brothers said: Joseph and his brother, from his mother, are dearer to our father than we,
h
and we are a group
, meaning: We are a group of eleven men.

A group of people is ten or more, it has been said up to fifteen, it does not have a singular form of its own, like a group and a tribe. Our father is clearly in error, meaning: Our father Jacob is clearly in error in his actions, in his preference for Joseph and his half-brother over us in love. What is meant by clear is that it is an error that is clear to anyone who contemplates and looks at it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: When they said, ‘Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we,’ he said: They meant Benjamin. He said: And they were ten. He said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Our father is in clear error, he said: in error in our matter.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And we are a group
, he said: And the group is the community.

x: ‍Abu Jaʿfar said: God Almighty says: The brothers of Joseph said to one another: Kill Joseph or throw him into a place on earth, meaning a place on earth, so that your father’s face will be free for you, meaning: Your father’s face will be free for you from his preoccupation with Joseph, for he had preoccupied him with us and turned his face away from us to him, and you will be after him a righteous people, meaning that they would repent for killing Joseph and the sin they committed in it, so that by their repentance from killing him after Joseph’s death they would be a righteous people. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Kill Joseph or cast him out to some land, so that your father’s favour will be exclusively for you, and you will be after him a righteous people. He said: You will repent for what you did, or: for what you did.

x: God Almighty says: One of Joseph's brothers said:
h
Do not kill Joseph
. It was said that the one who said that was Rubel, who was Joseph’s cousin.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Do not kill Joseph
. He told us that he was Rubil, the eldest of the people, and he was Joseph’s maternal cousin, so he forbade them from killing him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Kill Joseph, until his saying: If you are going to do something, he said: It was mentioned to me, and God knows best, that the one who said that among them was Reuben, the eldest of the sons of Jacob, and he was the most reasonable of them in his opinion about him.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do not kill Joseph
, he said: He was the eldest of his brothers, and he was Joseph’s maternal cousin, so he forbade them from killing him. It was said: The one who said that among them was Simon.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: A speaker among them said, ‘
h
Do not kill Joseph
,’ he said: He is Shimon. His saying:
h
And throw him into the bottom of the well
, means they threw him into the bottom of the well, where his report would disappear. There are different readings of this. So I read it as the people of Medina generally read:
h
The depths of the well
, in the plural. And the general public in all countries read it as: Ghayabat al-Jabb, with the singular form of ghayaba.

x: Reading it with monotheism is more beloved to me. And the well, the pit. It was said: It is the name of the well of Jerusalem.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding
h
the depths of the well
, he said: a well in Jerusalem.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The depths of the well

, he said: A well in Jerusalem. Absence, anything that hides something is absence, and the well, the uncovered well. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: in
h
the depths of the well
, in some of its corners, at its bottom.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And throw him into the bottom of the well
, he said: into some of its corners.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: And they cast him into the bottom of the well, he said: Their leader who stayed behind said it. He said: The well is a well in the Levant.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And throw him into the bottom of the well
, meaning the well.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: The well is the well. And his saying:
h
Some caravan picks it up
, he says: Some travelers who are passing by take it, If you are going to do, he says: If you are going to do what I tell you. So he mentioned that some Bedouins picked it up.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: Some of the travelers picked it up, he said: Some of the Bedouins picked it up. It was mentioned on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he read: Some of the caravan picks it up, with a ta.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me that, he said, Al-Qasim told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Matar Al-Warraq, on the authority of Al-Hasan.
m: It is as if Al-Hassan went in feminizing some of the car to the point that some of it did what it did. The Arabs do that in the report of was about an added feminine, so that the report about some of it is report about all of it, and that is like the poet’s saying: I see the passing years taking from me as secrets are taken from the crescent moon He said: They took it from me. He began the story about bitterness, since the story about bitterness was a story about the years, and as the other said: If one of their masters dies, a master rises up and the people of the villages and churches pay their respects to him. Qafal: I approached him, and the report is about the people of the villages, because the report about them is like the report about the villages. And whoever said that did not say: Hind’s slave girl approached him, because if the slave was thrown out of the speech, Hind would not indicate him, just as the report about the village indicates its people. That is because if it was said: The villages approached him, it would be known that it is report about its people. And likewise some of the caravan, if some was thrown out and it was said: The caravan will pick it up, it would be known that it is report about some or all, and the report about the caravan indicates it.

evidence.text: So I read it as the people of Medina generally read: The depths of the well, in the plural.
And the general public in all countries read it as: Ghayabat al-Jabb, with the singular form of ghayaba.

x: God Almighty says: Joseph’s brothers, when they conspired among themselves and agreed to separate him from his father Jacob, said to their father Jacob: O our father, why do you not trust us with Joseph? So you leave him with us when we go out of the city into the desert, and indeed we are his sincere advisers, surrounding him and protecting him.

The readings differed in the reading of that. The general reading of the people of Medina is: yart’i and yal’ab, with a kasra on the ‘ayn of yart’i and with a ya’ in yart’i and yal’ab, meaning: yafta’ala, from ra’i: irta’iytu so I irta’i, as if they directed the meaning of the speech to: send him with us tomorrow so that the camels may graze and play, and indeed, We will be his guardians. The majority of the people of Kufa read it as:
h
Send him with us tomorrow to frolic and play

, with a ya’ in both letters, and a sukoon on the ‘ayn, from their saying: So-and-so frolicked in his money, if he enjoyed it and was happy with it, and spent it on his desires. And from that is their saying in a proverb: The chain and the frolic, and from that is the saying of al-Qatami: I am ungrateful after death has been turned away from me and after you have given me a hundred blessings.
Some people of Basra read: yatra’a with a nun and na’lab with a nun in both of them, and the ayn is silent from natra’a.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said, Al-Qasim told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, he said:
m: Abu Amr used to recite: We play and we graze with a nun. He said: So I said to Abu Amr: How do they say we play when they are prophets? He said: They were not prophets at that time.

x: In my opinion, the most correct reading is that of the one who reads it with both letters with the ya’ and with the jasm of the ʿayn in yirtaʿ, because the people only asked their father to send Yusuf with them, and they deceived him by telling him about their asking him that, because of Yusuf’s joy, happiness, and activity in sending him with them, by going out to the desert and its spaciousness and playing there, not by telling him about themselves. This is also how the interpretation of the people of interpretation came.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Send him with us tomorrow to graze and play
, meaning: to run and be active.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: He frolics and plays, he said: He plays, is active, and strives.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Send him with us tomorrow to frolic and play
, he said: to be active and have fun.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
He grazes and plays
, he said: He strives and plays.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hisham told me, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He grazes and plays
, he said: He is amused and playing. He said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
h
Send him with us tomorrow to frolic and play
, to have fun. He said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Qatada:
h
Send him with us tomorrow to graze and play
. He said: to be active and play.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Naim bin Damdam Al-Amiri told us, he said:
m: I heard Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim regarding his statement:
h
Send him with us tomorrow to graze and play
, he said: He runs and is active. It is as if those who read it: He frolics and plays, with the letter ‘ayn broken from he frolics, interpret it in the way that:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Send him with us tomorrow to graze and play
, he said: To graze his sheep, and to look and reason, so that the man is known. Mujahid used to say about this, including:

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: We graze, some of us protect others, we rely on one another, we guard ourselves.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: We graze, he said: We protect each other, we rely on each other.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid - and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Warqaʿ, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: something similar.

x: The interpretation of the statement is: Send him with us tomorrow so that we may play, have fun, enjoy ourselves and be active in the desert, and we will protect him from anything that he dislikes or harms him.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The readings differed in the reading of that.

The general reading of the people of Medina is: yart’i and yal’ab, with a kasra on the ‘ayn of yart’i and with a ya’ in yart’i and yal’ab, meaning: yafta’ala, from ra’i: irta’iytu so I irta’i, as if they directed the meaning of the speech to: send him with us tomorrow so that the camels may graze and play, and indeed, We will be his guardians.

The majority of the people of Kufa read it as: Send him with us tomorrow to frolic and play, with a ya’ in both letters, and a sukoon on the ‘ayn, from their saying: So-and-so frolicked in his money, if he enjoyed it and was happy with it, and spent it on his desires.

Abu Jaʿfar said: In my opinion, the most correct reading is that of the one who reads it with both letters with the ya’ and with the jasm of the ʿayn in yirtaʿ, because the people only asked their father to send Yusuf with them, and they deceived him by telling him about their asking him that, because of Yusuf’s joy, happiness, and activity in sending him with them, by going out to the desert and its spaciousness and playing there, not by telling him about themselves.
It is as if those who read it: He frolics and plays, with the letter ‘ayn broken from he frolics, interpret it in the way that:

x: God Almighty says: Jacob said to them: It saddens me that you should take him with you to the desert, fearing that a wolf might eat him, while you are unaware of him and do not realize it.

God Almighty says: Joseph’s brothers said to their father Jacob: If Joseph is eaten by a wolf in the desert, and we are eleven men with him protecting him - and they are the group - then we will surely be losers, meaning: then we will surely be helpless and doomed.

In the speech there is something that was omitted and its mention was omitted, being satisfied with what appeared from what was omitted, which is: So he sent him with them, So when they went with him and agreed, he says: And their opinion was agreed upon, and they resolved to put him in the bottom of the well, as: Ibn Wakee' narrated that Amr ibn Muhammad narrated from Asbat from As-Suddi, regarding his statement: Indeed, it grieves me that you should take him away, the verse, he said, he said: I will not send him with you, I fear that a wolf will eat him while you are unaware of him, "They said: If the wolf should eat him while we are a company, then we will surely be losers," so he sent him with them, and they took him out and he was an honor to them, and when they took him out into the wilderness, they showed him enmity, and his brother began to beat him, and he would call for help from the other, and he would beat him, but he did not see any mercy from them, so they beat him until they were about to kill him, so he began to cry out and say: O my father, O Jacob, if you only knew what the sons of the slave girls did to your son, and when they were about to kill him, Judah said: Did you not give me a pledge not to kill him? So they took him to the well to throw him, and they began to lower him into the well, and he would cling to the edge of the well.

So they tied his hands and took off his shirt. He said: Brothers, give me back my shirt so that I may hide in it in the well. They said: Call the sun, the moon, and the eleven stars to keep you company. He said: I did not see anything. So they lowered him into the well. When he reached halfway there, they threw him in, wanting him to die. There was water in the well, so he fell into it. Then he took refuge in a rock and stood on it. He said: When they threw him in the well, he began to cry. They called out to him, and he thought that it was mercy that had overtaken them, so he obeyed them. They wanted to throw him against a rock and kill him, but Judah stood up and stopped them, saying: You have given me a pledge not to kill him. Judah used to bring him food. And his saying:
h
So when they went with him and gathered

, the waw was inserted in the answer, as Imru’ al-Qais said: When we crossed the courtyard of the neighborhood and we turned towards the valley of Khabt Dhi Qafaf Aqanqal So he inserted the waw in the answer to lama, but the speech is: When we crossed the courtyard of the neighborhood, he took us aside.
And likewise: When they went with him and gathered, because his saying: gathered is the answer. And His statement:
h
And We inspired him

, ‘You shall surely inform them of their affair,’ meaning: And We inspired Joseph, ‘You shall surely inform your brothers of this affair of theirs,’ meaning: of this action that they did to you, ‘while they perceive not,’ meaning: while they do not know and do not perceive. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning that God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
And they do not perceive

Some of them said: What he meant by that is that God revealed to Joseph that Joseph would inform his brothers of what they did to him: throwing him into the well, selling him, and all the other things they did to him, and his brothers were not aware of God’s revelation to him about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And We inspired him
, to Joseph.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And We inspired him

: You must inform them of this affair of theirs,” he said: We inspired Joseph: You must inform your brothers. He said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: “
h
And We inspired him

: ‘You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs while they do not perceive.’” He said: It was inspired to Joseph while he was in the well that he would inform them of what they had done, and they did not perceive that inspiration.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he said, Mujahid said:
m: h
And We inspired him
, he said: to Joseph.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: We revealed to Joseph what his brothers would do to him, and his brothers were not aware of God informing him of that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We inspired him
, ‘You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs while they do not perceive,’ with what God informed Joseph of their affair while he was in the well.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And We inspired him

: ‘You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs while they do not perceive.’” He said: God inspired Joseph while he was in the well to inform them of what they had done to him, and they did not perceive that revelation.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: something similar, except that he said: that He will inform them.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that Joseph will inform them of what they did to him, and they will not realize that he is Joseph.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they do not perceive
, he said:
h
And they do not perceive
that it is Joseph.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sadaqah bin Ubadah Al-Asadi told us, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas say: When Joseph’s brothers entered and he recognized them while they did not recognize him, he said: The measure was brought, and he placed it on his hand, then he tapped it and understood, and he said: This cup tells me that you had a brother from your father called Joseph, who brought him close to you, and that you took him and threw him into the bottom of the well. He said: Then he tapped it and understood, and you came to your father and said: The wolf ate him, and you came with false blood on his shirt. He said: So some of them said to one another: This cup tells him your story. Ibn Abbas said: So we do not think that this verse was revealed except about them: You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs while they do not perceive.

x: God Almighty said: And they came to their father at nightfall, weeping.

God Almighty says: And Joseph's brothers came to their father, after they had thrown Joseph into the bottom of the well, at nightfall, weeping. It was said: The meaning of his saying we race is we compete from the race, as: Ibn Wakee’ narrated, ‘Amr ibn Muhammad narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: They came to their father at night, crying. When he heard their voices, he was alarmed and said: What is the matter with you, my sons? Has anything happened to your sheep? They said: No! He said: What happened to Joseph? They said: O our father, we went racing and left Joseph with our belongings, and a wolf ate him! The old man cried and shouted at the top of his voice, and said: Where is the shirt? So they brought him the shirt with false blood on it. He took the shirt and threw it on his face, then he cried until his face was stained with the blood from the shirt.
And his saying:
h
And you will not believe us
, they say:
h
And you will not believe us
when we say that Joseph was eaten by a wolf, even if we were truthful! Like: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
h
And you will not believe us
, he said: You will not believe us! [If someone says: How did he say:
h
And if we were truthful
, and his saying:
h
And if we were truthful

, is either a report from them that they were not truthful, in which case that is a denial from them of themselves, or a report from them about their father that he would not believe them if they believed him, for you know that if they believed their father, he would believe them? It was said: This does not mean either of them, but rather it means: You would not believe us even if we were among the people of truth who are not accused, because of your bad opinion of us and your accusation of us.
God Almighty says:
h
And they brought his shirt with false blood

, and God called it a lie because those who brought the shirt with him on it lied and said to Jacob: It is Joseph’s blood, but it was not his blood, but rather it was the blood of a young goat, according to what was said.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Abdul Samad Al-Ansari told me, he said, Abu Osama told us, on the authority of Shibl, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they brought his shirt with false blood
, he said: The blood of a young goat.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they brought false blood on his shirt
, he said: The blood of a young goat, a sheep.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: with false blood, he said: the blood of a young goat, meaning a sheep.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: with false blood, he said: the blood of a young goat, a sheep.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: with false blood, he said: That blood was false, it was not the blood of Joseph.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: With false blood, he said: The blood of a young goat, a sheep.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: with false blood, he said: with the blood of a young goat.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: They slaughtered a young goat from the sheep, then they smeared the shirt with its blood, then they came to their father, and Jacob said: If this wolf is merciful! How did it eat his flesh and not tear his shirt? O my son, O Joseph, what did the sons of the female slaves do to you!

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And they came upon his shirt with false blood, he said: If a wild beast had eaten it, it would have torn the shirt.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abu Khalid told us, he said, Sufyan told us,
m: on his authority on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same, except that he said: If a wolf had eaten him, it would have torn his shirt.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And they brought his shirt with false blood
, he said: If the wolf had eaten it, it would have torn it.

c: Ubayd God ibn Abi Ziyad told me, he said, Uthman ibn Amr told us, he said, Qurra told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: Joseph’s shirt was brought to Jacob, and he began to look at it and saw traces of blood, but he did not see any tear in it. He said: O my son, I did not know the wolf to be patient.

c: Ahmad bin Abdul Samad Al-Ansari told us, he said, Abu Amer Al-Aqdi told us, on the authority of Qura, he said:
m: I heard Al-Hasan say: When they brought Joseph’s shirt, and Jacob did not see a tear, he said: O my son, by God, I have never known a wolf to be so forbearing!

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Hammad bin Mas’adah told us, on the authority of Imran bin Muslim, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: When the brothers came Joseph took his shirt to their father. He said: He kept turning it over and saying: I have never known a wolf to be so forbearing. He ate my son and left his shirt!

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they brought his shirt with false blood
, he said: When they brought his shirt to the Prophet of God, Jacob, he said: I do not see the trace of a wild animal, nor a stab wound, nor a tear.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: With false blood, false blood, it was not the blood of Joseph.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham told us, Mujalid told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: They slaughtered a kid and smeared it with its blood. When Ya’qub saw that the shirt was intact, he knew that the people had lied to him, so he said to them: If this wolf was so forbearing, how could he have taken pity on the shirt but not on my son! So he knew that they had lied to him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And they brought his shirt with false blood
, he said: When Jacob was brought Joseph’s shirt and he did not see a tear in it, he said: You have lied, if a wild beast had eaten it, it would have torn his shirt!

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ishaq Al-Azraq and Ya’la told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Amer, he said:
m: There were three signs on Joseph’s shirt: When they came upon his shirt with false blood. He said: And Jacob said: If a wolf had eaten him, it would have torn his shirt.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad told us, Zakariya told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Amer, who said:
m: He used to say: In Joseph’s shirt are three signs: when it was thrown over his father’s face and he regained his sight, when it was torn from behind, and when they came upon his shirt with false blood.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Amer, he said:
m: There were three signs on Joseph’s shirt: the tear, the blood, and he threw it on his father’s face and he regained his sight.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Abu Amer told us, Qara told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: When Joseph’s shirt was brought to Jacob, and he saw the blood but did not see the tear, he said: I have never known a wolf to be so forbearing! He said, Hammad bin Masada told us, he said, Qara told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, something similar.

x: How was it said: With false blood, when you know that it was blood without a doubt, and if it was not, it was Joseph’s blood?

There are two aspects to this statement: One of them: that it was said with false blood, because there was a lie in it, just as it is said: The night is the crescent, and just as it is said: So their trade did not profit them. This is a statement that some of the grammarians of Basra used to say.

The other aspect: It is said: It is a source with the meaning of a passive participle. Its interpretation is: And they came upon his shirt with false blood, just as it is said: He has no mind, nor is he rational, nor does he have skin, nor is he flogged. The Arabs do that a lot, they put a passive participle in the place of the source, and the source in the place of a passive participle, as Al-Ra’i said: Even if they left no flesh for his bones, nor any sense for his heart. This was said by some grammarians of Kufa.
And His statement: “He said: ‘Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something,’” God Almighty says:

c: Jacob said to his sons who told him that
m: the wolf had eaten Joseph, denying their story: The matter is not as you say. Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something, meaning: Rather, your souls have made something attractive to you in Joseph and made it good, so you did it, as:
b.via: Jacob said to his sons who

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something, he said, he says: Rather, your souls have made something attractive to you. And his saying:
h
So have beautiful patience
, meaning: So my patience with what you did to me in the matter of Joseph is beautiful patience, or it is beautiful patience. And his saying:
h
And God is the One sought for help against what you describe
, means:
h
And God is the One sought for help against what you describe
of lies. It was said: Beautiful patience is the patience in which there is no impatience.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So be patient and beautiful, he said: There is no impatience in it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So be patient and beautiful, without impatience. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said, Amr bin Awn told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Yahya, on the authority of Habban bin Abi Jabalah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about his statement: ‘So be patient, which is most fitting.’ He said: Patience in which there is no complaint. He said: Whoever persists and is not patient.” Surat Yusuf 12:18
h
And they brought his shirt with false blood
. He said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something, so patience is most fitting.
h
And God is the one sought for help against that which you describe

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Yahya told us, on the authority of Hubban bin Abi Jabalah:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about his statement: ‘So be patient and have good patience.’ He said: ‘Patience in which there is no complaint.’” He said, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: So be patient and beautiful, there is no impatience in it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: So be patient and most gracious, he said: without impatience.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of some of his companions, he said:
m: It is said: Three things are from patience: that you do not speak about your pain, nor your misfortune, nor praise yourself. He said: Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit: that the eyebrows of the Prophet Jacob, may God bless him and grant him peace, had fallen out, so he used to raise them with a rag. It was said to him: What is this? He said: The length of time and the abundance of sorrows! So God Almighty revealed to him: O Jacob, do you complain about Me? He said: O Lord, I committed a sin, so forgive me. And His saying:
h
And God is the one sought for help against that which you describe

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And God is the one sought for help against what you describe, meaning: against what you lie about.

evidence.text: Ubayd God ibn Abi Ziyad told me, he said, Uthman ibn Amr told us, he said, Qurra told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Joseph’s shirt was brought to Jacob, and he began to look at it and saw traces of blood, but he did not see any tear in it.

x: God Almighty says: And the travelers passed by on the road, and they sent their water-drawer, which is the one who goes to the watering place or the house, and his coming to it means his destination and his entry into it, and he lowered his bucket, meaning: he lowered his bucket into the well. It is said: I lowered the bucket into the well, meaning I sent it into it. If you draw water from it, you say: I lowered the bucket into the well. There is an omission in the speech, and the indication of what was mentioned was sufficient for it, so it was left out, and that is: So he lowered his bucket, and Joseph clung to it, so it came out, and the one who lowered it said: Good report, this is a boy. And what we said about that came the report from the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And a caravan came,
h
so they sent their water-drawer

, and he lowered his bucket. So Joseph held on to the rope, and he went out. When the owner of the rope saw him, he called out to one of his companions, whose name was Bushra, O Bushra, this is a boy.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So they sent their water-drawer
, and he lowered his bucket, and the boy clung to the bucket, and when he came out he said: Good report, this is a boy.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So they sent their water-drawer
, it is said: They sent their messenger, and when he lowered his bucket, the boy clung to it, He said, ‘
h
O good report
, this is a boy.’ They differed about the meaning of his saying: Good report, this is a boy.

x: Some of them said: This is good report from the one who guided his companions, in his hit on Joseph, that he hit a slave.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He said, ‘
h
O good report
, this is a boy.’ They were happy about him when they brought him out, and it is a desert in the land of Jerusalem, and its location is known.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
O good report
! This is a boy. He said: He gave them good report when he found Joseph.

x: Others said: Rather, it is the name of a specific man from the car, whom the guide called out to when Joseph came out of the well, clinging to the rope.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: O Bushra, this is a boy. He said: He called out to a man from among his companions called Bushra, and said, O Bushra, this is a boy.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Khalaf bin Hisham told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Qais bin Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O good report
, this is a boy, he said: His companion’s name was Bushra.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, he said, Al-Hakam ibn Dhahir told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O good report
, this is a boy, he said: The boy’s name is Bushra. He said:
h
O good report

, as you say: O Zaid. There are different readings of this: The majority of the readers of Medina read it as: Ya Bushra, with the addition of the ya’, except that he assimilated the alif into the ya’ in order to obtain the kasra that is required before the addition of the ya’ from the speaker, in his saying: my slave and my neighbor, in every case. This is from the language of Tayyi’, as Abu Dhu’ayb said: They preceded my passion and embraced their passion, so they were destroyed, and every side has its fate. The majority of the Kufians read it as: Ya Bushra, by sending the ya and leaving the addition. If this is read in this way, it has two interpretations: One of them is what Al-Suddi said, which is that it is the name of a man whom the seeker of water called by his name, as one says: O Zaid and O Amr, so it is good report, in the place of raising the call. The other: that he wanted to add the good report to himself, so he deleted the ya’ while he wanted it, so it is singular and there is an intention of addition in it, as the Arabs do in calling, so they say: O soul, be patient, and O my soul, be patient, and O my son, do not do it, and O my son, do not do it, so it is singular and raised, and there is an intention of addition in it. And sometimes it is added and broken, as you say: O young boy, come, and my young boy, come.

x: The reading that I like the most is the reading of the one who reads it with the ya’ open and the sukoon on it, because if it is the name of a specific man who was known among them, as al-Suddi said, then that is the correct reading without a doubt. And if it is from al-Tabsheer, then it is possible if it is read in this way, as I have explained. As for the emphasis and addition of the letter ya, it is an irregular reading. I do not see it as a reading, even though it is a well-known language, because the evidence from the readings is unanimously against it. As for his saying:
h
And they took him as merchandise
, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.

Some of them said: Al-Warid Al-Mustaqqi and his companions, the merchants who were with him, captured him and said to him: It is merchandise that some of the people of Egypt have bought, because they were afraid that if they knew that they had bought it for what they had bought it for, they would ask them for a share in it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And they took him as merchandise

, he said: The owner of the bucket and those with him said to their companions: We only took him as merchandise, fearing that they would share it with them if they knew its price. His brothers followed them, saying to the bucket-bearer and his companions: Be sure of him, lest he run away! Until they stopped him in Egypt and he said: Who will buy me and give me good report? So the king bought him, and the king was a Muslim.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar, except that he said: For fear that they would consult them if they knew about him, and his brothers followed them, saying to Al-Madli and his companions: Make sure he does not run away! Until they stopped him in Egypt, and the rest of the hadith is like the hadith of Muhammad bin Amr.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid...
m: he said, and Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar, except that he said: For fear that they would share in it with them, if they knew its price.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: in a similar manner, except that he said: For fear that they would consult them about it, if they knew its price. He also said: Until they stopped it in Egypt.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And they concealed it as merchandise

, he said: When the two men bought it, they were afraid that the company would say: We bought it, and they would ask them for a partnership, so they said: If they ask us: What is this? We will say: Merchandise that the people of the water have purchased. So that is what His saying:
h
And they concealed it as merchandise
, is between them.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: The merchants took him from one another.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, he said, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And they concealed it as merchandise
, he said: The merchants concealed it from one another.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim Al-Fadl told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And they concealed it as merchandise
, he said: The merchants concealed it from one another.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: They kept his sale secret.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasban bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they concealed his merchandise, he said: They concealed his sale.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And they concealed it as merchandise
, he said: They said to the people of the water: It is only merchandise.

x: Others said: What he meant by his saying:
h
And they took him as a commodity was Joseph’s brothers
, that they took Joseph as a commodity and that he was their brother. They said: He is our slave.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they concealed him as merchandise
, meaning: Joseph’s Surat Yusuf 12:19 And a caravan came,
h
so they sent their water-drawer
, and he let down his bucket. He said, "Good news! This is a boy!"
h
And they concealed him as merchandise

. And God is Knowing of what they do. brothers concealed his affair and concealed that he was their brother. Joseph concealed his affair for fear that his brothers would kill him, and he chose to sell him. His brothers mentioned him to the people’s visitor, so he called out to his companions and said: Good report! This is a boy for sale! So his brothers sold him.

x: The most correct of these statements is the statement of the one who said: And the one who brought water to the people who lowered his bucket and those with him from his traveling companions, was taken prisoner. Joseph ordered that they buy him, fearing that they would consult them, and they said to them: He is merchandise that the people of the water sell with us. This is because it follows the report about him, so what follows it from the report is report about him, which is more likely than it being report about someone who is not connected to the report about him. And His saying: And God is All-Knowing of what they do, God Almighty says: And God is All-Knowing of what Joseph’s sellers and buyers do in his affair. Nothing of that is hidden from Him, but He left that to change in order to carry out His previous judgment in His knowledge regarding it and in them, and so that Joseph’s brothers, Joseph, and his father may see His power in it.

This, even though it was report from God the Most High, mentioned about His Prophet Joseph, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a reminder from God to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a consolation from Him for what he was suffering from his polytheist relatives and kinsmen. He says: So be patient, O Muhammad, for what has befallen you for the sake of God, for I am able to change what these polytheists are befalling you, just as I was able to change what Joseph suffered from his brothers when they were doing to him what they did. My leaving that was not because of Joseph’s indignity to Me, but because of My previous knowledge of him and his brothers. Likewise, My leaving that which these polytheists are befalling you was not because of your indignity to Me, but because of My previous knowledge of you and them. Then your affair and their affair will turn to your superiority over them, and their submission to you, just as the affair of Joseph’s brothers turned to their submission to Joseph in their leadership over them, and Joseph’s superiority over them.

evidence.text: There are different readings of this: The majority of the readers of Medina read it as: Ya Bushra, with the addition of the ya’, except that he assimilated the alif into the ya’ in order to obtain the kasra that is required before the addition of the ya’ from the speaker, in his saying: my slave and my neighbor, in every case.
The majority of the Kufians read it as: Ya Bushra, by sending the ya and leaving the addition.

If this is read in this way, it has two interpretations: One of them is what Al-Suddi said, which is that it is the name of a man whom the seeker of water called by his name, as one says: O Zaid and O Amr, so it is good report, in the place of raising the call.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The reading that I like the most is the reading of the one who reads it with the ya’ open and the sukoon on it, because if it is the name of a specific man who was known among them, as al-Suddi said, then that is the correct reading without a doubt.
And if it is from al-Tabsheer, then it is possible if it is read in this way, as I have explained.
I do not see it as a reading, even though it is a well-known language, because the evidence from the readings is unanimously against it.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
And they sold him

, that Joseph’s brothers sold Joseph. But if he wanted to say that he bought it, he said: I bought it. From this is the saying of Ibn Mufrij Al-Himyari: I bought a cold, I wish I had been cold before He said: I sold Burd, who was a slave of his. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibrahim told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Abu Maʿshar, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: that he disliked buying and selling to the Bedouin. He said: The Arabs say: Sell me such and such, meaning: Sell me such and such, and he recited this verse:
h
And they sold him for a cheap price
, for a few dirhams, meaning: they sold him, and his sale was forbidden.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The brothers of Yusuf were eleven men,
h
and they sold him
when the one who lowered his bucket brought him out.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.
Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid.

c: And Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told me, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. He said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, And they sold it, he said: Ibn Abbas said: So it was sold among them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they sold him for a cheap price
, he said: They sold him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: So his brothers sold him
h
for a cheap price

x: Others said: Rather, what he meant by his saying:
h
And they sold him for a cheap price is the car
, that they sold Joseph
h
for a cheap price
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told me, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And they sold him for a cheap price
, and they were the caravansers who sold him.

x: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said: The interpretation of that is: And Joseph’s brothers bought Joseph
h
for a cheap price

. That is because God Almighty has informed about those who bought him that they concealed the purchase of Joseph from their companions, fearing that they would consult them, by claiming that he was merchandise. They did not say that except out of a desire that he would be purely for them and not them, and to conceal the price for which they bought him, because they bought him as God Almighty said:
h
for a cheap price

. If those who bought him from his brothers were among those who were ascetics, then their saying to their companions: He is merchandise would have no meaning, nor would their buying him while they were among those who were ascetics have any reason, unless they were overcome by their minds, because it is impossible for a person of sound mind to buy something that he is ascetic in without being forced to do so, and then lie about it to the people by saying: He is merchandise, I did not buy him, despite his asceticism in it.

Rather, this statement is made by someone who is stingy with his goods because they are precious to him, and because he hopes for a high price for them and a great profit. As for his saying: Bakhs, it means: deficiency. It is a source from the saying of the speaker: I defrauded someone of his right, if I wronged him, meaning: I wronged him and reduced what was due to him in fulfillment: I defrauded him, and from this is his saying: And do not defraud people of their things, but what was meant was: with a defrauded and diminished price, so he put defrauding, which is a source, in place of the object, just as it was said: with false blood, but it is: with blood that was lied about.
The interpreters differed about the meaning of this: Some of them said: It was said:
h
For a cheap price
, because it was forbidden to them.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
And they sold him for a cheap price
. He said: The cheap price is the forbidden.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Ali bin Asim told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: h
And they sold him for a cheap price
, he said: It is forbidden.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Its price was cheap, forbidden, and it was not permissible for them to eat it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they sold him for a cheap price
, he said: They sold him
h
for a cheap price
. He said: Selling it was forbidden, and buying it was forbidden.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: h
For a cheap price
, he said: It is forbidden.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
For a cheap price
, he said: It was not permissible for them to eat its price.

x: Others said: The meaning of bakhs here is injustice.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they sold him for a cheap price
, he said: Cheapness is injustice. And the sale of Joseph and his price were forbidden to them.

c: Muhammad bin Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said, Qatada said:
m: h
And they sold him for a cheap price
, he said: injustice.

x: Others said: What is meant by cheapness in this context is little.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: Bakhs means little.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the same.

x: We have explained the correct statement on this matter. As for his saying: counted dirhams, God Almighty means that they sold him for unmeasured dirhams, incomplete and not sufficient, because they were ascetic in him. It was said: It was said: counted to indicate that it was less than forty, because at that time they did not weigh anything that weighed less than forty dirhams, because the smallest and smallest of their weights was the ounce, and the weight of the ounce was forty dirhams. They said: What he said: counted indicates is the smallness of the dirhams for which they sold it.
Some of them said: It was twenty dirhams.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hamid bin Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Zuhair, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: What Joseph bought with was twenty dirhams.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: h
And they sold him for a cheap price
, for a few dirhams, he said: Twenty dirhams.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Nawf al-Bakali,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they sold him for a cheap price
, for a few dirhams, he said: Twenty dirhams.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Nawf al-Shami,
m: He cheated dirhams, he said: It was twenty dirhams.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Nawf,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said
m: regarding his statement:
h
For a cheap price
, a few dirhams, he said: Twenty dirhams.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Counted dirhams, he said: It was twenty dirhams.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: It was mentioned to us that it was sold for twenty dirhams, and they were among those who were ascetics about it.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abu Idris, on the authority of Atiyah, he said:
m: The dirhams were twenty dirhams, and they divided them two dirhams each.

x: Others said: Rather, its number was twenty-two Surat Yusuf 12:20
h
And they sold him for a cheap price
, for a few dirhams, and they were among those who were indifferent to him. dirhams, and each of Joseph’s brothers, who were eleven men, took two dirhams each.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Asbat told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Counted dirhams, he said: Twenty-two dirhams.
