c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding God’s statement: counted dirhams, he said: Twenty-two dirhams for Joseph’s brothers, and his brothers were eleven men.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: counted dirhams. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

x: Others said: Rather, it was forty dirhams.
Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: Counted dirhams, he said: Forty dirhams.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: They sold him, but the price they sold him for did not reach an ounce. This is because people at that time used to trade in ounces, so whatever was less than an ounce was a number. God says:
h
And they sold him for a cheap price
, for a few dirhams, meaning it did not reach an ounce.

x: The correct statement in this regard is that God, the Most High, mentioned that they sold him for their house, counted but not weighed, and He did not specify the amount of that by weight or number, nor did He set any evidence for it in a book or report from the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. It may be possible that it was twenty - and it may be possible that it was twenty-two - or that it was forty, or less than that or more. Whichever of these it was, they were counted but not weighed, and there is no benefit in knowing the amount of that weight that falls into a religion, nor does ignorance of it cause harm in it. Belief in the apparent meaning of the revelation is obligatory. And everything other than that is removed from our effort to know. And His statement:
h
And they were among those who were ascetic in him
, God Almighty says: And Joseph’s brothers were among those who were ascetic in Joseph.

They did not know his honor with God, nor did they know his status with Him. Despite that, they loved to come between him and his father, so that his face would be clear to them, and they would cut him off from being close to him, so that the benefits that were spent on Joseph without them would be spent on them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abu Marzuq, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: And they were among those who were ascetics about him, he said: They did not know about his prophethood and his status with God.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak, regarding His statement: And a caravan came, and it descended into the well, so they sent their water-drawer, so he drew water from the well. Then he brought out Joseph, and they were happy that they had found a boy, and they did not know his knowledge or his status with his Lord, so they were not interested in him and sold him. And his sale was forbidden,
h
and they sold him
for a few dirhams.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: h
And they were among those who were ascetic in him
, he said: His brothers were ascetic, so they did not know his status with God, his prophethood, and his position.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: His brothers were indifferent to him, they did not know his status with God.

evidence.text: He said: The Arabs say: Sell me such and such, meaning: Sell me such and such, and he recited this verse: And they sold him for a cheap price, for a few dirhams, meaning: they sold him, and his sale was forbidden.

x: God Almighty says: And the one who bought Joseph from his seller in Egypt said. He said that his name is: Qatfeer.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The name of the one he bought was Qatfir. It was said that his name was Itfir bin Ruhaib, who was Al-Aziz, and he was in charge of the treasuries of Egypt, and the king at that time was Al-Rayyan bin Al-Walid, a man from the Amalekites, likewise:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq.
m: It was said: The one who sold it in Egypt was Malik bin Dhir bin Buwaib bin Afqan bin Madyan bin Ibrahim, likewise:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas.
m: h
And the one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife
, whose name, according to Ibn Ishaq, was Rachel, daughter of Rael.

c: Ibn Hamid told us that, he said, Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq.
m: h
Honor his abode

, meaning: Honor the place where he resides, which is where he will dwell and reside. It is said: So-and-so resided in such-and-such a place, if he stayed there. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
Honor his abode
, his status, and she is the wife of Al-Aziz.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife
, ‘Make his stay comfortable.’ He said: His place.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The king bought him, and the king was Muslim. And his saying,
h
Perhaps he will be of benefit to us

, or we may adopt him as a son, he mentioned that the buyer of Joseph said this to his wife, when he gave him to her, because he had no son, and he had not had intercourse with women, so he said to her: Honor him, perhaps he will relieve us of some of what we are suffering from in our affairs if he understands and knows the matters that he is charged with, or we may adopt him as a son, meaning: or we may adopt him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Itfir, as I was told, was a man who did not have intercourse with women, and his wife Ra’il was a beautiful, soft, well-fed woman, in a kingdom and in the world.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: The three most discerning people are: Al-Aziz when he discerned Joseph and said to his wife: Make his stay honorable, perhaps he will benefit us or we will adopt him as a son, and Abu Bakr when he discerned Umar, and the woman who said: O my father, hire him, for the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Joseph went to Egypt, and Al-Aziz, the king of Egypt, bought him. He went with him to his house and said to his wife: Treat him well,
h
perhaps he will be of benefit to us
or we will adopt him as a son.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: The most perceptive of people are three: Al-Aziz when he said to his wife: Treat him with honor, and the people were indifferent to him; Abu Bakr when he had insight into Umar and appointed him as his successor; and the woman who said: O my father, hire him. And His saying:
h
And thus We established Joseph in the land

, the Almighty says: And just as We saved Joseph from the hands of his brothers when they intended to kill him, and brought him out of the well after he had been thrown into it, and granted him honor and a high position with the Mighty One of Egypt, thus We established him in the land, and made him over its storehouses. And His saying:
h
And that We might teach him the interpretation of dreams
, the Most High says: And in order for us to teach Joseph the interpretation of the vision, We established him in the land, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: From the interpretation of hadiths, he said: The expression of the vision.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And to teach him from the interpretation of hadiths, he said: the interpretation of dreams.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Shibl, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And to teach him the interpretation of dreams, he said: The expression of dreams. And His saying:
h
And God is predominant over His affair
, God Almighty says: And God is in control of Joseph’s affair, He governs it, manages it, and protects it. The letter ha in his saying: on his command refers to Joseph.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair
m: regarding the meaning of Ghalib: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
h
And God is predominant over His affair
, he said: Effective. And his saying:
h
But most of the people do not know

, he says: But most of the people who were indifferent to Joseph, and sold him for a cheap price, and those among whom he was from the people of Egypt when he was sold among them, do not know what God will do with Joseph, and to Him Joseph will return his affair.

x: God Almighty says: And when Joseph reached his prime, meaning: And when he reached the peak of his strength and power in his youth alone, and that was between eighteen years and sixty years, and it was said: up to forty years. It is said: The man's strength has passed, meaning his intensity, and it is a plural, like the harmful and the evil, and it has not been heard with a singular form of it.

i: And it is necessary by analogy that its singular be shadd, just as the singular of the harmful is dar, and the singular of the evil is shar, as the poet said:
x: Is it not that the evil has increased and the war of the kings has destroyed much wealth?
Hamid said: And if the critics would blame you after the most severe, there are four complete ones.
The people of interpretation differed about what God meant in this place by the amount of the most severe.
Some of them said: He meant thirty-three years.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, they said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And when he reached his prime, he said: thirty-three years.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Al-Haitham, on the authority of Bishr bin Al-Mufaddal, on the authority of Abdullah bin Othman bin Khathim, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas say regarding his statement:
h
And when he reached his full strength
, he said: Thirty-some years.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant twenty years.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when he reached his full strength
, he said: twenty years.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, through an unsatisfactory source, that he said:
m: Between eighteen and thirty years. I have explained the meaning of the most severe.

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God informed that He gave Joseph when he reached his prime in wisdom and knowledge, and the prime is the end of his strength and youth. It is possible that He gave him that when he was eighteen years old, and it is possible that He gave him that when he was twenty years old, and it is possible that He gave him that when he was thirty-three years old. There is no evidence for that in the Book of God, nor in any trace from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor in the consensus of the nation, on which of them it was. And if that does not exist from the aspect that you mentioned, then it is correct to say about it as God the Almighty said, until proof is established for the correctness of what was said about that from the aspect that must be accepted, so it is accepted at that time.
And the saying: We gave him wisdom and knowledge, means that God Almighty says: We gave him then understanding and knowledge, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Wisdom and knowledge, he said: Reason and knowledge before prophethood. And His statement:
h
And thus do We reward the doers of good

, the Most High says: And just as I rewarded Joseph, giving him wisdom and knowledge for his obedience to Me, and empowered him in the land, and rescued him from the hands of his brothers who wanted to kill him, thus do We reward those who do good in their work, obey Me in My command, and refrain from the sins I forbade them from. Although this is apparently directed at every doer of good, what is meant by it is Muhammad, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God Almighty says to him: Just as I did this to Joseph after he suffered from his brothers what he suffered, and endured the affliction that he endured, and I established him in the land, and made the lands easy for him, so I will do this to you, and I will save you from the polytheists of your people who intend to be hostile to you, and I will establish you in the land, and I will give you wisdom and knowledge, because that is My reward for the people of goodness in My commands and prohibitions.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And thus do We reward the doers of good
, meaning: the guided ones.

x: God Almighty says: And the wife of Al-ʿAziz, who was the one in whose house Joseph was, sought to seduce him to have intercourse with her, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: When he reached maturity, the woman in whose house he was, the wife of Al-Aziz, tried to seduce him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And the woman in whose house he was sought to seduce him, he said: She loved him. He said, and my father told me, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: She said: His sandals. And his saying:
h
And the doors were closed
, means: And the woman closed the doors of the houses on herself and on Joseph, when she wanted from him and tried to seduce him, door after door. And his saying:
h
And she said

, ‘Come to you,’ the reading of that differed. The general reading of Kufa and Basra is: Hayt lak, with the ha’ and ta’ open, meaning: come to you, come close, and draw near, as the poet said to Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him: Tell the Commander of the Faithful, the brother of Iraq, when you come Iraq and its people are yours, so come on come on Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Mukhrami told me, he said, Abu Al-Jawab told us, he said, Ammar bin Zuraiq told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Heet Lak, he said: Come to you.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: Heet lak, you say: Come to you.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told us, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Hait lak, you say: Come to you.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Asim bin Bahdala, on the authority of Zur bin Habish,
m: that he used to read this letter: Hait lak, in the accusative case, meaning: come to you.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said, his statement: Heet laka, he said: You say: Come to you.

c: Ahmad bin Suhayl al-Wasiti told me, he said, Qara bin Isa told us, he said, al-Nadr bin Arabi al-Jazari told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Heet laka, he said: Come to you, he said: It is in Hawraniyah.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And she said
, ‘Come to you,’ Al-Hasan said: He is saying: Come to you.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Heet lak, some of them say: Come to you.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And she said
, ‘Come to you,’ he said: Come to you, and it is in Coptic.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab bin Ata’ told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Heet lak, he said: a word in Syriac, meaning: upon you.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Heet lak, he said: Come to you.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Khalaf bin Hisham told us, he said, Mahbub told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Heet lak, he said: Come to you. He said, Affan told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, Heet lak, meaning: Come.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us, he said:
m: It reached me regarding his saying: Hey, come to you, he said: Come to you.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told us, Abu Ubaid told us, Ali bin Asim told us, on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that he read: Heet laka, and he said: She invites him to herself.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: Heet Lak, he said: It is an Arabic language, you call upon Him with it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, except that he said: It is a dialect in Arabic, in which she calls him to herself.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Shababah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: like the hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr, exactly the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told us, he said, Al-Qasim told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Hait lak, with the ha and the ta open, and he said: You say: Hallam lak.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abu Ubaid said:
m: Al-Kisa’i used to say it, meaning: Come to you. He said: And he said: It is the language of the people of Hawran that reached the Hijaz, and its meaning is: Come. He said: And Abu Ubaidah said: I asked a knowledgeable sheikh from the people of Hawran, and he mentioned that it is their language, and he knows it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Heet lak, he said: Come.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And she said
, ‘Come to me.’ He said: Come to me.

x: A group of the ancients read it as: And I have prepared for you, with a kasra on the ha’, a damma on the ta’, and a hamza, meaning: I have prepared for you, from the saying of the speaker: I have prepared for the matter, I have prepared a state. Among those who narrated this from him are Ibn Abbas, Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Qasim Al-Salami, and a group of others.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told us, Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Aban Al-Attar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Ibn Abbas read it like this, with a kasra on the ha’ and a damma on the ta’. Ahmad said: Abu Ubaidah said: I do not know it except with a hamza.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, on the authority of Aban Al-Attar, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Salami:
m: It is ready for you, meaning: it is prepared for you. He said, Abd al-Wahhab told us, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah, the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Ikrimah used to say: I have prepared myself for you.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: I prepared it for you. Ikrimah said: I prepared it for you.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Asim bin Bahdalah, he said:
m: Abu Wa’il used to say: Ha’it laka, meaning: I have prepared myself for you. Abu Amr bin Al-Ala’ and Al-Kisa’i used to reject this reading. Narrated on the authority of Ali bin Al-Mughira, who said: Abu Ubaidah Muammar bin Al-Muthanna said: I witnessed Abu Amr and Abu Ahmad - or Ahmad - asked him. He was a scholar of the Qur’an and had brilliance. Then he grew old and sat in his house, and the Qur’an was taken from him, and he was with the judges. So he asked him about the statement of the one who said: Ha’at laka with a kasra on the ha’ and a hamza on the ya’. Abu Amr said: It is bad, i.e. false. He made it a verb from tahay’at. This is the trench, so review the Arabs until you reach Yemen. Do you know anyone who says: Ha’at laka?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Qasim told us, he said:
m: Al-Kisa’i did not narrate I prepared for you from the Arabs. The majority of the people of Medina read it as Hayt laka, with a kasra on the ha’, a sukoon on the ya’, and a fatha on the ta’. Some Meccans read it as: Hayt laka with the ha’ open, the ya’ silent, and the ta’ closed. Some Basrans, including Abdullah bin Ishaq, read it as: Hayt lak, with the ya open and the ta closed. Some narrators recited a verse by Tarafa bin Al-Abd about Heet, with the ha’ open and the ta’ closed, and it is: My people are not the farthest away if a caller from the tribe says: Hit Abu Jaʿfar said: The most appropriate reading for this is the reading of those who read it: Hayt laka, with the ha’ and ta’ open, and the ya’ silent, because it is the language known among the Arabs and not others, and it is, as mentioned, the reading of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, he said: Ibn Mas’ud said:
m: I heard the recitation, and I heard them close together: So recite as you have been taught, and beware of being too strict and differing, for it is like one of you saying: Come, come. Then Abdullah recited: Heet you, so I said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, some Surat Yusuf 12:23 And the woman in whose house he was sought to seduce him, and she closed the doors and said, "Come here!" He said, "God forbid! Indeed, my Lord has made my stay good. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed." people recite it: Heet you. Abdullah said: I recite it as you have been taught, and it is more beloved to me.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, he said:
m: I heard Abdullah bin Masoud reciting this verse:
h
And she said
, ‘Come to you,’ he said: They said to him: We did not recite it except ‘Come to you,’ so Abdullah said: I recite it as you were taught, it is more beloved to me.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, he said: Abdullah said:
m: Hayt laka, so Masruq said to him: Some people read it: Hayt laka? He said: Leave me, for I like to read it as you read it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam Al-Asqalani told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, he said:
m: Hait lak, with the ha’ and the ta’ in the accusative case, and without a hamza. Abu Ubaidah Maʿmar ibn al-Muthanna said: The Arabs do not dualize, pluralize, or feminize heet, and that they form it in every case. The number is only determined by what comes after it, as well as the feminine and masculine forms. He said: You say to one person: Heet for you, to two al-Nas 114:Heet for you both, to a group: Heet for you, and to women: Heet for you. And the Almighty says: God forbid, meaning that He, the Most High, says: Joseph said, when the woman called him to herself and said to him: Come to me, I seek refuge in God from that to which you are calling me, and I seek His protection from him. And his saying:
h
He is my Lord
, He has made my abode good, means: Your companion and husband is my master, just as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: God forbid,
h
he is my Lord
, he said: My master. He said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh:
h
He is my Lord
, he said: My master.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He said, ‘God forbid! My Lord has made my stay good.’ He said: My master, meaning the woman’s husband.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: He said, ‘God forbid,
h
he is my Lord
,’ meaning: Atfir. He said: He is my master. And his saying:
h
He made my abode good
, means: He made my position good, honored me, and entrusted me, so I will not betray Him, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: h
He made my abode good
, meaning he made me feel secure in his house and his family.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
He made my abode good
, so I will not betray him in his family.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: My abode is good, he said: He means Joseph, his master, the woman’s husband. And his saying: Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed, means that he who commits injustice will not attain survival nor will he succeed, so he does what he should not do. And this immorality that you are calling me to is injustice and betrayal of my master who entrusted me with his home, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed. He said: What you are calling me to is injustice, and whoever acts upon it will not succeed.

evidence.text: And his saying: And she said, ‘Come to you,’ the reading of that differed.

The general reading of Kufa and Basra is: Hayt lak, with the ha’ and ta’ open, meaning: come to you, come close, and draw near, as the poet said to Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him: Tell the Commander of the Faithful, the brother of Iraq, when you come Iraq and its people are yours, so come on come on Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Mukhrami told me, he said, Abu Al-Jawab told us, he said, Ammar bin Zuraiq told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Heet Lak, he said: Come to you.

Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Asim bin Bahdala, on the authority of Zur bin Habish, that he used to read this letter: Hait lak, in the accusative case, meaning: come to you.

A group of the ancients read it as: And I have prepared for you, with a kasra on the ha’, a damma on the ta’, and a hamza, meaning: I have prepared for you, from the saying of the speaker: I have prepared for the matter, I have prepared a state.

Ahmad bin Yusuf told us, Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Aban Al-Attar, on the authority of Qatada: Ibn Abbas read it like this, with a kasra on the ha’ and a damma on the ta’.
Abu Amr bin Al-Ala’ and Al-Kisa’i used to reject this reading.
The majority of the people of Medina read it as Hayt laka, with a kasra on the ha’, a sukoon on the ya’, and a fatha on the ta’.
Some Meccans read it as: Hayt laka with the ha’ open, the ya’ silent, and the ta’ closed.
Some Basrans, including Abdullah bin Ishaq, read it as: Hayt lak, with the ya open and the ta closed.

Some narrators recited a verse by Tarafa bin Al-Abd about Heet, with the ha’ open and the ta’ closed, and it is: My people are not the farthest away if a caller from the tribe says: Hit Abu Jaʿfar said: The most appropriate reading for this is the reading of those who read it: Hayt laka, with the ha’ and ta’ open, and the ya’ silent, because it is the language known among the Arabs and not others, and it is, as mentioned, the reading of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, he said: Ibn Mas’ud said: I heard the recitation, and I heard them close together: So recite as you have been taught, and beware of being too strict and differing, for it is like one of you saying: Come, come.
Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed." people recite it: Heet you.
Abdullah said: I recite it as you have been taught, and it is more beloved to me.

Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, he said: I heard Abdullah bin Masoud reciting this verse: And she said, ‘Come to you,’ he said: They said to him: We did not recite it except ‘Come to you,’ so Abdullah said: I recite it as you were taught, it is more beloved to me.
Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, he said: Abdullah said: Hayt laka, so Masruq said to him: Some people read it: Hayt laka?
He said: Leave me, for I like to read it as you read it.

x: It was mentioned that when the wife of Al-Aziz was interested in Joseph and wanted to seduce him, she began to mention to him his good qualities and to make him yearn for herself, as: Ibn Wakee' narrated, Amr ibn Muhammad narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And she desired him and he desired her. He said: She said to him: O Joseph, how beautiful your hair is! He said: It is the first thing to fall from my body. She said: O Joseph, how beautiful your face is! He said: It is eaten by the dust. She did not stop until she fed him. She desired him and he desired her. They entered the house, the doors were closed, and he went to undo his trousers, and suddenly he saw the image of Jacob standing in the house, biting his finger and saying: O Joseph, do not have intercourse with her, for until you have intercourse with her, your example is like that of a bird in the sky that cannot be tamed.

And if you have intercourse with her, your example is like that of a bird that dies and falls to the ground, unable to defend itself. And your example, unless you have intercourse with her, is like that of a stubborn bull that cannot be worked on. And your example, if you have intercourse with her, is like that of a bull when it dies, and ants enter the base of its horns, and it cannot defend itself. So he tied up his trousers and went to go out, but she caught up with him and took hold of the back of his shirt from behind and tore it, until she pulled it out of him and he fell, and Yusuf threw it and ran towards the door.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: She leaned on him, meaning the woman, sometimes tempting him and other times hiding him, and inviting him to the pleasure of men’s need for her beauty, goodness, and possessions, and he was a young man who found the same lust for men as a man finds, until he felt pity for her because of what he saw of her preoccupation with him, and he did not fear her until he and she became interested in him, until they were alone in one of his houses. The meaning of worrying about something in Arabic is: a person’s thinking about doing something unless he does it. As for Joseph’s concern for the woman and her concern for him, the scholars said about that what I will mention, and that is what: Abu Kurayb, Sufyan ibn Wakee’, and Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi told us:

c: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: He was asked about the concern of Joseph, what had happened? He said: He untied the purse and sat there as a circumciser would. The wording of the hadith is from Abu Kurayb.

c: Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Ibn Uyaynah told us,
m: he heard Ubayd God Ibn Abi Yazid Ibn Abbas regarding:
h
And she certainly desired him and he desired her

, he said: He sat with her as a circumciser would, and he untied the belt. Ziyad bin Abdullah Al-Hassani, Amr bin Ali, and Al-Hassan bin Muhammad told us, they said, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Yazid, he said, I heard Ibn Abbas asked: What happened to Joseph’s anxiety? He said: He untied the purse and sat there like a circumciser.

c: Ziyad bin Abdullah told me, he said, Muhammad bin Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Abbas: How much anxiety did Joseph have? He said: She lay down for him, and he sat between her legs.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah:
m: And she desired him and he desired her, he said: She lay down for him and untied his clothes.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Qubaysah bin Uqbah told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And she certainly desired him and he desired her
. What did he reach? He said: She lay down for him, and he sat between her legs, and he untied his clothes - or: her clothes.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yahya bin Saad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Abbas: How much anxiety did Joseph have? He said: She lay on her back, and he sat between her legs to take off his clothes.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Wakiʿ told us, and Wakiʿ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Nafiʿ bin Umar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas was asked about his statement:
h
And she certainly desired him and he desired her
, what was the extent of Joseph’s desire? He said: He untied the belt, meaning the trousers.

c: Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us, he said,
m: I heard Al-A’mash, on the authority of Surat Yusuf 12:24 And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her
h
had he not seen the proof of his Lord
. Thus did We avert from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants. Mujahid, regarding the statement:
h
And she certainly desired him and he desired her
, he said: He untied his trousers until they reached his buttocks, and she lay down for him.

c: Ziyad bin Abdullah Al-Hassani told us, Malik bin Sa’ir told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And she certainly desired him and he desired her
, he said: He untied his trousers until they fell on his buttocks.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And she certainly desired him and he desired her
, he said: He sat with her as a man sits with his wife.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, he said, Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza told me:
m: And she desired him and he desired her. He said: As for her desire for him, she lay down for him, and as for his desire for her, he sat between her legs and took off his clothes.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Abdullah bin Abi Malekah told me,
m: who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: How much did Joseph worry? He said: She lay down for him, and he sat between her legs, taking off his clothes.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Yahya bin Al-Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr and Ikrimah, they said:
m: He untied his trousers and sat in them as a circumcised person would.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad Al-Anqazi told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And she desired him and he desired her, he said: She lay down, and he untied his clothes until he reached his buttocks.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: And she desired him and he desired her, he said: He released the button of his trousers.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Abi Malikah, he said:
m: I witnessed Ibn Abbas being asked about the concern of Joseph, how much? He said: He untied the purse, and sat there as a circumciser would.

x: How can he be described in such a way, while he is a prophet of God?
The scholars differed on that.

Some of them said: Whoever among the prophets was afflicted with a sin, God afflicted him with it so that he would be fearful of God Almighty when he mentioned it, and would find in his obedience compassion for it, and would not rely on the breadth of God’s forgiveness and mercy.
Others said: Rather, God tested them with this, to make them know the place of His blessing upon them, by His pardoning them and leaving His punishment upon them in the Hereafter.

Others said: Rather, He tested them with this to make them leaders for the people of sin in the hope of God’s mercy, and to leave them despairing of His forgiveness for them if they repent. As for others who disagreed with the sayings of the predecessors and interpreted the Qur’an according to their opinions, they said different things about that.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: The woman intended to harm Joseph, and Joseph intended to strike her or harm her, and he intended to harm her from what she wanted, had Joseph not seen the proof of his Lord, and that prevented him from harming her, not that she was deterred of her own accord. They said: The evidence for the correctness of that is His statement:
h
Thus did We turn away from him evil and immorality
. They said: So evil is what he intended to harm her with, and it is not immorality.

Others among them said: The meaning of the statement is: And she was certainly intent on him, and the report about her ended. Then the report about Joseph began, and it was said: And Joseph was intent on her
h
had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, as if they directed the meaning of the statement to the fact that Joseph was not intent on her, and that God only informed that Joseph
h
had he not seen the proof of his Lord

for them, but he saw the proof of his Lord and did not intend to do so, as it was said: And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few.

What invalidates these two statements is that the Arabs do not put the answer to lawla before it. They do not say: I stood up if it were not for Zayd, but rather they mean: If it were not for Zayd, I would have stood up. This is in addition to the disagreement between them and the scholars of the interpretation of the Qur’an, from whom its interpretation is taken.

Others among them said: Rather, the woman was interested in Joseph, and Joseph was interested in the woman, but their interest was a wavering between action and inaction, not determination or will. They said: There is no harm in talking to oneself, nor in mentioning the heart, if there was no determination or action with them. As for the proof that Joseph saw, which made him refrain from committing the sin, scholars differ on it.
Some of them said: It was announced that it was forbidden to commit sin.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord

, he said: He was called, O Joseph, are you committing adultery and becoming like a bird whose feathers have fallen out, so it goes flying but has no feathers? He said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He was not given the call until he saw the proof of his Lord. He said: A statue of the image of his father’s face - Sufyan said: Biting his finger - and he said: O Joseph, will you commit adultery and become like a bird whose feathers are gone?

c: Ziyad bin Abdullah Al-Hassani told me, he said, Muhammad bin Abi Uday told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abi Abi Malekah, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: It was called out: O son of Yaqub, do not be like a bird that has feathers, but when it commits adultery its feathers are lost, or it sits without feathers. He said: So he did not respond to the call, so he did not do more than that. Ibn Jurayj said: And more than one person told me that he saw his father biting his finger.

c: Abu Kurayb told me, he said, Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Nafi’ ibn Umar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: He was called but he did not hear, so it was said to him: O son of Jacob, do you want to commit adultery, so that you will be like a plucked bird with no feathers?

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Talhah, on the authority of Amr al-Hadrami, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, he said:
m: It has reached me that when Joseph sat between the woman’s legs and was untying his belt, he was called: O Joseph, son of Jacob, do not commit adultery, for when a bird commits adultery, its feathers scatter. So he turned away. Then he was called, so he turned away, and Jacob appeared to him biting his finger, so he stood up.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said,
m: Qubaysah bin Uqbah urged us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: It was called: O son of Ya’qub, do not be like the bird that when it commits adultery its feathers fall and it is left without feathers! But he did not obey the call, so he was frightened.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Abdullah bin Abi Malekah told me,
m: who said, Ibn Abbas said: It was called: O son of Jacob, do not be like a bird that has feathers, but when it commits adultery its feathers are lost - he said: or it sits without feathers - so he did not give anything in response to the call, until he saw the proof of his Lord, so he was afraid and fled.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Malikah, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: It was called: O son of Yaqub, do you commit adultery, so that you become like a bird whose feathers have fallen out, so it goes to fly but has no feathers?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Nafi’ bin Yazid told me, on the authority of Hammam bin Yahya, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Joseph was called and it was said: You are written among the prophets, yet you do the work of fools?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, he said:
m: It was called: Yusuf bin Ya’qub, are you committing adultery, so you will be like a plucked bird with no feathers?

x: Others said: The proof that saw Joseph and stopped committing the sin, for his sake, is the image of Jacob, peace be upon them, threatening him.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad Al-Anqazi told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: He saw an image - or: a statue - of the face of Jacob, biting his finger, and his desire came out of his fingers.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad Al-Anqazi told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: Jacob appeared to him, and he struck him on the chest, and his desire came out of his fingers.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr:
m: h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: He saw the statue of his father’s face, saying with his palm like this - and he spread out his palm - and his desire came out of his fingers.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: Jacob appeared to him biting his fingers, so he struck his chest, and his desire came out of his fingers.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Abdullah bin Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: He saw the image of Jacob placing his fingertip on his mouth, threatening him, so he fled.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Yahya bin Ibad told us, Jarir bin Hazim told us,
m: I heard Abdullah bin Abi Malekah narrating on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement:
h
And she certainly desired him and he desired her

, he said: When he saw Jacob on the roof of the house. He said: So his desire that he had been feeling was removed, until he ran out to the Surat Yusuf 12:24 And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her
h
had he not seen the proof of his Lord
. Thus did We avert from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants. door of the house, and the woman followed him.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Qura bin Khalid Al-Sadusi, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: They claimed, and God knows best, that the roof of the house split open, and he saw Jacob biting his fingers.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: He saw the statue of Jacob biting his finger, saying: Joseph! Joseph!

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Amr Al-Anqazi told us, Sufyan Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: He saw the statue of Jacob’s face, and his desire came out of his fingers.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ali ibn Badhima, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, who said:
m: He saw a picture in which there was the face of Jacob, biting his fingers, so he pushed him in the chest, and his desire came out of his fingers. So every son of Jacob had twelve sons, except for Joseph, who was diminished by that desire, and only eleven were born to him.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus bin Yazid told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab: that Hamid bin Abd al-Rahman told him:
m: that the proof that saw Joseph was Jacob.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Isa bin Al-Mundhir told us, he said, Ayoub bin Suwaid told us, he said, Yunus bin Yazid Al-Ayli told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Hamid bin Abd Al-Rahman,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: Jacob appeared to him like this.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: Jacob.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, and Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Yaqub gave him an example.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: He sat with her as a man sits with his wife, until he saw the image of Jacob on the walls.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: Jacob gave him an example.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, he said,
m: It was called: O son of Jacob, do not be like the bird that has feathers, but when it commits adultery it sits down without feathers. So he did not pay attention to the call and sat down, then raised his head and saw the face of Jacob biting his finger, so he stood up terrified, shy before God, and that is what God said:
h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, the face of Jacob.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Nadr Ibn Arabi, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: Jacob appeared to him biting his finger.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Nadr bin Arabi, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the same.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: Jacob appeared to him, he pushed him in the chest, and his desire came out of his fingers. He said, Abdul Aziz told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, who said: Each man of them had twelve sons, except for Joseph, who had eleven sons, because of what came out of his lust.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abu Shuraih said:
m: I heard Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar say: Joseph’s desire reached such a level that it came out of his fingertips.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ya’la ibn Ubayd told us, on the authority of Muhammad al-Khurasani, he said:
m: I asked Muhammad ibn Sirin about his statement:
h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: Jacob appeared to him biting his fingers, saying: Joseph, son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, the friend of God, your name is among the prophets, and you do the work of fools?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: He saw Jacob biting his finger, saying: Joseph!

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said, Qatada said:
m: He saw the image of Jacob and said: O Joseph, do you commit the act of the wicked, and you are written among the prophets? So he felt shy of him.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord

, he saw a sign of the signs of his Lord, by which God prevented him from disobeying Him. He mentioned to us that Jacob appeared to him until he spoke to him, so God protected him and removed every desire that was in his joints. He said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan: He saw Jacob biting one of his fingers.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Ismail bin Salim told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, he said:
m: He saw the image of Yaqub on the ceiling of the house, biting his finger and saying: O Joseph! He meant his saying:
h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansur and Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: He saw the image of Jacob on the ceiling of the house, biting his finger.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Salem, on the authority of Abu Saleh,
m: similarly, and he said: Biting his finger, saying: Joseph! Joseph!

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqoub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Hamid, on the authority of Shammar ibn Atiyah, he said:
m: We flew to Joseph to the image of Jacob biting his finger and saying: O Joseph! That is where he stopped, and he stood up and pushed away.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim and Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: He saw a picture in which there was the face of Jacob biting his fingers, so he pushed him in the chest, and his desire came out from between his fingers.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: He saw the statue of his father’s face, and desire came out of his fingers.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Yahya told us
m: - meaning Ibn Abbad - he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Salim, on the authority of Abu Salih:
h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: the statue of the image of Jacob in the ceiling of the house.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Jaafar bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of Yunus bin Ubaid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: He saw Yaqub biting his hand. He said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement:
h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: Jacob struck his chest with his hand, and his desire came out of his fingers.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, a sign from his Lord, and they claim that Jacob appeared to him, so he was ashamed of him.

x: Others said: Rather, the proof that Joseph saw is what God Almighty threatened his people with fornication.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, he said, on the authority of Abu Mawdud, he said,
m: I heard Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi say: He raised his head to the ceiling of the house, and there was writing on the wall of the house: “Do not come near adultery. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and an evil way.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Mawdud, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b, he said:
m: Joseph raised his head to the ceiling of the house when they were about to go out, and he saw writing on the wall of the house: “Do not come near adultery. Indeed, it is an immorality and an evil way.” He said, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, on the authority of Abu Maʿshar, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaʿb,
h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he said: Had he not seen in the Qur’an the glorification of adultery.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Nafiʿ ibn Zayd told me, on the authority of Abu Sakhr, he said:
m: I heard Al-Qurazi say about the proof that Joseph saw: Three verses from the Book of God: There are guardians over you the verse, and His saying: And you are not in any affair and His saying: Is he who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned? Nafiʿ said: I heard Abu Hilal say the same as Al-Qurazi, and he added a fourth verse: And do not come near to adultery.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abu Maʿshar told us,
m: on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaʿb Al-Qurazi!
h
Had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, so he said: What God has forbidden him of adultery.

x: Others said: Rather, he saw the statue of the king.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her
h
had he not seen the proof of his Lord
, he says: The signs of his Lord, he saw the statue of the angel.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Some of the people of Surat Yusuf 12:24 And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her
h
had he not seen the proof of his Lord

. Thus did We avert from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants. knowledge, as far as I have heard, used to say: The proof that Joseph saw and turned away evil and indecency from him was Jacob biting his finger, and when he saw him he ran away.

x: Some of them say: It was only the imagination of his master Atfir, when he approached the door. That is because when he ran away from her and she followed him, they found him at the door.

The most correct of the sayings in this regard is to say: God, the Most High, informed about the intention of Joseph and the wife of the Aziz, each one of them with his companion, had Joseph not seen the proof of his Lord. This is a sign from God that deterred him from committing what Joseph intended to commit of immorality. It is possible that this sign is a picture of Jacob, and it is possible that it is a picture of the king, and it is possible that the threat in the verses that God mentioned in the Qur’an is for adultery, and there is no conclusive argument for the excuse, no matter which of them it was. The correct thing is to say about this what God, the Most High, said, and to believe in it, and to leave everything else to His Knowledge. And His statement:
h
Thus did We turn away from him evil and immorality

, the Most High says: Just as We showed Joseph Our proof of the deterrent against the immorality he intended to commit, thus We caused him, in every thought that he intended to commit that which did not please Us, to be deterred and repelled from it, so that We might turn away from him the commission of what We have forbidden him and the committing of adultery, to purify him from the filth of that.
And his saying:
h
He is one of Our sincere servants
, there is a difference in the reading of that. The general reading of the people of Medina and Kufa is:
h
He is one of Our sincere servants

, with the opening of the lam of the sincere, with the interpretation: Joseph is one of Our servants whom We have sincerely devoted to Ourselves, and whom We have chosen for Our prophethood and message.
Some of the Basran reciters read:
h
He is one of Our sincere servants

, with a kasra on the lam, meaning: Joseph is one of Our servants who sincerely believed in our monotheism and worship of us, so they did not associate anything with us, and they did not worship anything other than us.

The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings that have been recited by many reciters, and they are in agreement in meaning. That is because whoever God has made sincere to himself and chosen him, he is sincere in monotheism and worship of God, and whoever is sincere in monotheism and worship of God and does not associate anything with God, he is one of those whom God has made sincere, so whichever of the two the reciter recites, he is correct.

evidence.text: And his saying: He is one of Our sincere servants, there is a difference in the reading of that.

The general reading of the people of Medina and Kufa is: He is one of Our sincere servants, with the opening of the lam of the sincere, with the interpretation: Joseph is one of Our servants whom We have sincerely devoted to Ourselves, and whom We have chosen for Our prophethood and message.

Some of the Basran reciters read: He is one of Our sincere servants, with a kasra on the lam, meaning: Joseph is one of Our servants who sincerely believed in our monotheism and worship of us, so they did not associate anything with us, and they did not worship anything other than us.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings that have been recited by many reciters, and they are in agreement in meaning.

x: God Almighty says: And Joseph and the wife of the Aziz raced to the door of the house. As for Joseph, it was fleeing from committing an immoral act when he saw the proof of his Lord, who forbade him from it. As for the woman, she sought Joseph to satisfy her need from him, which she had tried to seduce him with. So she caught up with him and clung to his shirt, preventing him from leaving through the door.
She lost him from behind, meaning she tore him from behind, not from the front, because Joseph was the one who fled, and she was the one seeking, as:

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they raced to the door, he said: He and the woman raced to the door, and she burned his shirt from the back.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: When he saw the proof of his Lord, he ran away from her, and she followed him and took his shirt from the back and tore it on him. And his saying:
h
And they found her master at the door
, God Almighty says: And they found her master - who is the woman’s husband - at the door, meaning: at the door, like the one who:

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And they found her master, he said: her master is her husband, at the door, he said: at the door.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, he said:
m: The master is the husband.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
And they found her master at the door
, meaning at the door. Ibn Wakee' narrated, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad narrated, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
h
And they found her master at the door

, he said: Sitting at the door, and her cousin was with him. When she saw him, she said: What is the reward of one who intended evil for your family? He sought to seduce me, so I repelled him and tore his shirt. Joseph said: Rather, she sought to seduce me, and I fled from her, then she caught up with me and tore my shirt. Her cousin said: This is evident in the shirt. If the shirt is torn from the front, then she is telling the truth and he is one of the liars. But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she is lying and he is one of the truthful. So the shirt was brought to him, and he found it torn from the back. He said: "Indeed, it is of your plot. Indeed, your plot is great. Joseph, turn away from this and ask forgiveness for your sin. Indeed, you were of the sinners."

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: h
And they found her master at the door
, Itfair, standing at the door of the house, so she said, fearing him: What is the recompense for one who intends evil for your family
h
except that he be imprisoned

or a painful punishment? And she smeared the place with the bad word, fearing that her master would accuse her of something ugly. So he said, and the hadith confirmed him: She tried to seduce me. And His statement: She said, ‘What is the reward of one who intended evil for your family?’ God Almighty says: The wife of Al-Aziz said to her husband when they found him at the door, and he omitted accusing her of immorality: What is the reward of a man who intended to commit adultery with your wife
h
except that he be imprisoned
in prison, or except that he be a painful punishment? He says: Painful. He said:
h
Except that he be imprisoned
or a painful punishment, because his saying:
h
Except that he be imprisoned
means: except imprisonment, so he linked the punishment to it, and that is because that and what it works on are like a noun.

x: God Almighty said: He said, ‘She sought to seduce me.’ And a witness from among her family testified, ‘If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is among the liars.’
God Almighty said: And if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is among the truthful.

God Almighty says: Joseph said, when the wife of Al-ʿAziz accused him of wanting to commit adultery with her, denying what she accused him of and repelling what was attributed to him: I did not seduce her, but she seduce me. It has been said that Joseph would not have mentioned that further, if she had not accused him of what she accused him of before her master.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Ammarah told me, he said, Ubayd God bin Musa told us, he said, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Nawf al-Shami, he said:
m: Joseph did not want to mention it, until she said: What is the recompense of one who intended evil for your family? The verse, he said: So he became angry and said: She tried to seduce me. As for his saying:
h
And a witness from among her family testified
, the scholars differed regarding the description of the witness.

x: Some of them said: He was a baby in the cradle.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Ala’ bin Abdul-Jabbar told us, on the authority of Hamaj bin Salamah, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Four spoke in the cradle while they were young: the son of the hairdresser of Pharaoh’s daughter, the witness of Joseph, the companion of Jurayj, and Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said:
m: Jesus, the companion of Joseph, and the companion of Gregory, meaning: they spoke in the cradle.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Zaydah told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: A boy.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: He was a baby in the cradle.

c: Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me, he said, Ayoub bin Jaber told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: A boy.

c: Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: similarly.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: He was a boy in his cradle.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Hilal bin Yasaf:
m: h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: A baby in the cradle.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abu Marzuq, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: A boy whom God made to speak. And it is said: An opinionated person with his opinion.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Affan told us, he said, Hammad told us, he said, Ata bin Al-Saib told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Four spoke when they were young, and he mentioned among them the witness of Joseph.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And a witness from among her people testified
, they claim that he was a boy in the house.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: He was a baby in the cradle.

x: Others said: He was a man with a beard.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: He had a beard.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: He was one of the king’s special people. And he said, my father told us, on the authority of Imran bin Jadir, who heard Ikrimah say:
h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: He was not a boy, but he was a wise man.

c: Suwar bin Abdullah told us, Abdul Malik bin Al-Sabah told us, Imran bin Hudayr told us, on the authority of Armah,
m: and he mentioned in his presence:
h
And a witness from among her people testified
, and they said: He was a boy. He said: He is not a boy, but he is a wise man.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: He was a man.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: A man.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: A man.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: A man.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: A bearded man.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Her cousin, the witness was from her family.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: A bearded man.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Ghassan told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: He has a beard.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah:
m: h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: He was one of the king’s special people.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a witness from among its people testified
, he said: A wise man who was from among its people.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a witness from among its people testified
, he said: A wise man from among its people.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: He was a man.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: A man with an opinion indicated his opinion.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And a witness from among her people testified

. He said: It is said that the witness was an advisor, a man from the people of Itfir, and he was assisted by his opinion, except that he said: I testify that if his shirt is torn from the front, then you have told the truth and he is the liar. It was said: The meaning of his saying: And a witness testified is the ruling of a judge. I narrated this on the authority of Al-Farra’, on the authority of Ma’la bin Hilal, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid.

x: Others said: What he meant by the witness was the torn shirt.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he said: His shirt was torn from the back, so that is the testimony.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a witness from among her family testified
, that his shirt was torn from the back, and that is the testimony.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And a witness from among her people testified
, he was not from among the humans. He said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And a witness from among her people testified
. He said: It was from the command of God, and it was not human.

x: The correct statement about that is the statement of those who said: He was a child in the cradle, based on the report that we mentioned from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he mentioned someone who spoke in the cradle, and he mentioned that one of them was the companion of Joseph. As for what Mujahid said about it being the torn shirt, it Surat Yusuf 12:28 So
h
when he saw his shirt torn from the back

, he said, "Indeed, this is of your plot. Indeed, your plot is great." is meaningless, because God Almighty mentioned about the witness who testified that he was from the woman’s family, saying: And a witness from her family testified, and it is not said about the shirt: it is from the man’s family, nor the woman’s. And his saying:
h
If his shirt was torn from the front
, then you have told the truth and he is one of the liars, because if the wanted person is a fugitive, then he will be approached from his anus.
