So it was known that if the tear was from the front, then he would not be a fugitive wanted person, but he would be a pursuer who was repelled, and that would be evidence of his lie. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that he said: I testify that if his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is one of the liars. That is because a man only approaches a woman from the front. But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is one of the truthful, that is because a man does not approach a woman from the back. He said: It is not appropriate for anything other than that to be the truth. So when he saw that his shirt was torn from the back, he knew that it was from her trickery, so he said: “It is from your trickery. Indeed, your trickery is great.”

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He said - meaning: the witness from her family - the shirt judges between them, “If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is among the liars. And if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is among the truthful. But
h
when he saw his shirt torn from the back
, he said, ‘Indeed, it is of your plot. Indeed, your plot is great.’”

x: The word that with which the testimony is received was omitted because he took the testimony to the meaning of the statement, as if he said: And a speaker from among her people said: If it was his shirt, as it was said: “God commands you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females,” because he took the commandment to the meaning of the statement. His saying:
h
When he saw his shirt torn from the back

, is a report about the woman’s husband, who said to her: This action is from your plotting - that is, your doing, meaning from the doing of women, Indeed, your plotting is great. It was said: It is report about the witness that he is the one who said that.
This is what was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, a report from God Almighty mentioned on the authority of Qayl, the witness, that he said to the woman and to Joseph.
He means by his saying: Joseph, O Joseph, disregard this, he says: Disregard mentioning what she did to you in the way she tried to seduce you, so do not mention it to anyone, like:

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: Joseph, turn away from this, he said: Do not mention it, and seek forgiveness, you and your husband, he said: Ask him not to punish you for the sin that you committed, and to forgive it and cover it up for you. You were among the sinners, he says: You were among the sinners in your attempt to seduce Joseph. It is said of it: he made a mistake in the sin, he made a mistake and a mistake, as the Most High said: Indeed, their killing was a great mistake, and the mistake in the matter. And it was also said in the correctness, the correctness and the correctness, as the poet said: By your life, my mistake and my correction are on me, and I did not waste money. And he recites the verse of Umayyah: Your servants make mistakes, but You are the Lord who protects against fate and inevitability. From: Man's mistake. It was said: You were among the sinners, and he did not say: among the sinful women, because he did not mean by that to inform about women, but rather he meant to inform about the one who does that and makes a mistake.

evidence.text: And he recites the verse of Umayyah: Your servants make mistakes, but You are the Lord who protects against fate and inevitability.

x: God Almighty says: And the women talked about the matter of Joseph and the matter of the wife of Al-Aziz in the city of Egypt, and what happened about them became widespread there, so it was not concealed, and they said: The wife of Al-Aziz is seeking to seduce her young man, her slave, for himself, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: The talk spread in the village, and the women talked about his affair, his affair, and her affair, and they said: The wife of Al-Aziz is trying to seduce her young man, meaning her slave. As for Al-Aziz, he is: the king in the speech of the Arabs, and from this is the saying of Abu Dawood: A pearl that a merchant dived for, I showed it to Aziz one day It means the king, which is from the word Izza. His saying:
h
He was overcome with love for her

, means: Joseph’s love reached the depths of her heart and entered beneath it, until it overcame her heart. The pericardium is the covering and veil in which it is located. Al-Nabigha Al-Dhubyani meant it when he said: They prevented it from entering the pericardium that the fingers seek. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Amr bin Dinar told me:
m: that he heard Ikrimah say regarding his statement:
h
He was overcome by love for her
, he said: His love entered under the pericardium.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He has overwhelmed her with love
, he said: His love has entered her pericardium.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
He has overwhelmed her with love
, he said: His love has entered her pericardium.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
He was overcome with love for her

, he said: His love was in her heart. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, like Al-Hasan Ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Shababah.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He has become passionately in love with her
, meaning:
h
He has become passionately in love with her

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He has overcome her with love
, he said: He has overcome her.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ayoub bin Aaidh al-Ta’i, on the authority of al-Sha’bi:
m: He was madly in love with her, he said: The madly in love is the lover, and the madly in love is the madman. And he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu al-Ashhab, on the authority of Abu Raja and al-Hasan: He was madly in love with her. One of them said: He was madly in love with her. And the other said: He was truly in love with her.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He has filled her with love
, he said:
h
He has filled her with love
. Yaqub said: Abu Bishr said: The people of Medina say,
h
He has filled her with love

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: I heard him say regarding His statement:
h
He has filled her with love
, he said: Her stomach is filled with love. And the people of Madinah say that.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, on the authority of Qura, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: He was deeply in love with her, he said: He was deeply in love with her.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abu Qatan told us, he said, Abu Al-Ashhab told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: He has made her mad with love, he said: Her stomach is full of love for him.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Surat Yusuf 12:
m: 30 And some women in the city said, "The wife of Al-'Aziz is seeking to seduce her young man. Love has overwhelmed her. Indeed, we see her in manifest error." Al-Hasan: He was madly in love with her, he said: He was infatuated with her.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
He has overwhelmed her with love
, he said: Her love for him has overwhelmed her.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
He has made her passionately in love
, meaning: He has made her attached.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He has fallen in love with her, he said: He has become attached to her with love.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: It is the love that sticks to the heart.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
He was overcome with love for her
, meaning: She died of love for him, and the pericardium is the pericardium of the heart.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told me, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
He was overcome with love for her

. He said: The pericardium is a skin on the heart called the tongue of the heart. He says: Love entered the skin until it affected the heart. There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of this. So I read it as most of the countries read it with the letter ghayn: qad ghafaha, with the meaning of what I described of the interpretation. Abu Raja read it as: He has made her thirsty, with an ‘ayn’.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Abu Qatan told us, Abu Al-Ashhab told us, on the authority of Abu Raja:
m: He was very fond of her. He said, Khalaf told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ashhab, or Aouf, on the authority of Abu Raja:
h
He was overcome with love for her

, with the eye. He said, Khalaf told us, Mahbub told us, Aouf read it: He has made her thirsty. He said, Abd al-Wahhab told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Asid, on the authority of al-A’raj: He was madly in love with her, and he said: Madly in love with her, if he loved her. They interpreted the meaning of the speech as meaning that love had overwhelmed her.

x: Some of the scholars of Arabic language from Kufa said: It is from the saying of the speaker: He was passionate about it, as if he went with it in every direction, from the peaks of the mountains, which are their tops.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i that he said:
m: Shaghaf is the passion of love, and Sha’af is the passion of an animal when it is frightened.

c: Al-Harith told me that, on the authority of Al-Qasim, who said:
m: It is narrated on the authority of Abu Awana, on the authority of Mughira, on his authority. Al-Harith said, Al-Qasim said: Ibrahim believes that the root of passion is panic. He said: And it is also as Ibrahim said in the original, except that the Arabs may have borrowed the word and put it in the wrong place. Imru’ al-Qais said: Are you killing me while her heart is infatuated with the way a happy woman is infatuated with a handsome man? He said: The passion of a woman comes from love, and the passion of a happy woman comes from fear, so he likened the pain of love and its atmosphere to that. Ibn Zayd said about this:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
He was passionately in love with her

, he said: Passion and passion are different, and passion is in hatred, and passion is in love. What Ibn Zayd said is meaningless, because in the speech of the Arabs, the word sha’f means love in general, and is more famous than for someone who is knowledgeable in their speech to be ignorant of it.

x: The correct reading in our view is: Qad ghafha with a ghayn, due to the consensus of the evidence from the readings on it. And His saying: Indeed, we see her in manifest error, they said: Indeed, we see the wife of Al-Aziz in her seduce of her young man, and his love for her overwhelming her, in a clear error in action, and a deviation from the intended path, clear, for whoever contemplates it and knows that it is error, and a mistake that is not correct or sound. Rather, what they said of that, and what they spoke of about her and Joseph, was a plot on their part, as mentioned, to show them Joseph.

evidence.text: There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of this.
So I read it as most of the countries read it with the letter ghayn: qad ghafaha, with the meaning of what I described of the interpretation.
Abu Raja read it as: He has made her thirsty, with an ‘ayn’.
He said, Khalaf told us, Mahbub told us, Aouf read it: He has made her thirsty.
Abu Jaafar said: The correct reading in our view is: Qad ghafha with a ghayn, due to the consensus of the evidence from the readings on it.

x: God Almighty says: When the wife of Al-Aziz heard about the treachery of the women who said in the city what God Almighty mentioned about them.
And he was forced to do what:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: When I heard of their treachery, he said: of their words.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: When the women revealed that, by saying: She is seducing her slave!, as a trick to show them Joseph, and he was described to them as being handsome and beautiful, So when she heard of their trick, she sent to them and prepared for them a place to recline.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So when I heard of their plot

, meaning their talk, I sent to them, he says: I sent to the women who talked about her and Joseph. I prepared for them, I prepared for them a reclining place, meaning a place to eat, and what they recline on of cushions and pillows. It is an artificial verb, derived from the saying: I leaned on. It is said: throw him a cushion, meaning: something to lean on. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Al-Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Saeed:
m: And I prepared for them a place to recline, he said: food, drink, and a place to recline. He said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And I prepared a place to recline for them, he said: They would recline on it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And I prepared for them a reclining place

, he said: a seat. He said, Amr bin Awn told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ashhab, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he used to recite: reclining and say: It is the sitting place and the food. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah bin Yazid told us: Whoever reads: reclining, light, yani means food. And whoever reads, reclining, means: the recliner. This that we mentioned from those we mentioned the interpretation of this word, is the meaning of the word, and the interpretation of the recliner, and that she prepared for the women a council in which there was a recliner, food, drink, and citron. Then some of them interpreted the recliner as the food, in the manner of reporting on the one for whom the recliner was prepared, and some of them on the reporting of the citron, since it was in the speech:
h
And she gave each one of them a knife
, because the knife is only prepared for the citron and what is similar to it that is cut with, and some of them on the buzmaward.

c: Harun bin Hatim Al-Muqri’ told me, he said, Hisham bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And I prepared for them a reclining place

, he said: Al-Bazmaward. Abu Ubaidah Muammar ibn al-Muthanna said: The cushion is a cushion that one leans on. He said: Some people claimed that it is a citron. He said: This is the most false falsehood on earth, but perhaps with the cushion there is a citron that they eat. Abu Ubaid Al-Qasim bin Salam narrated the words of Abu Ubaidah, then he said: The jurists are more knowledgeable about interpretation than him. Then he said: Perhaps it is some of what has been lost from the speech of the Arabs, for Al-Kisa’i used to say: Much of the speech of the Arabs has been lost and its people have become extinct.

x: The statement that the jurists are more knowledgeable in interpretation than Abu ʿUbaydah, as Abu ʿUbaydah said, is without doubt. However, Abu ʿUbaydah was not far from the truth in this statement, rather the statement is as he said, that he said about the recliner: it is the citron, but rather he explained what was prepared in the assembly in which the recliner is, and for which the knives were given, because it is known that knives are not prepared for the recliner except to ruin it! And they were not given the knives for that reason.

What shows the correctness of that statement is what we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the recliner is the seat, then it was narrated on the authority of Mujahid on his authority, what:

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us, he said: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And she prepared for them a place to recline and gave each one of them a knife, he said: She gave them citrons, and gave each one of them a knife. It is clear that Abbas, in this narration of Mujahid, did not give the women anything, and he ignored mentioning the meaning of the recliner, since its meaning was known. It was mentioned that he said in the interpretation of the recliner what we mentioned:

c: Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me, he said, Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And I prepared for them a reclining place
, he said: the citron.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Awf, he said,
m: I was told on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to read it: Muttaka’ with a light Muttaka’ and he would say: It is the citron.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Atiyah:
m: h
And I prepared a reclining place for them
, he said: food.

c: Yaqub and Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told me, they said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And I prepared a reclining place for them
, he said: Our food.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Ghundar told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And I prepared for them a reclining place
, he said: Food.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Wahb bin Jarir told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Whoever reads: reclining, it is food, and whoever reads it as reclining, and makes it lighter, it is the citron.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: reclining, he said: Our food.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid - and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Abu Khalid Al-Qurashi told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Whoever reads: Mataka, lightly, it is the citron.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, he said:
m: I heard some of them say: The citron.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And I prepared for them a place to recline, meaning food.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same. He said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: reclining, he said: food.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And I prepared for them a place to sit, meaning the citron.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And I prepared a reclining place for them
, and the reclining place is the food. He said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And I prepared a reclining place for them
, he said: food.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And I prepared for them a reclining place
, he said: Our food.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding his statement: reclining, that it refers to anything that is cut with a knife. Surat Yusuf 12:31 So when she heard of their plot, she sent to them and prepared for them a recliner and gave each one of them a knife and said, "Come out to them." But when they saw him, they were amazed at him and cut their hands and said, "God forbid!
h
This is not a human being
h
This is none other than a noble angel

x: God Almighty said, informing about the wife of Al-ʿAziz and the women who spoke about her in the city:
h
And she gave each one of them a knife
, meaning by that, may His praise be glorified: And she gave each one of the women who were present with her, a knife to cut whatever food she could cut with.
And that is what I mentioned that she gave them: either citron, or bezmaward, or something else that can be cut with a knife, like:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And each one of them was given a knife, and an citron for them to eat.

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told us: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And she gave each one of them a knife
, he said: She gave them a citron,
h
and she gave each one of them a knife

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And each one of them was given a knife, so that they could cut some of their food with it.

c: Yunus Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And she gave each one of them a knife
, and she gave them tangerines and honey, so they would cut the tangerines with the knife and eat them with the honey.

x: “This statement demonstrates the correctness of what we have said and chosen in His statement: ‘
h
And I prepared for them a reclining place

.’ This is because God, the Most High, mentioned that the wife of Al-ʿAziz gave the women knives, and left what he had given them as knives, since it is known that knives are not given to someone invited to a gathering except to cut what is eaten, if he cuts with them. So the listener’s understanding of the mention of her giving her companions the knives is sufficient, without mentioning what he had given them as a reclining place. Likewise, the mention of her preparing a reclining place for them is sufficient, without mentioning what is prepared for a reclining place from what is present in gatherings of food, drink, fruits, and various types of distraction, for the listeners’ understanding of what is meant by that, and the indication of His statement: ‘
h
And I prepared for them a reclining place
As for the reclining place itself, it is what we have described specifically and nothing else.” And His statement: And she said, ‘Come out to them.’
h
So when they saw him

, they glorified him, God Almighty says: And the wife of the Aziz said to Joseph, Come out to them, so Joseph came out to them. And when they saw him, they glorified him, God Almighty says: So when they saw Joseph, they glorified him and honored him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
We magnified Him
, meaning
h
we magnified Him

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he said, and Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: When they saw him, they glorified him, meaning: they magnified him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And she said, ‘Come out to them,’ to Joseph. And when they saw him, they glorified him, they magnified him.

c: Ismail bin Saif Al-Ajli told us, he said, Ali bin Abbas told us, he said,
m: I heard Al-Suddi say regarding His statement:
h
So when they saw him
, they glorified him, he said: they magnified him.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Go out to them
, so he went out, and when they saw him, they were amazed and astonished.

c: Ismail bin Saif told us, he said, Abdul Samad bin Ali Al-Hashemi told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So when they saw him
, they glorified him, meaning: embraced him.

c: Ali bin Dawud told us, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So when they saw him
, they glorified him, he said: they magnified him.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Yahya bin Abi Zaidah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: This statement - I mean the statement that was narrated from ʿAbd al-Samad, from his father, from his grandfather, regarding the meaning of they honored him, that it is a hug - if he did not mean by it that they hugged him out of their reverence for Joseph, and their glorification of what God had allotted him of splendor and beauty, and what women find of that when they see him, then it is a statement that has no meaning. Because the interpretation of that is: So when they saw Joseph, they honored him. The ha in they honored him is from the mention of Joseph, and there is no doubt that it is impossible for Joseph to be hugged. But the report, if it is authentic from Ibn ʿAbbas according to what was narrated, then it is appropriate that its meaning in that is: that they hugged because they honored Joseph’s beauty and handsomeness in themselves, and they found what women find of that.

Some narrators claimed that some people recited to him in Akbarna meaning: embrace, a verse that I do not think has any basis, because it is not known among the narrators, and that is: We come to women when they are pure, but we do not come to women when they are very old. He claimed that its meaning is: if he embraces. And his saying:
h
And cut off their hands
, the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that.
Some of them said: It means that they cut their hands with a knife, thinking that they were cutting an citron.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And cut off their hands
, cutting them in half with a knife.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
And cut off their hands
, he said: Cut, cut with knives.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid -
m: ... he said, and Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And cut off their hands
, he said: Cut, cut with a knife.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And they cut off their hands
, he said: The women began to cut off their hands, thinking that they were cutting off citrons.

c: Ismail bin Saif told us, Ali bin Abis told us,
m: I heard Al-Suddi say: They had knives in their hands with citrons, so they cut their hands and blood flowed, so they said: We blame you for loving this man, and we have cut our hands and blood flowed!

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: They began to cut their hands with knives, and they did not think that they were cutting oranges, their minds had gone from what they saw!

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And they cut off their hands
, meaning they cut off their hands.

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us, he said: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: They began to cut their hands, and they thought that they were cutting citrons.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And they cut off their hands
, he said: They began to cut off their hands without realizing it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: She said to Joseph:
h
Go out to them

, so he went out to them, and when they saw him, they were amazed by him, and their minds were overcome with amazement when they saw him, so they began to cut their hands with the knives they had with them, not understanding anything of what they were doing,
h
and they said
, ‘God forbid!
h
This is not a human being

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that they cut off their hands, even their children, without realizing it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: They cut off their hands until they threw them away.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they cut off their hands
, he said: They cut off their hands until they threw them away.

x: The correct statement about this is to say: God informed us that they cut off their hands without realizing it, out of respect for Joseph. It is possible that this was a clear cutting, and it is possible that it was a cutting with a cut and a scratch, and there is no statement about this that is more correct than accepting the apparent meaning of the revelation.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: Joseph and his mother were given a third of al-Hasan.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same. And on his authority, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: A third of Al-Hasan was divided for Yusuf and his mother.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: Joseph and his mother were given a third of good character.

c: Ahmad bin Thabit and Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Raziyan told me, they said, Affan told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, he said, Thabit told us, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Joseph and his mother were given half of beauty. Surat Yusuf 12:31 So when she heard of their plot, she sent to them and prepared for them a recliner and gave each one of them a knife and said, "Come out to them." But when they saw him, they were amazed at him and cut their hands and said, "God forbid!
h
This is not a human being
h
This is none other than a noble angel

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Muadh, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Joseph and his mother were given one-third of the beauty of the people of this world, and the people were given two-thirds, or he said: Joseph and his mother were given two-thirds, and the people were given one-third.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Rabia Al-Jurashi, he said:
m: Beauty was divided in half, so Joseph and his mother Sarah were given half of beauty, and the other half was given to the rest of creation.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Rabia Al-Jarshi, he said:
m: Al-Hasan divided it in half, he divided half for Yusuf and his mother, and half for the rest of the people.

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Rabia Al-Jarashi, who said:
m: Al-Hasan divided it into two halves, and gave half to Joseph and Sarah, and gave half to the rest of creation.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Isa bin Yazid, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Joseph and his mother were given a third of the beauty of this world, and the people were given two-thirds. And his saying:
h
And they said

, ‘God forbid.’ There is a difference in the reading of that. The majority of the Kufians read it as: Hash God, with the shin open and the ya deleted. Some Basrans read it with the addition of the letter ya: Hashi God. And there are languages in which it is not read: God forbid, as the poet said: Except for Abu Thawban, he is reluctant to be rude and insulting. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he used to read in this language: Hashi God and Hash God, with the shin and alif silent, combining the two silent letters. As for the reading, it is in one of the first two languages: whoever reads: Hash Lillah, with the shin open and the ya dropped, then he meant the language of the one who said: Hash Lillah, with the ya added, but he deleted the ya because of its frequency on the tongues of the Arabs, just as the Arabs deleted the alif from their saying: La aba li ghairak and La aba li shanik, and they mean: La aba li ghairak and La aba li shanik.

x: Some scholars of Arabic speech claimed that the phrase God forbid has two places in speech: One of them: sanctification. The other: the exception. In this place, we have the meaning of glorifying God, as if it was said: God forbid.

As for the statement about reading that, it is said: The reader has the choice to read it with whichever of the two readings he wants, if he wants with the reading of the Kufians, or if he wants with the reading of the Basrans, which is Hash Lillah and Hash Lillah, because they are two well-known readings and two well-known languages with one meaning. Other than that, they are languages that are not permissible to read with, because we do not know of a reader who read with them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And they said
, ‘God forbid.’ He said: God forbid.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his saying: God forbid, God forbid.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his saying:
h
And they said
, ‘God forbid,’ God forbid.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his saying: God forbid, God forbid. He said, Abdul Wahhab told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan: God forbid, God forbid.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Yahya told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. And his saying:
h
This is not a human being
, he says: They said:
h
This is not a human being

, because they had not seen anyone with the beauty of his appearance among humans, so they said: If he were a human being, he would be like some of what we have seen of the appearance of humans, but he is from the angels, not from humans, as:

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: “
h
And they said
: God forbid!
h
This is not a human being
,” that is not how humans are! And with this reading, the majority of the readers of the regions read, and:

c: It was narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Ziyad Al-Farra’,
m: who said: Di’amah bin Raja’ Al-Taimi - who was a warrior - narrated to me on the authority of Abu Al-Huwairith Al-Hanafi: that he recited: This is not good report, meaning: This is not something to be bought. He meant by this that they denied that someone like him could be a slave who could be bought and sold.

x: I do not permit reading with this reading, because the readers of the regions have agreed to disagree with it. We have explained that what they have agreed upon, it is not permissible to disagree with it. As for the accusative of humans, it is from the language of the people of Hijaz. If they drop the ba’ from the predicate, they put it in the accusative case, and say: Ma Amru qa’iman. As for the people of Najd, it is from their language to raise it, and they say: Ma Amru qa’iman. From this comes the saying of some of them where he says: How different I intend and all my father's sons intend, these two are not equal They wished me death, which separates the young man, and every young man and death meet. As for the Qur’an, it came in the accusative case in all of that, because it is in the language of the people of Hijaz.
And his saying:
h
This is none other than a noble angel
, means: They said: This is none other than an angel from among the angels, as:

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
This is none other than a noble angel
. He said: They said: An angel from the angels.

evidence.text: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Awf, he said, I was told on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to read it: Muttaka’ with a light Muttaka’ and he would say: It is the citron.

Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Whoever reads: reclining, it is food, and whoever reads it as reclining, and makes it lighter, it is the citron.
There is a difference in the reading of that.
The majority of the Kufians read it as: Hash God, with the shin open and the ya deleted.
Some Basrans read it with the addition of the letter ya: Hashi God.

As for the reading, it is in one of the first two languages: whoever reads: Hash Lillah, with the shin open and the ya dropped, then he meant the language of the one who said: Hash Lillah, with the ya added, but he deleted the ya because of its frequency on the tongues of the Arabs, just as the Arabs deleted the alif from their saying: La aba li ghairak and La aba li shanik, and they mean: La aba li ghairak and La aba li shanik.

Abu Jaʿfar said: As for the statement about reading that, it is said: The reader has the choice to read it with whichever of the two readings he wants, if he wants with the reading of the Kufians, or if he wants with the reading of the Basrans, which is Hash Lillah and Hash Lillah, because they are two well-known readings and two well-known languages with one meaning.
Other than that, they are languages that are not permissible to read with, because we do not know of a reader who read with them.
And with this reading, the majority of the readers of the regions read, and:
Abu Jaafar said: I do not permit reading with this reading, because the readers of the regions have agreed to disagree with it.

x: God Almighty says: The wife of Al-'Aziz said to the women who cut off their hands: This is what happened to you in your seeing him, and in his looking at you, you looked at him, what happened to you of the loss of reason and the absence of understanding and infatuation, distracted you until you cut off your hands, it is what you blamed me for in my love for him, and my heart's passion for him, so you said: The wife of Al-'Aziz has become passionately in love with her young man, we see her in clear error!

Then she admitted to them that she had tried to seduce him, and that what they had said about her in his affair was true, so she said: And she did try to seduce him, but he refused, from what she tried to seduce him about, as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: “She said, ‘This is what you blamed me for. I tried to seduce him, but he refused.’” She said: After he untied his pants, he refused. I do not know what happened to him!

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: So he resisted, meaning: he was obstinate.

c: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his saying: So he sought protection, meaning: he refrained. And his saying:
h
And if he does not do what I command him

, he will surely be imprisoned and will be among the humiliated, meaning: And if he does not obey me in what I call him to do due to my need for him, he will surely be imprisoned, you say: he will be detained, and he will be among the people of humiliation and degradation by imprisonment and jail, and I will humiliate him. And the pause at his saying: he will surely be imprisoned, is with the letter nun, because it is doubled, just as it was said: he will be slow. As for his saying: Wa li-yakuna, the pause on it is with an alif, because it is the light nun, and it is similar to the nun of i’rab in nouns in the saying of the speaker: I saw a man with you, so if he pauses on the man it is said: I saw a man, so the nun becomes an alif. So it is the same in: Wa li-yakuna. And similar to it is his saying: We will seize by the forelock * forelock - the pause on it is with an alif for what I mentioned, and from it is the saying of al-A’sha: Pray in the evening and the morning, and do not worship Satan, but worship God. It is: Worship, but if you stop at it, you stop with an alif.

x: This report from God indicates that the wife of Al-ʿAziz had repeatedly tried to seduce Joseph, and threatened him with imprisonment and confinement if he did not do what she had called him to do. He chose prison over what she had called him to do, because if she had not repeatedly tried to seduce him and threatened him with that, it would have been impossible for him to say: My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they call me, while he was not being called to anything, nor was he being threatened with imprisonment. And prison is the confinement itself, and it is the house of confinement. And by breaking the seen, it is read by the readings of all the countries. The Arabs place the places derived from verbs in the place of the verbs, so you say: the sun rose in the morning, and set in the evening, so they make them, and they are nouns, successors of the sources.

And so it is with the prison, so if you open the seen of the prison, it is a correct source. It has been mentioned that some of the predecessors read it: Prison is dearer to me, with the seen open. I do not permit reading it in this way, because the evidence from the readings is unanimously against it.
The interpretation of the words is: Joseph said: O Lord, confinement in prison is more beloved to me than what they call me to of disobeying You, and what they tempt me to do of immorality, as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: He said, ‘My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me,’ of adultery.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Joseph said, and he added to his Lord, and sought His help for what had befallen him: My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me, meaning: Prison is more to my liking than that I should do what You dislike. And His saying:
h
And unless You avert their plot from me

, I will incline toward them, meaning: And if You do not avert from me, O Lord, what they do to me, in their attempts to seduce me against themselves, I will incline toward them, meaning: I will incline toward them, and I will follow them in what they want from me and desire. From the saying of the speaker: So-and-so was drawn to such-and-such, and from it the saying of the poet: To Hind my heart yearns, and Hind like her it yearns And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: I follow them, he says: I follow them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And unless You turn away their plot from me
, meaning: what I fear from them, I will incline toward them.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And unless You turn away their plot from me
, I will incline toward them and be among the ignorant, he said: Unless there is support and protection from You, there will be no support from me or with me. And his saying:
h
And I will be among the ignorant
, he says: And I will be, through my infatuation with them, among those who are ignorant of Your right, and disobey Your command and prohibition, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And be among the ignorant, meaning: ignorant, if you commit your sin.

evidence.text: And by breaking the seen, it is read by the readings of all the countries.
It has been mentioned that some of the predecessors read it: Prison is dearer to me, with the seen open.
I do not permit reading it in this way, because the evidence from the readings is unanimously against it.

x: If someone were to say: What is the meaning of his saying:
h
And his Lord responded to him

, when Joseph did not ask his Lord for anything, nor did he ask to turn their plots away from him, but rather he informed his Lord that prison was more beloved to him than his disobedience? It was said: In his telling this there is a complaint from him to his Lord about what he encountered from them, and in his saying: And unless You turn away their plot from me, I will incline toward them, there is the meaning of a supplication and a request from him to his Lord to turn away their plot, and for this reason God Almighty said: So his Lord responded to him, and that is like the saying of one who says to another:
h
If you do not visit me
, I will humiliate you, and the other responds: Then I will visit you, because in his saying:
h
If you do not visit me
, I will humiliate you, there is the meaning of a command to visit.
The interpretation of the statement is: So God answered Joseph’s prayer, and diverted from him what the wife of Al-Aziz and her companions wanted from him of disobeying God, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: “So his Lord responded to him and averted from him their plot. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.” That is, He saved him from committing a sin in them, and some of what he was warned against had happened to him. And His saying: He is the All-Hearing, is the supplication of Joseph when he called upon Him to divert the women’s plots from him, and the supplication of every supplicant among His creation, the All-Knowing, of his request and need and what is good for him, and of the need of all His creation and what is good for them.

x: God Almighty says: Then it occurred to Al-Aziz, the husband of the woman who had tried to seduce Joseph. It was said: It appeared to them, and he is one, because he did not mention his name and meant him specifically, and this is similar to his saying: Those to whom the people said, ‘The people have gathered against you, so fear them.’ It was said: The one who said that was one. It was said that the meaning of his saying: Then it changed its mind to them is the opinion they had of leaving Joseph alone, and they thought that they should imprison him after they saw the signs of his innocence from what the wife of Al-Aziz had accused him of.
And those verses were about tearing the shirt from the back, scratching the face, and cutting off their hands, as:

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Nasr bin Auf, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Then it appeared to them after they had seen the signs, he said: Among the signs were: a tear in the shirt, and scratches on the face.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father and Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Nasr, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Then it appeared to them after they had seen the signs, he said: a piece of the shirt from the back.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: After they saw the signs, he said: The shirt was torn from the back.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid -
m: ... he said, and Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Warqaʿ, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: After they saw the signs, he said: The signs, he cut their hands, and the shirt.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The shirt is cut from the back.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Then it appeared to them, after they had seen the signs, to imprison him, by acquitting him of what he was accused of, of tearing his shirt from behind, to imprison him for a time.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: After they saw the signs, the shirt, and the cutting off of the hands. And his saying:
h
He will imprison him for a time

, means: He will imprison him until the time when they will see what they want. God made this imprisonment for Joseph, as mentioned, a punishment for his desire for the woman, and an expiation for his sin.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Zaidah, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: He will surely imprison him for a time. Joseph, peace be upon him, made three mistakes: when he was about to do so, so he was imprisoned. When he said, Mention me to your Lord, so he remained in prison for several years, and Satan made him forget to mention his Lord. And he said to them, You are indeed thieves, so they said, If he steals, a brother of his stole before. He stated that the reason for his imprisonment was the complaint of Al-Aziz’s wife to her husband about his and her affairs, as follows: Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs, to imprison him for a time. He said: The woman said to her husband: This Hebrew slave has disgraced me before the people. He apologizes to them and tells them that I tried to seduce him, but I cannot bear to make an excuse like this. So either give me permission to go out and apologize, or imprison him as you imprisoned me. This is what God says: Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs, to imprison him for a time. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the inclusion of this lam in lisajnanhu. Some Basrans said: It was entered here because it is a place where it falls in any, and when the interrogative letter entered it, the nun entered it, because the nun is used in interrogation. You say: It appeared to them which of them to take, meaning: it became clear to them. Some Arab scholars denied this and said: This is an oath, and his saying: Will you stand up with an oath? And that you stand up, it can only be an oath. Some Kufa grammarians said: It seemed to them means saying, and saying comes with all speech, with an oath and with a question, so it is permissible to say: It seemed to them that Zayd stood up, and it seemed to them that he would stand up. It was said: The word now in this context means seven years.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
He will imprison him for a time
, he said: seven years.

x: God Almighty says: And young men entered the prison with Joseph, so He indicated with that an omitted part of the speech, which is: Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs, to imprison him for a time, so they imprisoned him and put him in prison, and young men entered with him, so the evidence for His statement:
h
And young men entered the prison with him
, on their putting Joseph in prison, was sufficient from mentioning it.
The young men, as mentioned, were two of the king’s servants, one of whom was his drinker and the other his food provider, as follows:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: So he was thrown into prison - meaning Joseph - and two young men entered the prison with him, two young men who belonged to the great king, Rayyan ibn al-Walid, one of whom was in charge of his drinking, and the other of some of his affairs, in his anger with them, the name of one of them was Mujalth, and the name of the other was Nabu, and Nabu, the one who was in charge of the drinking.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And two young men entered the prison with him. He said: One of them was a baker for the king regarding his food, and the other was his cupbearer regarding his drink. The reason for the king’s imprisonment of the two young men, as mentioned, was as follows:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: The king became angry with his baker, he heard that he wanted to poison him, so he imprisoned him and imprisoned the one who made him drink, he thought that he had conspired with him in that, so he imprisoned them both, and that is what God said: And there entered the prison with him two young men. And his saying: “
h
One of them said

: ‘I saw myself pressing wine.’” It was mentioned that when Joseph, peace be upon him, was put into prison, he said to the prisoners in it, and they asked him about his work: I interpret dreams. So one of the two young men who were put into prison with him said to his companion: Come, let us test him, as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: When Joseph entered prison, he said: I interpret dreams. One of the two young men said to his companion: Come, let us test this Hebrew slave. They appeared to him and asked him questions, without having seen anything. The baker said: I see myself carrying bread on my head from which birds eat. The other said:
h
I see myself pressing wine

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us,
m: and Ibn Hamid said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Amara bin Al-Qa’qa’, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The two companions of Joseph did not see anything. They only dreamed of him to test his knowledge.

x: Some people said that the young men asked him about a dream that they had seen that was true and real, and that they had confirmed it to Joseph because he knew how to interpret it.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: When the young men saw Joseph, they said: By God, young man, we loved you when we saw you. He said, Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: That Yusuf said to them when they said that to him: I ask you by God not to love me, for by God, no one has ever loved me except that a calamity came upon me because of his love. My aunt loved me, and a calamity came upon me because of her love. Then my father loved me, and a calamity came upon me because of his love. Then my companion’s wife loved me, and a calamity came upon me because of her love for me. So do not love me, may God bless you both! He said: But they refused to do anything but love him and be kind to him wherever he was, and they began to admire what they saw of his understanding and intellect. And when they were put in prison, they had seen a vision. Mujalith saw that he was carrying bread on his head from which birds were eating, and Nabu saw that he was pressing wine. So they asked him about it and said to him: “Tell us its interpretation. Indeed, we see that you are among the doers of good,” if you do that. He meant by his saying:
h
I squeeze wine
, that is: I see in my dream that I squeeze grapes, and this is also the case in the recitation of Ibn Masoud, according to what was reported from him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah al-Sayegh,
m: on the authority Surat Yusuf 12:36 And there entered the prison with him two young men.
h
One of them said
, "Indeed,
h
I see myself pressing wine
h
And the other said
, "Indeed, I see myself carrying bread on my head from which birds eat.
h
Inform us of its interpretation

. Indeed, we see you among the doers of good." of Ibrahim ibn Bashir al-Ansari, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, who said: In Ibn Masoud’s recitation: Indeed, I see myself pressing grapes. He mentioned that this is from the language of the people of Oman, and that they call grapes wine.

x: Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd urged us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding his statement:
h
I see myself pressing wine
, he said: I am pressing grapes, and in the language of the people of Oman, they call grapes wine.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: I saw myself pressing wine. He said: Grapes, such-and-such land. They call grapes wine.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: I saw myself pressing wine, he said: grapes.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Sharik, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: He came to him and said: I saw in a dream that I planted a rope of grapes, and it grew and produced clusters of grapes, so I squeezed them and gave them to the king to drink. He said: You will remain in prison for three days, then you will come out and give him wine to drink. And His statement: “
h
And the other said
, ‘Indeed, I saw myself carrying bread on my head, from which birds were eating.
h
Inform us of its interpretation

.’” God Almighty says: And the other of the two young men said: I saw myself in my dream carrying bread on my head, meaning: I was carrying it on my head, so it was placed on a place on, from which birds were eating, meaning: from the bread. And his saying:
h
Inform us of its interpretation
, he says: Inform us of what the interpretation of what we told you we saw in our dreams will be, and it will be returned to, as:

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Qasim told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Inform us of its interpretation

, he said: It is. Al-Harith said, Abu Ubaid said: Mujahid means that the interpretation of a thing is the thing. He said: And from it: the interpretation of a vision, it is only the thing that it is interpreted to. And his saying: Indeed, we see you among the doers of good.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of goodness, with which he described the young men of Joseph.
Some of them said: He used to visit their sick, console their grieving, and if one of them needed something, he would collect it for him.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Saeed bin Mansour told us, Khalaf bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, who said:
m: I was sitting with him in Balkh, and he was asked about his statement: “
h
Inform us of its interpretation

. Indeed, we see you are of the doers of good.” He said: It was said to him: What was the goodness of Joseph? He said: When a person was sick, he would take care of him, and if he was in need, he would gather for him, and if he was in need, he would make things easier for him.

c: Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abu Israel, who said: Khalaf bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said:
m: A man asked Ad-Dahhak about his statement: Indeed, we see you among the doers of good. What was his goodness? He said: If a person was sick in prison, he would take care of him, and if he needed something, he would gather for him, and if the place was too small for him, he would make room for him.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Hussein narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdullah, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, we see you among the doers of good, he said: We have been informed that his goodness was that he used to treat their sick, console their grieving, and strive for his Lord. He said: When Joseph reached the prison, he found people in it whose hope had been cut off, and whose affliction had become severe and whose grief had become prolonged, so he began to say: Be of good cheer and be patient, and you will be rewarded, for this has a reward, for this has a recompense. They said: O young man, may God bless you, how beautiful your face is, and how good your character is, we have been blessed in your company, we would not like to be otherwise since we were imprisoned, because of what you tell us about the reward, expiation, and purification. Who are you, O young man? He said: I am Joseph, son of the chosen one of God, Jacob, son of the sacrificed one of God, Isaac, son of Abraham, the friend of God. And he was loved. The prison guard said to him: Boy, by God, if I could, I would set you free, but I will treat you well and keep you in prison well, so stay in whatever prison cell you want.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Khalaf al-Ashjaʿi, on the authority of Salamah ibn Nabit, on the authority of al-Dahhak,
m: regarding: Indeed, we see you among the doers of good, he said: He used to make room for men in his council, and he used to visit the sick.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: We see you among the doers of good, if you inform us of the interpretation of our vision.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: They asked him about their dreams, and he said to him: Tell us its interpretation, for we see that you are among the doers of good, if you do.

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter, in our view, is the saying that we mentioned on the authority of Ad-Dahhak and Qatada.

What is the point of speaking if the matter is as you said, and you know that their asking Joseph to tell them the interpretation of their dreams is not in any way a report of his description of visiting the sick and taking care of them and treating those in need well? Rather, it is said to the man: Tell us the interpretation of this, for you are knowledgeable. This is one of the situations in which descriptions of knowledge are improved, not otherwise.

The reason for that is that they said to him: Tell us the interpretation of our vision, and be kind to us in informing us of that, just as we see you doing well in all your actions: Indeed, we see you among the doers of good.

evidence.text: He meant by his saying: I squeeze wine, that is: I see in my dream that I squeeze grapes, and this is also the case in the recitation of Ibn Masoud, according to what was reported from him.

x: God Almighty says: Joseph said to the two young men who interpreted the dream: No food will come to you, young men, in your sleep, that you will be provided with except that I will inform you of its interpretation, in your waking state, before it comes to you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Joseph said to them: No food will come to you that you are provided with, in a dream, except that I will inform you of its interpretation, in wakefulness.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Joseph said to them: No food will come to you that you are provided with, meaning: in your sleep, except that I will inform you of its interpretation. What he means by his saying: by its interpretation is what the food they saw in their dreams would lead to and become. And his saying:
h
That is from what my Lord taught me
, he says: This is what I remember that I know of the interpretation of dreams, from what my Lord taught me, so I learned it,
h
I have abandoned the religion of a people who do not believe in God

, and the report came as a subject, meaning I have abandoned the religion of a people, and the meaning is: I have not deviated. And he began with that, because in the beginning is evidence of its meaning. And his saying:
h
I have abandoned the religion of a people who do not believe in God

, means: I have abandoned the religion of those who do not believe in God and acknowledge His oneness, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter, meaning: And with their abandonment of belief in the oneness of God, they do not acknowledge the afterlife or resurrection, nor reward or punishment. And they repeated it twice, so it was said: They are disbelievers in the Hereafter, because His saying: in the Hereafter came between them, so the first they became like the one that was cancelled, and the reliance was on the second, just as it was said: And they are certain of the Hereafter, and just as it was said: Does He promise you that when you die and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth?

x: What is the meaning and significance of this report from Joseph? And where is his answer to the two young men about what they asked him about the interpretation of their dreams, from this speech?

Joseph was reluctant to answer them about the interpretation of their dreams, because he knew that it would be unpleasant for one of them, so he ignored mentioning it and started doing something else, so that they would ignore asking him for an answer to what they asked him about. And in a manner similar to what some scholars said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement: “Indeed, I saw myself pressing wine. And the other said, “Indeed, I saw myself carrying bread on my head from which birds eat. Inform us of its interpretation.” He said: So he disliked the expression to them, and he told them something they had not asked him about, to show them that he had knowledge. And when the king wanted to kill someone, he would prepare a specific food for him and send it to him. So Joseph said:
h
No food will come to you that you will be provided with

, to His statement: give thanks. So he did not call him, so he turned away from them, and disliked the expression to them. So he did not call him until he interpreted it for them. So he turned away from them and said: O my two companions of the prison, are separate lords better or God, the One, the Prevailing? to His statement: they know. So he did not call him until he interpreted it for them, and he said: O my two companions of the prison, as for one of you, he will give his lord wine to drink, and as for the other, he will be crucified and the birds will eat from his head. They said: We did not see anything in it; we were only playing! He said: The matter you are asking about has been decided.

x: According to this interpretation that Ibn Jurayj interpreted, his statement,
h
No food will come to you that you will be provided with

, was in wakefulness, not in sleep. Rather, he informed them according to this statement that he had knowledge of what would happen to the food that would come to them from the king and from others with him, because he knew the type that if it came to them would be a sign of the killing of the one who came to it from them, and the type that if it came to him would be a sign of something else, so he informed them that he had Surat Yusuf 12:37 He said, "No food will come to you that you are provided with except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. That is from what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in God and who, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers." knowledge of that.
What he means by his saying:
h
And I have followed the religion of my fathers

, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and I have followed their religion, not the religion of the polytheists, It is not for us to associate anything with God, meaning: It is not permissible for us to make a partner for God in His worship and obedience, but rather what is upon us is to single Him out for divinity and worship,
h
That is from the grace of God upon us

, meaning: My following the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in Islam, and abandoning the religion of a people who do not believe in God and are disbelievers in the Hereafter, is from the grace of God that He has bestowed upon us, so He bestowed favors when He honored us with it, and upon the people, meaning: That is also from the grace of God upon the people, since He sent to them callers to His Oneness and obedience, But most people are not grateful, meaning: But whoever disbelieves in God does not thank Him for that from His grace upon him, because he does not know who bestowed it upon him, nor does he know the One who bestowed it upon him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
That is from the grace of God upon us
, that He made us prophets, and upon the people, he says: that He sent us as messengers to them.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
That is from the grace of God upon us and upon the people

, he mentioned to us that Abu al-Darda’ used to say: O Lord, there is someone who is grateful for a blessing but is not unaware of the one who has been blessed, and there is someone who carries knowledge but is not knowledgeable.

x: It was mentioned that Joseph, peace be upon him, said this statement to the two young men who entered prison with him, because one of them was a polytheist, so he called him with this statement to Islam and to abandon the worship of gods and idols, so he said: O companions of the prison, meaning: O one who is in prison, and he made them his companions, because they were in it, just as God Almighty said to the inhabitants of Paradise: Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally, and he said the same to the people of Hell, and called them its companions, because they were in it. And his saying:
h
Are separate lords better or God

, the One, the Prevailing? He says: Is the worship of different separate lords, and gods who neither benefit nor harm, better than the worship of the One God who has no equal in His power and authority, who has subdued everything and made it subservient, so that it obeys Him willingly or unwillingly.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O my two companions of prison

, are they separate lords? to his statement: They do not know, when the Prophet of God, Joseph, learned that one of them would be killed, he called them to their share from their Lord, and to their portion of their afterlife.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: O my two companions of the prison, Yusuf said it. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Then he called them to God and to Islam, and he said: O my two companions in prison, are separate lords better or the One, All-Powerful God? That is, is it better for you to worship one God, or separate gods who do not benefit you at all?

x: What he means by his saying:
h
What you worship besides Him

, is what you worship besides God. He said, What do you worship? He began the speech by addressing two people, saying, O my two companions of the prison, because he intended the one he was addressing, and the one who was residing in polytheism with God from the people of Egypt. So he said to the one he was addressing: What do you and the one who is like you in worshipping idols worship, except names which you and your fathers have named, and that is their naming of their idols as gods and lords, as polytheism on their part, and likening them in the names by which they named them to God, the Most High, who is far above having a likeness or resemblance, for which God has sent down no authority, meaning: They named them with names that He did not give them permission to name, nor did He establish for them that those names were their names, as evidence or proof, but rather they invented them and fabricated them.
And His saying: “
h
The rule belongs only to God

He has commanded that you worship none but Him,” means: He is the One who has commanded that you and all of His creation worship none but God, to whom belongs divinity and worship, purely without anything else besides Him, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah,
m: regarding his statement: “The rule is only for God. He has commanded that you worship none but Him,” he said: The religion was founded on sincerity to God alone, with no partner for Him. And His saying:
h
That is the right religion

, meaning: This to which I have called you, of disavowing the worship of idols other than God, and of devoting worship to the One, Almighty God, is the right religion in which there is no crookedness, and the truth in which there is no doubt. But most people do not know, meaning: But the people of polytheism with God are ignorant of that, so they do not know its reality.

x: God Almighty says, informing about what Joseph said to those who entered prison with him: O my companions of prison, will one of you serve his master wine? He is the one who saw that he was pressing wine and serving his master, meaning his master, who was their king, wine. He says: He will be the one who drinks it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
