Then he will give his master wine to drink

, he said: his master. As for the other, he is the one who saw that there was report on his head from which birds were eating, so he would be crucified and the birds would eat from his head, they mentioned that when he interpreted what they had told him that they had seen in their dream, they said to him: We did not see anything! So he said to them: The matter about which you were asking has been decided, meaning: The matter about which you were asking was concluded, and God’s judgment upon you is obligatory based on what I told you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amara, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: The two who entered prison with Yusuf said: We did not see anything! He said: The matter about which you are inquiring has been decided.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Amara bin Al-Qa’qa’, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: The matter about which you are asking has been decided. He said: When they said what they said, he told them, and they said: We did not see anything! So he said: The matter about which you are asking has been decided.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Amara, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding the two young men who came to Joseph and the vision, they were only dreaming to test him, but when he saw their vision they said: We were only playing! He said: The matter about which you were asking has been decided. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Jarir narrated, on the authority of Amara, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: The two companions of Joseph did not see anything. They were only dreaming to test his knowledge. One of them said: I see myself pressing grapes! The other said: I see myself carrying bread on my head from which birds are eating. “Tell us its interpretation. Indeed, we see you are of the doers of good.” He said: O companions of the prison, as for one of you, he will give his master wine to drink, and as for the other, he will be crucified and the birds will eat from his head. When he interpreted it, they said: We did not see anything! He said: The matter about which you are inquiring has been decided, as Joseph interpreted it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: He said to Mujalth: As for you, you will be crucified and the birds will eat from your head. And he said to Nabu: As for you, you will be returned for your deeds, and your companion will be pleased with you. The matter about which you are asking has been decided, or something like that.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said... You should ask about it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The matter about which you were asking has been decided, when they said: We did not see a dream, we were only playing! He said: The dream came true as you interpreted it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: that about which you both seek a fatwa, and he mentioned something similar.

x: God Almighty says: Joseph said to the one who knew that he would be saved from his two companions who had interpreted the dream for him:
h
Mention me to your Lord
, meaning: Mention me to your master, and tell him of my injustice, and that I am imprisoned without a crime, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said,
m: he said - meaning to the Prophet:
h
Mention me to your Lord
, meaning: Mention to the Most High King my injustice and my imprisonment for no reason. He said: I will do it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
Mention me to your Lord
, he said: To the one who was saved from the two companions of the prison, Joseph, he said: Mention me to the king.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Asbat:
m: And he said to the one whom he thought would be saved from the two of them, ‘Remember me before your Lord.’ He said: Before the King of the Earth.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Mention me to your Lord
, meaning the angel.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And he said to the one whom he thought would be saved from the two of them, ‘
h
Mention me to your Lord
,’ the one who was saved from the two prison guards, Joseph said: Mention me to the king.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham told us, Al-Awam bin Hawshab told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi:
m: When he reached the prison door, a companion said to him, What do you need? Advise me about your need! He said, My need is that you
h
mention me to your Lord
, other than the Lord. Yusuf said, Qatada was directing the meaning of suspicion, in this place, to suspicion, which is the opposite of certainty.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And he said to the one whom he thought would be saved from the two of them, ‘
h
Mention me to your Lord
.’ The vision is only expressed in conjecture, so God confirms what He wills and invalidates what He wills.

x: What Qatada said, that the expression of the vision is a conjecture, is also the case with other than the prophets. As for the prophets, it is not permissible for them to tell of a matter that it was and then will not be, or that it will not be and then will be, while testifying to the truth of what they told of, that it was or will not be, because if that were permissible for them in their reports, then such a thing would not be believed in any of their reports. And if that is not believed in their reports, then their proof against the one to whom they sent is dropped. If that is the case, then it is not permissible for them to tell of a matter unless it is true and honest. So it is known, since the matter was as it was described, that Joseph did not cut off his testimony to what he told the two young men who asked him to tell him would happen, so he said to one of them: As for one of you, he will give his master wine to drink, and as for the other, he will be crucified and the birds will eat from his head, then he confirmed that by saying: The matter about which you are asking has been decided, when they said: We have not seen anything, except that he was certain that what he told them of its occurrence and existence would inevitably happen, without doubt.

And because he was certain of that, he said to the one who had been saved from them: Remember me to your Lord. Thus, he demonstrated the corruption of what Qatada said about the meaning of his statement:
h
And he said to the one he thought would be saved from them
. And His saying:
h
Then Satan made him forget the remembrance of his Lord

, this is report from God, may He be glorified, about a negligence that happened to Joseph because of Satan, because of which he forgot to remember his Lord, who, if he had called upon Him for help, would have hastened his salvation.
But he slipped because of her, so he prolonged his imprisonment because of her, and made her suffer his punishment, as:

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Jaafar bin Sulaiman Al-Dab’i told us, on the authority of Bastam bin Muslim, on the authority of Malik bin Dinar, he said:
m: When Joseph said to the cupbearer:
h
Mention me to your Lord

, it was said: O Joseph, have you taken a guardian besides me? I will prolong your imprisonment! So Joseph wept and said: O Lord, my heart has forgotten the great affliction, so I said a word, so woe to my brothers.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Had he - meaning Joseph - not said the word that he said, he would not have remained in prison as long as he did.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim and Ibn Wakee’ told me, they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on Joseph. If he had not spoken to him, he would not have remained in prison as long as he did.” He meant by his saying:
h
Remember me with your Lord
. He said: Then Al-Hasan wept and said: When something befalls us, we turn to the people.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And he said to the one of them whom he thought would be saved
h
Mention me to your Lord

,’ he said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Had it not been for the word of Joseph, he would not have remained in prison as long as he did.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Yazid, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If Joseph had not said - meaning the word that he said - he would not have remained in prison as long as he did, meaning when he sought relief from someone other than God.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “Had Joseph not interceded with his Lord, he would not have remained in prison as long as he did. Rather, he was punished for interceding with his Lord.”

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: He said to him:
h
Mention me to your Lord

. He said: So he did not mention him until the king saw the vision, and that was because the devil made Joseph forget to mention his Lord, and ordered him to mention the king and seek relief from him, so he remained in prison for several years because of his saying:
h
Mention me to your Lord

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar, except that he said: So he remained in prison for several years, as punishment for his saying:
h
Remember me with your Lord
. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, like the hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr, the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: like the hadith of Al-Muthanna, he said, on the authority of Abu Hudhayfah. Muhammad bin Ishaq used to say: The devil made the cupbearer forget to mention the matter of Joseph to their king.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: When he - meaning the one who thought he was saved from the two of them - went out, he returned to what he was doing, and his companion was pleased with him, but Satan made him forget to mention that to the king whom Joseph had ordered him to mention. So Joseph remained in prison for several years after that. God Almighty says: So Joseph remained in prison, because he said to the one who was saved from the two companions of the prison, from the saying: Mention me to your master, for several years, as a punishment for him from God for that.

x: The interpreters differed about the amount of time Joseph spent in prison.
Some of them said: It is seven years.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad Abu Uthma told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Joseph remained in prison for seven years.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He remained in prison for a number of years, he said: seven years.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Imran Abu al-Hudhayl al-San’ani told us, he said:
m: I heard Wahb say: Job was afflicted with affliction for seven years, and Joseph was left in prison for seven years, and Nebuchadnezzar was tortured, so he was among the beasts for seven years.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: They claimed that it - meaning the few - was seven years, as Joseph stayed.

x: Others said: a few, meaning between three and nine.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Sulayman told us, Abu Hilal told us:
m: I heard Qatada say: The few is between three and nine.

c: Wakiʿ told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: A few years, he said: between three and nine. Surat Yusuf 12:42
h
And he said to the one of them whom he thought would be saved
h
Mention me to your Lord
." But Satan made him forget to mention his Lord, so he remained in prison for several years.

x: Others said: Rather, it is less than ten.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: A few years, less than ten. Al-Farraa claimed that the word bad’ is only mentioned with ten and with twenty to ninety, which is a little bit between three and nine. He said: “I saw the Arabs do this. They do not say: bad’ and a hundred, nor bad’ and a thousand. If it is for males, it is said: bad’.”

x: The correct thing in the word bad’ is from three to nine to ten, and it should not be less than three. Likewise, what is more than ten to one hundred, and what is more than one hundred does not have bad’ in it.
He, may He be glorified, meant by His statement:
h
And the king of Egypt said

: I see in a dream seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean cows. He said, I see, and he did not mention that he saw in his dream or elsewhere, because the Arabs are familiar with each other in their speech when one of them says: I see that I am doing such and such, that it is a report of his seeing that in his dream, even if he did not mention the dream. And He, may He be glorified, presented the report in the manner in which the Arabs have been accustomed to using it among themselves. And seven green ears of corn, he says: And I see seven green ears of corn in my dream, and another, he says: And seven other ears of corn, dry, O assembly, he says: O nobles from my men and companions: Examine my vision, so interpret it, if you are to interpret the vision, a lesson. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Kayʿ told us, he said, ʿAmr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: God showed the king in his sleep a vision that terrified him. He saw seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of corn and seven dry ones. So he gathered the magicians, the soothsayers, the fortune-tellers, and the soothsayers and told them about it. They said, These are confused dreams, and we are not experts in the interpretation of dreams.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Then King Rayyan bin Al-Walid saw the dream that he saw, which terrified him, and he knew that it was a dream that would come true, but he did not know what its interpretation was, so he said to the leaders around him from the people of his kingdom: I see seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, until his saying: in two worlds.

x: God Almighty says: The leaders whom the King of Egypt asked about the interpretation of his dream said: This dream of yours is a confused dream, meaning: it is a mixture, a false dream that has no truth to it. It is the plural of daghth, and daghth is originally a bundle of grass. It is likened to mixed dreams that have no interpretation. Dreams, the plural of dream, is a vision that is not true. Among the dreams is the saying of Ibn Muqbil: She looks like her bed is filled with basil leaves in the morning of the north. And from it the other said: The fetus's membrane protects it from the pressure of the uterus, which is hidden in the abdomen. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: confused dreams, he said: ambiguous.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: confused dreams, is false.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: When the king told his companions about the dream he had seen, they said: Confused dreams, meaning he had acted out dreams.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Confused dreams, he said: Mixed dreams, and we are not knowledgeable about the interpretation of dreams.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abu Marzuq, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said:
m: Confused dreams, are false. He said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: They said, ‘It is nonsense.’ He said: It is a lie.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: confused dreams, that they are false dreams. And his saying:
h
And we are not experts in the interpretation of dreams

, means: And we are not experts in what false dreams are interpreted into. The first ba in interpretation is from the connection of the two worlds, and the one in the two worlds is the ba that enters into the report with ma which means denial, and raising confused dreams, because the meaning of the speech is: This vision is nothing, it is only confused dreams.

x: God Almighty said: And the one who was saved from the two of them and remembered after a while said, ‘I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me.’

God Almighty says: And the one who escaped from being killed, of the two companions of the prison who interpreted the vision for Joseph, said, And remember, meaning: And remember what he had forgotten about the matter of Joseph, and he remembered his need for the king which he had asked him when he interpreted his vision to mention to him by saying: Mention me to your Lord, “after a time,” meaning: after a time, like the one who:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And remember after a time
, he said: after a while.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razeen, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us:
m: h
And remember after a time
, after a while.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razin, he said:
m: h
And remember after a time
, he said: after a while.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Razin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly. He said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying:
h
And remember after a time
, he said: after a while.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told us, he said, my uncle told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And remember after a time
, he said: Remember after a while.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And remember after a time
, after a while.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Affan told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed bin Abi Arubah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And remember after a time
, after a while.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Kathir said:
m: After a nation means after a while. Ibn Jurayj said: And Ibn Abbas said: After a nation means after years.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And remember after a time
, he said: after a while.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: And remember after a nation, meaning: after a period of time.

x: This interpretation is based on the reading of those who read: After a nation, with a damma on the alif and a shaddah on the meem, and this is the reading of the people of the lands of Islam.

c: It was narrated from a group of the ancients
m: that they read it: After his mother, with the alif open, the mim softened and opened, meaning: after forgetting.

x: Some of them mentioned that the Arabs say something like this: A man forgets his mother, may God have mercy on him, if he forgets. And the one who read it interpreted it in the same way.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Affan told us, he said, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: that he used to recite: After his mother, and explain it, after forgetting.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Bahz bin Asad told us, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: that he used to recite: After his mother, meaning: after forgetting.

c: Abu Ghassan Malik bin Al-Khalil Al-Yahmadi told me, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Abu Harun Al-Ghanawi, on the authority of Ikrimah
m: that he read: After his mother and the nation, forgetfulness. Surat Yusuf 12:46 Yusuf, O truthful one, give us your ruling concerning seven fat cows which seven lean ones have eaten, and seven green ears of corn and others dry, so that I may return to the people that they may know.

c: Yaqub and Ibn Wakee’ told me, they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Abu Harun al-Ghanawi told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said,
m: Harun said, and Abu Harun Al-Ghanawi told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, after his mother, after forgetting. He said, Abdul Wahhab told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah: And he remembered after his mother, after forgetting.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: meaning after forgetting.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And he remembered after his mother, he said: after he forgot.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Al-Nu’man A’rim told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim Abu Umayya Al-Mu’allim, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: that he recited:
h
And remember after his mother

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abu Marzuq, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: And he remembered after his mother, he said: after forgetting.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And remember after his mother
, he said: after forgetting. He mentioned a third reading, which is:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hamid, he said:
m: Mujahid read:
h
And remember after his mother

, with the meem in the jussive mood and lightened. It is as if the reader of this also meant the source of their saying: his mother, his mother, her mother. The interpretation of this reading is similar to the interpretation of the one who opens the alif and the mim. And his saying:
h
I will inform you of its interpretation
, meaning:
h
I will inform you of its interpretation

. Then send, meaning: then release me, so that I may go and bring you its interpretation from the One who knows it. There is something omitted in the speech, the mention of which was left out, as what was apparent sufficed with what was left out, and that is: So they sent him, and he came to Joseph and said to him: O Joseph, O truthful one, as:

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said, Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: The king said to the leaders around him: I see seven fat cows, the verse, and they said to him what he said, and Nabu heard from that what he heard and his question about its interpretation, he mentioned Joseph and what he interpreted for him and his companion, and what came from that according to what he said from his saying:
h
I will inform you of its interpretation

, so send, God says: And remember after a period, meaning a period of time, so he came to him and said: O Joseph, the king saw such and such, so he told him the vision, and Joseph said about it what God mentioned to us in the book, so its interpretation came to them like the break of dawn, so Nabu left Joseph with what he had given them of the interpretation of the king’s vision, and he told him what he had said. It was said that the one who escaped from them said: Send me, because the prison was not in the city.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And the one of the two who had escaped and remembered after a while said, ‘
h
I will inform you of its interpretation
, so send me.’ Ibn Abbas said: The prison was not in Medina, so the cupbearer went to Joseph and said: Give us your judgment concerning seven fat cows, the verses. His saying:
h
Give us your legal opinion about seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones

, and seven green ears of corn and seven others dry, means: Give us your legal opinion about seven fat cows being seen in a dream, seven of them being eaten by lean ones, and seven green ears of corn also being seen, and seven others dry. As for the fat cows, they are the fertile years, as:

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Give us a fatwa regarding seven fat cows that are eaten by seven lean ones. He said: As for the fat ones, they are fertile years, and as for the seven lean ones, they are barren years that do not produce anything.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Give us a fatwa regarding seven fat cows. The fat ones are the fertile ones, the lean cows, and the lean cows are the years of drought. His saying:
h
And seven green ears of corn and seven dry ones
. As for the green ones, they are the fertile years, and as for the dry ones, they are the drought-stricken years. Lean is the plural of Ajaf, which means emaciated. And his saying:
h
Perhaps I will return to the people so that they may know
, he says: that is, I will return to the people and inform them, perhaps they may know, he says: so that they may know the interpretation of what I asked you about regarding the vision.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: This interpretation is based on the reading of those who read: After a nation, with a damma on the alif and a shaddah on the meem, and this is the reading of the people of the lands of Islam.
It was narrated from a group of the ancients that they read it: After his mother, with the alif open, the mim softened and opened, meaning: after forgetting.
And the one who read it interpreted it in the same way.
He mentioned a third reading, which is:
The interpretation of this reading is similar to the interpretation of the one who opens the alif and the mim.

x: God Almighty says: Joseph said to his questioner about the king’s dream: You will plant for seven years in succession, meaning: You will plant these seven years, as you used to plant all the years before them according to your custom in the past. And habit, habit, and from that is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: As usual, from Umm Al-Harith before it and its neighbor Umm Al-Rabab in Masal It means: As usual from her. And his saying:
h
So whatever you harvest
, leave it in its ear, except a little of what you eat.
This is advice that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave to the people, and an opinion that he saw as good for them, ordering them to keep their food, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: The Prophet of God, Joseph, said to them: You shall cultivate for seven years, diligently, the verse, so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, only wanted to remain.

x: Then after the seven years in which you cultivated diligently, there will come seven difficult years, he says: barrenness and drought, they will eat what you have put in advance for them, he says: what you have put in advance in preparing for them in the seven fertile years of food and provisions will be eaten in them. And He, the Most High, said: They eat, so He described the years as they eat, but the meaning is that the people of that region eat during them, as it was said: Your day, you arrogant one, is full of negligence and heedlessness, your night is full of sleep, and destruction is inevitable for you. He described the day as being absent-minded and heedless, and the night as being asleep. He is absent-minded and heedless in this, and sleeps in this, so that those addressed know its meaning and what is intended by it. Except a little of what you protect, meaning: Except a little of what you protect.
And chastity is being placed in a fortress, but what is meant by it is protection. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They eat what you have put in store for them
, meaning: They eat what you have taken from them as food, except a little of what you have stored.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Then there will come after that seven difficult years, and they are the droughts, which will consume what you have put in store for them, except a little of what you have stored, of what you have stored.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Except a little of what you store, he said: you store.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: You fortify means you protect yourself.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
They eat what you have put in store for them
, except a little of what you have stored, he said: What you have stored.

x: These sayings about his statement, you are fortified, even if the words of those who said them differed, their meanings are close, and the origin of the word and its interpretation are as I have explained.

This is report from Joseph, peace be upon him, to the people about what was not in their king’s dream, but it is from the knowledge of the unseen that God gave him as evidence of his prophethood and proof of his truthfulness, as:

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Then God increased his knowledge of a year that they would ask him about, and he said: Then there will come after that a year in which people will be given relief and in which they will press [their grapes]. His saying,
h
In it people are helped
, means rain and downpour. And similar to what the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
Then there will come after that a year in which the people will be given rain
, he said: In it they will be given rain.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Muhammad bin Yazid Al-Wasiti told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: h
In it people are helped
, he said: with rain.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: Then there will come after that a year, he said: He informed them of something they had not asked him about, and God had taught it to him, a year in which people will be given relief, with rain.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
In it people are helped
, by rain. As for his saying:
h
And therein they press
, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.

x: Some of them said: It means: In it they squeeze grapes, dates, and the like.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And therein they press
, he said: grapes and oil.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
And therein they press
sesame oil, grape wine, and olive oil.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
A year in which people will be given rain and in which they will press grapes
, meaning: They will be afflicted with rain, in which they will press grapes, press oil, and press all kinds of fruits.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told me, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And in it they squeeze, he said: They squeeze their grapes.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And in it they press
, he said: grapes.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Muhammad bin Yazid Al-Wasiti told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: And in it they squeeze, he said: oil.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Aqtada:
m: And in it they squeeze, he said: They squeezed grapes and fruits.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And therein they press
, he said: They press grapes, olives, and fruits from the fertile soil. And this is knowledge that God gave Joseph, but he did not ask about it.

x: Others said: The meaning of his saying:
h
And in it they press
, is that they milk in it.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Fadala told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And in it they press
, he said: In it they milk.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, he said, al-Faraj ibn Fadala told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talha, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas used to recite: And in it you squeeze, with a ta’, meaning: you milk. There are different readings of this.

x: Some of the readers of Medina, Basra and Kufa read it as: And in it they squeeze, with a ya, meaning what was described, from the saying of those who said: the pressing of grapes and oils. The majority of the Kufian reciters read it as: And in it you squeeze, with a ta’.

Some of them read: And in it they squeeze, meaning: they make it rain. Surat Yusuf 12:49 Then there will come after that a year in which people will be given rain and in which they will press [their] grapes. This is a reading that I do not permit reading, because it is contrary to the reading of the regions.

The correct reading in this regard is that the reader has the choice to read it with whichever of the other two readings he wants, if he wants with the letter ya’, in response to the report about it from the people, meaning: in it the people are helped and in it they squeeze their grapes and oils, or if he wants with the letter ta’, in response to his statement: except a little of what you have stored up, and addressing it to the one he addressed with his statement: they will eat what you have put in store for them except a little of what you have stored up, because they are two readings that are widespread in the reading of the regions with an agreement in meaning, even if the wording differs in them. That is because those addressed by this were undoubtedly that if they were helped and squeezed, the people who were in their area would be helped and squeezed. Likewise, if the people in their area were helped and squeezed, those addressed would be helped and squeezed, so they are in agreement in meaning, even if the wording differed in the reading of that.

Some of those who had no knowledge of the sayings of the predecessors among the people of interpretation, who interpreted the Qur’an according to their opinion according to the way of the speech of the Arabs, directed the meaning of his statement:
h
Therein they press

, to: Therein they are saved from drought and famine by rain, and he claimed that it is from the word press and pressure, which means salvation, from the statement of Abu Zubayd al-Ta’i: Sadiya cries for help but is not helped, and he was squeezed by the helper Meaning: the oppressed. From the saying of Labid: So he and the captives spent the last part of their night, and they did not stop without a press. This is the interpretation that is sufficient as evidence of his mistake, contrary to the statement of all scholars among the Companions and Followers. As for the statement narrated by Al-Faraj bin Fadala, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, it is a statement that has no meaning, because it is contrary to what is known from the speech of the Arabs, and contrary to what is known from the statement of Ibn Abbas.

evidence.text: Some of the readers of Medina, Basra and Kufa read it as: And in it they squeeze, with a ya, meaning what was described, from the saying of those who said: the pressing of grapes and oils.
The majority of the Kufian reciters read it as: And in it you squeeze, with a ta’.
This is a reading that I do not permit reading, because it is contrary to the reading of the regions.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in this regard is that the reader has the choice to read it with whichever of the other two readings he wants, if he wants with the letter ya’, in response to the report about it from the people, meaning: in it the people are helped and in it they squeeze their grapes and oils, or if he wants with the letter ta’, in response to his statement: except a little of what you have stored up, and addressing it to the one he addressed with his statement: they will eat what you have put in store for them except a little of what you have stored up, because they are two readings that are widespread in the reading of the regions with an agreement in meaning, even if the wording differs in them.
Likewise, if the people in their area were helped and squeezed, those addressed would be helped and squeezed, so they are in agreement in meaning, even if the wording differed in the reading of that.

x: God Almighty says: When the messenger whom they had sent to Joseph returned, who said: I will inform you of its interpretation, so send, and informed them of the interpretation of the king’s vision about Joseph, the king knew the truth of what he had given him regarding the interpretation of his vision and the correctness of that, and the king said: Bring me the one who interpreted this vision of mine, like the one who… Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:

c: Then Nabu left Joseph with what he had told them
m: about the interpretation of the king’s dream, until he came to the king and told him what he had said.
b.via: Then Nabu left Joseph with what he had

c: When he told him
m: what was in his mind, it was like daylight, and he knew that what he had said would happen as he had said, he said: Bring him to me.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: When the king’s messenger came, he said: Bring him to me. And his saying:
h
So when the messenger came to him

, meaning: When the king’s messenger came to him calling him to the king, “he said: ‘Return to your lord,’” meaning: Joseph said to the messenger: Go back to your master, and ask him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands? And he refused to go out with the messenger and answer the king, until he knew the truth of his matter to them because of what they had disgusted him with regarding the women, so he said to the messenger: Ask the king what is the matter with the women who cut their hands, and the woman who was imprisoned because of them? Like: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: When the messenger came to him, he said, ‘Go back to your Lord and ask Him what happened to the women who cut their hands,’ and the woman who was imprisoned because of her matter, about what happened to that? Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said, Amr narrated, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:

c: When the messenger came to the king and informed him, he said:
m: Bring him to me. When the messenger came to him and invited him to the king, Joseph refused to go out with him and said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him what was the matter with the women who cut their hands, the verse. Al-Suddi said: Ibn Abbas said: If Joseph had gone out that day before the king knew about his situation, Al-Aziz would have still had a need for him. He would say: This is the one who tried to seduce his wife.
b.via: When the messenger came to the king and

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on Joseph, for he was patient. If I were the one imprisoned and he sent for me, I would have left quickly, for he was forbearing and patient.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said, Abu Salamah told us, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If I had remained in prison as long as Joseph remained, and then the caller came to me, I would have answered him, when the messenger came to him saying: ‘Return to your Lord and ask Him what was the matter with the women who cut their hands’” verse.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Sulayman bin Bilal told me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Zakariya bin Abaan Al-Masry told us, he said, Saeed bin Talid told us, he said, Abdul Rahman bin Al-Qasim told us, he said, Bakr bin Mudar told me, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Yunus bin Yazid, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said, Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab told me, on the authority of Abu Hurairah
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If I had remained in prison as long as Joseph remained, I would have answered the caller.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman,
m: and Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Affan bin Muslim told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And he recited this verse: Surat Yusuf 12:50 And the king said, "Bring him to me."
h
So when the messenger came to him

, he said, "Go back to your Lord and ask Him what was the matter with the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plot." ‘Return to your Lord and ask Him what was the matter with the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plot.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If it were me, I would have quickly answered and would not have sought an excuse.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, and Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: that he recited: Return to your Lord and ask Him what was the matter with the women who cut their hands, the verse, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If he had sent for me, I would have hastened to answer, and I would not have sought an excuse.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I was amazed by Joseph and his patience and generosity, may God forgive him, when he was asked about the lean and fat cows. If I were in his place, I would not have told them anything until I stipulated that they expel me. I was amazed by Joseph and his patience and generosity, may God forgive him, when the messenger came to him. If I were in his place, I would have rushed to the door, but he wanted to have an excuse.’”

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Go back to your Lord and ask Him what is the matter with the women
, the Prophet of God, peace be upon him, wanted him not to go out until he had an excuse.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: Go back to your Lord and ask Him what was the matter with the women who cut their hands. He said: Joseph wanted an excuse before he left prison. And his saying: Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plot, means: God Almighty is All-Knowing of their actions and deeds that they did to me and will do to other people. All of that is not hidden from Him, and He is the One who will punish them for that. It was said: The meaning of this is: My master, the dear Itfir, the husband of the woman who tried to seduce me, knows that I am innocent of the evil she committed against me.

evidence.text: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Affan bin Muslim told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And he recited this verse: Surat Yusuf 12:50 And the king said, "Bring him to me."

x: There is something omitted in this statement, and the evidence of what was mentioned about it is sufficient, which is: So the messenger returned to the king from Joseph with his message, and the king summoned the women who had cut their hands and the wife of the Aziz, and said to them:
h
What is the matter with you

that you tried to seduce Joseph? Like the one who: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: When the messenger came from Joseph with what he had sent to him, he gathered the women and said:
h
What is the matter with you
that you tried to seduce Joseph? What he means by his saying:
h
What is the matter with you
? What was your affair, what was your condition, when you sought to seduce Joseph for himself, and they answered him and said: God forbid! We know of no evil against him. The wife of the Aziz said:
h
Now the truth has become clear
, meaning:
h
Now the truth has become clear
and has been revealed and has become apparent, I sought to seduce him for myself, and Joseph is among those who were truthful in his saying:
h
She sought to seduce me for myself
And just as we said about the meaning of:
h
Now the truth has become clear
, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Now the truth has become clear
, he said: It has become clear.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
Now the truth has become clear
, it became clear: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Now the truth has become clear
h
now the truth has become clear

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Now the truth has become clear
, he said: It has become clear.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Now the truth has become clear
, he said: It has become clear.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Rachel, the wife of Ithavir al-Aziz, said:
h
Now the truth has become clear
, meaning: Now the truth has become apparent and clear, I sought to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful, regarding what Joseph had said of what she had claimed against him.

c: Ibn Wakee' told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: The king said:
m: Bring them to me! He said: What was the matter with you when you tried to seduce Joseph? They said: God forbid! We know of no evil against him.

c: But the wife of Al-Aziz told us that
m: she tried to seduce him, and he entered the house with her and untied his trousers, then tied them up after that, so she did not know what happened to him. Then the wife of Al-Aziz said:
h
Now the truth has become clear

c: Bunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said
m: about his statement:
h
Now the truth has become clear

, it has become clear. The root of Hashas is Has, but it is also said: Hashas, as he said: Fakabkabwa, in: Kabwa. It is also said: Kafkaf, in Kaf, and Dhardhar in Dhar. The root of Has is to uproot something. It is said from it: He uprooted his hair, if he uprooted it in parts. What is meant in this place by his saying:
h
The truth has become clear is that falsehood and lies have gone and been cut off
, and the truth has become clear and apparent.

x: What he meant by his saying:
h
That is so that he may know that I have not betrayed him in secret is this action that I did

, by returning the king's messenger to him, and not answering him and going out to him, and asking him to ask the women who had cut off their hands about their situation when they had cut off their hands, I only did it so that he may know that I had not betrayed him with regard to his wife, in secret, meaning: I did not commit an immoral act with her while he was absent from me.
And if he did not commit that act while he was absent, then when he was present with her he would be even more likely to be far from committing it, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: Joseph said:
m: That is so that he may know, the betrayal of his master, that I did not betray him in secret, that I would not have disobeyed him to his family without his knowledge.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
That is so that he may know that I have not betrayed him in secret
, Yusuf says it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
That is so that he may know that I have not betrayed him in secret
, Yusuf says it, I have not betrayed my master. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
That is so that he may know that I have not betrayed him in secret
, he said: Joseph said it.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret
. He said: This is Joseph.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Salem, on the authority of Abu Saleh,
m: regarding his statement:
h
That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret
, he said: He is Joseph, he did not betray Al-Aziz in his wife.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret
, that is, Joseph saying: I did not betray the king in secret. And his saying:
h
And that God does not guide the plot of the traitors
, he says: I did that so that my master would know that I did not betray him in secret,
h
And that God does not guide the plot of the traitors
, he says: And that God does not guide the actions of those who betray trusts, nor does He guide their actions in their betrayal of them. His statement,
h
That is so that he may know that I have not betrayed him in secret
, is connected to the statement of the wife of Al-Aziz, I sought to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful, so that the listeners may know its meaning, just as God’s statement,
h
And thus they do
, is connected to the statement of the woman, And they have made the most honorable of its people the most humble, because His statement,
h
And thus they do

, is the predicate of a subject, and likewise the statement of Pharaoh to his companions in Surat Al-A’raf, So what do you command? is connected to the statement of the leaders, He wants to expel you from your land.

x: Yusuf, peace be upon him, said: I do not exonerate myself from error and fault, so I purify it. Indeed, the soul is prone to evil. He says: The souls are the souls of the servants, commanding them to do what they desire, even if their desires are not in what pleases God. Except for what my Lord has mercy upon. He says: Except that my Lord has mercy upon whomever He wills of His creation, so He saves him from following his desires and obeying it in what it commands him to do of evil. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful. And ma in His statement:
h
Except what my Lord has mercy upon
, is in the accusative case, because it is an exception disconnected from what precedes it, like His statement:
h
Nor will they be saved * Except by mercy from Us

, meaning: Except that they are shown mercy. And an, if it is in the meaning of a source, is similar to ma. What he means by his saying: Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful is that God is forgiving of the sins of whoever repents from his sins, by leaving him punished for them and disgraced for them, Merciful to him after his repentance, by not punishing him for them.
It was mentioned that Joseph said this statement because when Joseph said:
h
That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret

, an angel said: Not even the day you thought of her? Then Joseph said: “And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil.” It was said: The one who said to Joseph: And not even one day did you think of her, so you took off your trousers? was the wife of the Aziz, so Joseph answered her with this answer. It was said that Joseph said that on his own initiative.

Who said that? Abu Kuraib narrated: Wakiʿ narrated, on the authority of Israʿil, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the king gathered the women and asked them: Did you try to seduce Joseph? They said: God forbid, we know of no evil against him! The wife of the Aziz said: Now the truth has become evident verse. Joseph said:
h
That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret
. Gabriel said to him: Not even on the day you intended what you intended? He said: “And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When the king gathered the women, he said to them: Did you try to seduce Joseph? Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith, like the hadith of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Wakee’.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When Pharaoh gathered the women, he said: Did you try to seduce Joseph? Then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: Gabriel nudged him and he said: Not even when you thought of her? Then Joseph said: “And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: When Joseph said:
h
That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret
, Gabriel, or an angel, said: Not even on the day you intended what you intended? He said: “And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil.”

c: Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, he said, Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: something similar, except that he said: The angel said to him: Not even when you were thinking of her? And he did not say: Or Gabriel. Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith in the same way.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bishr and Ahmad ibn Bashir told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr:
m: h
That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret
. He said, “Then the angel - or Gabriel - said to him: ‘Not even when you intended to do it?’ So Joseph said: ‘And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil.’”

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abu al-Hudhayl, who said:
m: When Joseph said,
h
That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret
, Gabriel said to him, Not even on the day you intended what you intended? He said, “And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Hudhayl,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: like the Surat Yusuf 12:53 And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except for that upon which my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful. hadith of Ibn Wakee’, on the authority of Muhammad bin Bishr and Ahmad bin Bashir, the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Ala’ bin Abdul-Jabbar and Zaid bin Habbab told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
That is so that he may know that I have not betrayed him in secret
. Gabriel said to him: Mention your concern! He said: “And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil.”

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Affan told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
That is so that he may know that I have not betrayed him in secret
. Gabriel said: O Joseph, mention your concern! He said: “And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil.”

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Salim, on the authority of Abu Salih,
m: regarding his statement:
h
That is so that he may know that I have not betrayed him in secret

, he said: This is what Joseph said. He said: Gabriel said to him: Not even when you untied your trousers? Joseph said: “And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil,” the verse.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Salem, on the authority of Abu Saleh,
m: something similar.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret

, he mentioned to us that the king who was with Joseph said to him: Mention what you intended to do. The Prophet of God said: “And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil.”

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It reached me that the king said to him when he said what he said: Do you remember your concern? He said: “And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except for that upon which my Lord has mercy.”

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret
, the king said, and he stabbed him in the side: O Joseph, not even when you intended to? He said: He said: And I do not acquit myself. It was mentioned that the one who said that was the woman.

c: Ibn Wakee' told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
That is so that he may know that I have not betrayed him in secret

, he said: Joseph said that when he was brought, so that Al-Aziz may know that he had not betrayed him in secret with regard to his family, and that God does not guide the plot of traitors. Then the wife of Al-Aziz said: O Joseph, not even the day you untied your trousers? Joseph said: "And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil." It was mentioned that Joseph said that to himself, without mentioning the one who mentioned it, but he remembered what had happened before from him in that regard.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told us, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret

and that God does not guide the plot of the traitors, is what Joseph said to his king, when God showed him his excuse, and he mentioned that he had intended to do it and she intended to do it, so Joseph said: “And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil,” the verse.

x: God Almighty says: And the king said, meaning the greatest king of Egypt, who, according to what Ibn Ishaq mentioned, is Al-Walid bin Al-Rayyan.

c: Ibn Hamid told us that, he said, Salamah told us,
m: on his authority. When Joseph's excuse became clear, and his trustworthiness and knowledge were known, he said to his companions: Bring him to me so that I may choose him for myself, meaning: I will make him one of my chosen ones, and no one else. And his saying: So when he spoke to him, he says: So when the king spoke to Joseph, and knew of his innocence and the greatness of his trustworthiness, he said to him: Indeed, O Joseph, you are with us, established and trustworthy, meaning: you are able to do whatever you want and whatever needs you have before us, due to the high status and position you have with us, trustworthy over whatever you have been entrusted with.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: When the king found an excuse for him, he said: Bring him to me so that I may take him for myself.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: I select him for myself, he said: I take him for myself.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Wakiʿ narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, who said:
m: The king said to him: Bring him to me so that I may take him for myself. He said: The king said to him: I want to take you for myself, but I am loath to have you eat with me. So Joseph said: I am more deserving of being loathed, I am the son of Ishaq - or: I am the son of Ishmael - Abu Jaʿfar was uncertain, and in my book: The son of Ishaq, the sacrifice of God, the son of Abraham, the friend of God.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Hudhayl,
m: something similar, except that he said: I am the son of Abraham, the friend of God, the son of Ishmael, the sacrifice of God.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, who said:
m: The Aziz said to Joseph: There is nothing but I would love for you to share it with me, except that I would love for you not to share my family with me, and for my servant not to eat with me! He said: Do I disdain to eat with you? But I am more deserving of disdain than you. I am the son of Abraham, the friend of God, and the son of Isaac who was sacrificed, and the son of Jacob whose eyes turned white from grief.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Sufyan ibn Uqbah narrated to us, on the authority of Amza al-Zayyat, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, who said:
m: When the Aziz saw the elegance, intelligence and charm of Joseph, he invited him and he would eat lunch and dinner with him without his servants. When what happened between him and the woman happened, she said to him: Come closer! Order him to eat lunch with the servants. He said to him: Go and eat lunch with the servants. Joseph said to him to his face: Do you wish to eat with me - or: are you turning away - I, by God, am Joseph, son of Jacob, the Prophet of God, son of Isaac, the sacrifice of God, son of Abraham, the friend of God.

x: God Almighty says: Joseph said to the king: Appoint me over the treasuries of your land. It is the plural of treasury.

i: The definite article al-ard the land was added to the word as a replacement for the addition, as the poet said:
x: Dreams are not single This is from Joseph, peace be upon him, a request from him to the king to give him control over the food and taxes of his country, and to take care of the affairs of his country, so the king did that for him, as far as I have been informed, as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: Put me in charge of the storehouses of the land, he said: Pharaoh had many storehouses other than food. He said: So he surrendered all his authority to him, and made the judgment his, his command and judgment are binding.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Ibrahim bin Al-Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Shaiba Al-Dhabi,
m: regarding his statement: Put me in charge of the storehouses of the earth, he said: in charge of preserving food. And his saying:
h
I am the Guardian
, the Knower, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.

x: Some of them said: The meaning of this is: I am the guardian of what you have entrusted to me, and I know what you have entrusted to me.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
I am the Guardian
, the Knower. I am the guardian of what you have entrusted to me, and I will do what you have entrusted to me. He said: I have done so.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, I am the Preserver, the Knower, meaning: I am the Preserver of what I have been entrusted with, and I am the Knower of its command.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibrahim bin Al-Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Shaiba Al-Dhabi,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed,
h
I am the Guardian
, the Knower, he said:
h
I am the Guardian
of what you entrusted to Me, and I am the Knower of the years of famine.

x: Others said: I am a guardian of the account, knowledgeable of tongues.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Al-Ashja’i:
m: I am a guardian, knowledgeable, a guardian of the account, knowledgeable of tongues.

x: The more correct of the two opinions in our view is the opinion of the one who said: The meaning of that is: I am a guardian of what you have entrusted to me, and I know what you have given me, because that follows his saying:
h
Make me over the storehouses of the earth

, and his asking the king to suffice him in the storehouses of the earth, so informing him that he has experience in that and that he is sufficient for him is more similar to informing him that he has preserved the account and is familiar with the tongues.

God Almighty says: And thus We established for Joseph in the land - meaning the land of Muʿammar - to settle therein wherever he wills, meaning: to take a home in the land of Egypt wherever he wills, after confinement and hardship, We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will, of Our creation, just as We bestowed upon Joseph, so We established him in the land after slavery and captivity, and after being thrown into the well, and We do not waste the reward of the doers of good, meaning: And We do not invalidate the reward of the work of the one who did good and obeyed his Lord, and did what He commanded him, and refrained from what He forbade him, just as We did not invalidate the reward of the work of Joseph when he did good and obeyed God. And Joseph was empowered in the land as: Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that he said: When Joseph said to the king: “Appoint me over the storehouses of the land.

Indeed, I am a knowing guardian,” the king said: I have done so! So he appointed him, as they say, to the work of Itafir, and removed Itafir from what he had been in charge of. God says: And thus We established Joseph in the land, to settle therein wherever he pleased, the verse. He said: It was mentioned to me, and God knows best, that Itafir had died during those nights, and that King Rayyan ibn al-Walid had married Joseph to Itafir’s wife Ra’il, and that when she entered upon him he said: Is this not better than what you wanted? He said: They claim that she said: “O friend, do not blame me, for I was a woman as you see, beautiful and lovely, comfortable in a kingdom and a world, and my companion did not come to women, and I was as God made you in your beauty and appearance, so my soul overcame me with what I saw.” They claim that he found her a virgin, so he had intercourse with her and she bore him two men: Have you seen Ibn Yusuf and Misha Ibn Yusuf.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And thus We established Joseph in the land, to settle therein wherever he willed. He said: The king appointed him over Egypt, and he was its ruler, and he was in charge of buying and selling, and all of its affairs. So that is what he said: And thus We established Joseph in the land, to settle therein wherever he willed.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, He may settle therein wherever he wishes, he said: We have given him control over whatever he wishes of that world, to do with it whatever he wishes, it has been entrusted to him. He said: And if he had wanted to make Pharaoh under his control and above him, he would have done so.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Kufi, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The king who was with Joseph converted to Islam.

x: God Almighty says: And the reward of God in the Hereafter is better for those who believe, meaning: for those who believed in God and His Messenger, from what Joseph was given in this world of His empowerment in the land of Egypt, and were fearful, meaning: and they were fearful of God, fearing His punishment for disobeying His command and making permissible His prohibitions, so they obeyed Him in His commands and prohibitions.

God Almighty says: And Joseph’s brothers came and entered upon him, and he recognized them, Joseph, but they, Joseph, disagree, they do not recognize him. The reason for their coming was Joseph, as he told me, as follows: Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Joseph was reassured in his kingdom and emerged from the affliction he was in, and the fertile years had passed, for which he had ordered them to prepare for the years he had told them would come, the people struggled in every direction and set out for Egypt seeking provisions from every town. When Joseph saw what he saw of the hardship that had befallen the people, he had been sympathetic to them, and he would not carry for each man more than one camel, nor would he carry for each man two camels, in order to be fair and generous to them. So he brought his brothers with those who had come to him seeking provisions from Egypt, and he recognized them while they did not recognize him, because God wanted to convey to Joseph, peace be upon him, what he wanted.

Ibn Wakee' narrated, Amr narrated, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: Famine struck the people, even reaching the land of Jacob where he was. So he sent his sons to Egypt, and he detained Joseph's brother Benjamin. When they entered upon Joseph, he recognized them, but they did not recognize him. When he looked at them, he said: Tell me what your matter is, for I do not recognize your affair! They said: We are people from the land of Ash-Sham. He said: What brought you? They said: We came to buy food. He said: You lie. You are spies. How many are you? They said: Ten. He said: You are ten thousand, each man of you is a commander of a thousand, so tell me your story. They said: We are brothers, sons of a man of truth, and we were twelve, and our father loved a brother of ours, and he went with us into the desert and one of us perished in it, and he was the most beloved of our father.

He said: Then to whom did your father live after him? They said: To a brother of ours who was younger than him. He said: How can you tell me that your father is a truthful man, and he loves the younger among you more than the older? Bring me this brother of yours so that I may look at him. But if you do not bring him to me, you will have no measure with me, nor will you come near him. They said, We will surely persuade his father about him, and we will surely do so. He said, Then place one of you as a hostage until you return. So they placed Simeon.
