c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they do not recognize him, he said: They do not know him.

x: He says: When Joseph loaded his camels with food for his brothers, and he loaded each man with his camel, he said to them:
h
Bring me a brother of yours from your father

, so that I can load another camel for you, so that you will have another camel’s load, Do you not see that I give full measure, so that I do not withhold from anyone, and I am the best of those who host, and I am the best of those who host a guest upon themselves from the people in this town, so I host you. Like: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And I am the best of hosts, and Yusuf says it, I am the best of those who host in Egypt.

c: Ibn Humayd told me, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: When Joseph was prepared with those who were prepared from among the people, he loaded each man with a camel for their equipment, then he said to them:
h
Bring me a brother of yours from your father

, so I will give you another camel, or something like that: Do you not see that I give full measure, meaning: I do not deprive people of anything, and I am the best of hosts, meaning: I am better for you than others, for if you bring him, I will honor your position, treat you well, and you will gain a camel with him for your equipment, for I will not give each man of you more than a camel, but if you do not bring him to me, then you will have no measure with me, nor shall you come near, do not come near my country.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Bring me a brother of yours from your father
, meaning Benjamin, who was Joseph’s brother from his father and mother.

x: God Almighty says, informing about what Joseph said to his brothers: But if you do not bring him to me, meaning your brother from your father, then you will have no measure with me, meaning: you will have no food with me that I can feed you, and you will not come near, meaning: and you will not come near my land. His saying:
h
And do not come near
, is in the place of a jussive with a prohibition, and the nun is in the place of an accusative, and it was broken because its ya was deleted, and the speech is:
h
And do not come near
me.
God Almighty said: They said, 'We will surely tempt his father away from him, and indeed, we will do so.'

God Almighty says: Joseph's brothers said to Joseph, when he said to them: Bring me a brother of yours from your father. "They said: We will seduce his father from him, and we ask him to leave him with us until he brings him to you, and we will surely do," meaning by that: And we will surely do what we told you we would do of seduce our father from our brother from him, and we will strive. Like: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: And indeed, We will do it, we will strive.
And His saying:
h
And he said to his young men
, ‘Put their merchandise in their saddlebags,’ God Almighty says: And Joseph said, to his young men, and they are his servants, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And he said to his young men

, meaning: to his servants. Put their merchandise in their saddlebags, he says: Put the price of the food that you took from them, in their saddlebags. And the traveler, the plural of traveler, is the plural of large. As for the small plural of it, it is: traveler, and it is the plural of between three and ten. And similar to what we said about the meaning of merchandise, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Put their merchandise in their saddlebags, meaning: their papers.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Then he ordered their merchandise for which he had given them the food he had given them to be put in their saddlebags without them knowing.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: h
And he said to his young men
while he was measuring for them: Put their merchandise in their saddlebags so that they may recognize it when they return to their families, so that they may return, to me.

x: Why did Joseph order his young men to put his brothers’ merchandise in their bags?

This could be interpreted in one way or another. One of them: That he feared that his father would not have any money, as the year was one of drought and famine, and taking it from them would harm him, and he wanted it to return to him. Or: He wanted his father and brothers to have more of it, despite their little need for it, so he returned it to them without them knowing the reason for his return. Yours sincerely. The third: That he intended by that that they would not break their promise to return, if they found in their baggage the price of food that they had taken and that someone else had taken possession of, in exchange for his food, and they would be embarrassed to keep the price of food that they had taken until they paid it to its owner, so that would be more likely for them to return to it.

God Almighty says: When Joseph’s brothers returned to their father, They said, ‘O our father, we have been denied the measure, so send our brother with us, that we may measure.’ He says: We have been denied the measure, in addition to the measure that was given to us, and each man among us was given only a camel’s measure, so send with us our brother, Benjamin, to measure for himself another camel’s measure in addition to the measure of our camels, and indeed, We will guard him, from any harm befalling him on his journey. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

Who said that? Ibn Wakee' narrated, he said, Amr narrated, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi: When they returned to their father, they said: O our father, the king of Egypt has honored us with an honor that we would not have been honored with if a man from the descendants of Jacob had been honored with. He has taken Simeon as a host and said: Bring me this brother of yours, whom your father devoted himself to after your brother who perished. If you do not come to me, do not come near my country. Jacob said: Shall I trust him with you except as I trusted you with his brother before? But God is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful. Jacob said to them: When you come to the king of Egypt, convey my greetings to him. And say: Our father prays for you and supplicates for you because of what you have given us.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: They went out until they came to their father, and their home was, according to what some of the people of knowledge told me, in the Arabat of the land of Palestine in the Ghor of Ash-Sham, and some say: in Al-Awlaj on the side of the valley, below Hisma, and he was a desert owner who had sheep and camels, so they said: O our father, we have come to the best man, he gave us a place and he honored our home, and he was kind to us and did not deprive us, and he ordered us to bring to him a brother of ours from our father, he said: If you do not do that, then do not come near me and do not enter my country. So Jacob said to them: Shall I entrust him to you except as I entrusted him to you before? But God is the best guardian, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: We measure. The majority of the people of Medina, and some of the people of Mecca and Kufa, read it as naktal with a nun, meaning: we and he both read it. The majority of the people of Kufa read it as: yaktul, with a ya’, meaning: he measures for himself, just as we measure for ourselves.

x: The correct statement in this regard is that they are two well-known readings that agree in meaning, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. This is because they informed their father that he had forbidden them to measure more than the number of their heads, so they said: O our father, he has forbidden us to measure. Then they asked him to send their brother with them to measure for himself. So if he measured for himself and they measured for themselves, then the brother was included in their number. So it is the same whether the report was about himself specifically, or about all of them in the wording of all, since the meaning of the speech and what was intended by it is understood.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: We measure.
The majority of the people of Medina, and some of the people of Mecca and Kufa, read it as naktal with a nun, meaning: we and he both read it.
The majority of the people of Kufa read it as: yaktul, with a ya’, meaning: he measures for himself, just as we measure for ourselves.

x: God Almighty says: Their father Jacob said: Shall I trust you with regard to your brother from your father, whom you ask me to send with you, except as I trusted you with regard to his brother Joseph before? He says: Before him. There is a difference in the reading of his saying:
h
So God is the best protector

. This was read by most of the people of Medina, some of the Kufians and the Basrans: God is the best of you in preservation, meaning: God is the best of you in preservation. The majority of the Kufians and some of the people of Mecca read it as:
h
So God is the best protector
, with an alif, based on the explanation of the protector that it is an interpretation of the good, just as it is said: He is the best man, and the meaning is:
h
So God is the best protector
among you, then the kaf and the mim were deleted.

The correct statement about this is that they are two well-known readings with similar meanings. Each of them has been recited by people of knowledge of the Qur’an, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. This is because whoever describes God as the best of them in memorization has described Him as the best of them in preserving, and whoever describes Him as the best of them in preserving has described Him as the best of them in preserving. And He is the Most Merciful of the merciful, He says: God is the Most Merciful of the merciful to His creation. He has mercy on my weakness in my old age, and my loneliness in losing my son, so He does not waste him, but rather He protects him until He returns him to me for His mercy.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: So God is the best protector.
This was read by most of the people of Medina, some of the Kufians and the Basrans: God is the best of you in preservation, meaning: God is the best of you in preservation.

The majority of the Kufians and some of the people of Mecca read it as: So God is the best protector, with an alif, based on the explanation of the protector that it is an interpretation of the good, just as it is said: He is the best man, and the meaning is: So God is the best protector among you, then the kaf and the mim were deleted.
Each of them has been recited by people of knowledge of the Qur’an, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct.

x: God Almighty says: When Joseph's brothers opened their goods that they had brought from Egypt from Joseph, they found their merchandise, which was the price of the food that they had measured from him, "returned to them. They said, "O our father, what do we want? This is our merchandise that has been returned to us." That is, they said to their father: What do we want? This is our merchandise that has been returned to us, as a way of pleasing himself with what he had done to them in returning their merchandise to them. If the speech is directed to this meaning, what is an interrogative in the accusative case, as in the saying: we want. Qatada directed him to this interpretation.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: What we seek, he said: We seek nothing beyond this, for our merchandise has been returned to us, and the full measure has been given to us. And his saying:
h
And we provide for our people

, means: We ask for food for our people and buy it for them. It is said: So-and-so provides for his family, and from it the poet said: I sent you as a guide, but you stayed for a year. When will your help come? And we will protect our brother, whom you send with us, and we will add a camel’s load, meaning: And we will add a camel’s load to our loads of food, and we will be measured out what another camel of ours has carried, that is a small load, meaning: This is a small load, as:

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Qasim told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: And we will gain an additional camel’s load, he said: Each man among them had a camel’s load, so they said: Send our brother with us, so we will gain an additional camel’s load. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: A camel’s load, a donkey’s load. He said: It is a language. Al-Qasim said: Mujahid meant that in some languages a donkey is called a camel.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And we will give you an additional camel’s load
, meaning: a camel’s load.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And we add a camel’s load, we count a camel with our camels, that is a small load.

x: God Almighty says: Jacob said to his sons: I will not send your brother with you to the king of Egypt, until you give me a covenant from God, meaning: until you give me a covenant from God, meaning a pledge, which is what is pledged with from an oath and a covenant, that you bring him to me, meaning: that you bring me your brother,
h
unless you are surrounded
, meaning: unless you are all surrounded by something that makes you unable to bring him to me. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told me, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
So when they gave him their pledge
, he said: their covenant.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Unless you are surrounded
, unless you all perish.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said, and Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Unless you are surrounded
, he said: Unless you are overcome until you are unable to do that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: regarding his saying:
h
Unless you are surrounded
, unless something happens to you that takes you all away, then that will be an excuse for you with me. And his saying:
h
So when they gave him their pledge

, meaning: when they gave him their covenants, he said, meaning: Jacob: God is witness over what we say, meaning: I and you, to the truth, meaning: He is a witness over us to the fulfillment of what we all say.

x: God Almighty says: Jacob said to his sons, when they wanted to leave him for Egypt to buy food:
h
O my sons
, do not enter Egypt through one path, but enter through separate gates.

It is reported that he said that to them because they were men of beauty and appearance, and he feared the evil eye if they entered in groups from one path, and they were the sons of one man, so he ordered them to separate when entering it, as:

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Yazid Al-Wasiti told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: Do not enter from one door, but enter from different doors. He said: He feared the evil eye for them.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O my sons
, do not enter through one door, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, feared the evil eye for his sons, who were of good appearance and beauty.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And enter through separate gates, he said: They had been given an image and beauty, so he feared for them the people’s souls.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And he said,
h
O my sons
, do not enter by one gate, but enter by separate gates, he said: Jacob, peace be upon him, was given the spring.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Do not enter through one gate
, that Jacob feared the evil eye for his son.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b,
m: Do not enter through one door, he said: He feared the evil eye for them. He said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: Jacob, peace be upon him, feared the evil eye for his sons, so he said:
h
O my sons
, do not enter from one gate, lest it be said: These belong to one man! Rather, enter from different gates.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said,
m: when they decided to go out - meaning the sons of Jacob - Jacob said:
h
O my sons
, do not enter from one gate, but enter from different gates, he feared for them from the eyes of the people, because of their appearance, and that they were one man. And His saying:
h
And I cannot avail you against God at all

, meaning: I am not able to ward off from you any of the decree of God that He has decreed upon you, whether small or large, because His decree is effective in His creation. The judgment is only for God, meaning: The judgment and ruling are only for God, not for anything else, for He rules over His creation as He wills, so He executes His judgment upon them and decides upon them, and His decree is not rejected. In Him I have put my trust, meaning: I have put my trust in God, so I have placed my confidence in Him regarding you and in your preservation of me, until He returns you to me while you are safe and sound, not regarding your entry into Egypt if you enter it through separate gates. And in Him let the trustful put their trust, meaning: And to God let those who put their trust entrust their affairs.

x: God Almighty says: And when the sons of Jacob entered from where their father had commanded them, and that was their entry into Egypt from different gates, it did not avail, their entry into it thus, for them, from the decree of God that He decreed concerning them and made it inevitable, of anything except a need in Jacob’s soul which He fulfilled, except that they satisfied a desire for Jacob by their entry, not from one path, for fear of the evil eye upon them, so his soul was reassured that they had not come from before that, or that something bad had befallen them because of him, as:

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Except for a need in Jacob’s soul that he fulfilled, fearing the evil eye on his sons.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Except for a need in Jacob’s soul that he fulfilled, he said: fear of the evil eye upon them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Except for a need in Jacob’s soul which he fulfilled

, he said: What he feared for his sons from the eyes of the people, because of their appearance and their equipment. And His saying: And indeed, he was possessed of knowledge because of what We taught him, God Almighty says: And indeed, Jacob was possessed of knowledge because of what We taught him. It was said: Its meaning is: He is a guardian of the knowledge that We have entrusted to his heart. He differed from Qatada in that:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: And indeed, he is possessed of knowledge of what we have taught him, meaning: of what we have taught him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Aruba, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He is a man of knowledge because of what we taught him, he said: He acts according to what he learned. Al-Muthanna said, Ishaq said, Abdullah said, Sufyan said: He is a man of knowledge, from what we have learned. And he said: He who does not act is not knowledgeable. But most people do not know, God Almighty says: But many people, other than Jacob, do not know what he knows, because We deprived him of that and he did not know it.

x: God Almighty says: When Jacob's son entered upon Joseph, he took his brother into his care, meaning: he took his brother from his father and mother into his care. And his sheltering him was as follows: Ibn Wakee' narrated, he said, Amr narrated, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
h
And when they entered upon Joseph

, he sheltered his brother with him. He said: He recognized his brother, so he accommodated them in a place, and provided them with food and drink. When night came, he came to them with a parable, and said: Let each of your two brothers sleep in a parable. When the boy was left alone, Joseph said: This one will sleep with me on my bed. So he spent the night with him, and Joseph began to smell his scent and hug him until morning. And Reuben kept saying: We have never seen anything like this! Give us relief from him! Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that he said: When they entered upon Joseph, they said: This is our brother whom you ordered us to bring to you.

We have brought him to you. It was mentioned to me that he said to them: You have done well and you have hit the mark, and you will find that with me, or something like that. Then he said: I see that you are men, and I want to honor you. He called his host and said: Bring down each man by two, then honor them and treat them well. Then he said: I see that this man whom you have brought has no one else with him, so I will take him to myself, and his home will be with me. So he brought them down two by two in different homes, and brought down his brother with him, and took him into his home. When he was alone with him, he said: I am your brother, I am Joseph, so
h
do not be sad
about what they did to us in the past, for God has been good to us, and do not tell them anything of what I have told you. God says: “
h
And when they entered upon Joseph
, he took his brother to himself. He said, ‘Indeed, I am your brother, so
h
do not be sad
about what they were doing.’”

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
And when they entered upon Joseph
, he took his brother into his care, he embraced him and brought him down, and he was Benjamin.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, he said, Abdul Samad bin Maqal told me, he said:
m: I heard Wahb bin Munabbih say - and he was asked about the words of Joseph: “
h
And when they entered upon Joseph
, he took his brother to himself. He said, ‘Indeed, I am your brother, so
h
do not be sad

over what they used to do.’” - how did he affect him when he took him with the measure, and he had told him that he was his brother, and you claim that he continued to disguise himself from them and plot against them until they returned? He said: He did not acknowledge the relationship to him, but he said: I am your brother, in place of your dead brother, so
h
do not be sad
over what they used to do, meaning: Do not be saddened by his position. His saying:
h
Do not be sad

, means: Do not be submissive or sad. It is: Do not make it from misery, it is said from it: he became miserable, he became miserable, misery. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatah:
m: h
Do not be sad
, he said:
h
Do not be sad
and do not despair.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, he said, Abdul Samad told me, he said:
m: I heard Wahb bin Munabbih say:
h
Do not be sad
, he said:
h
Do not be sad
about his place.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: So
h
do not be sad
about what they used to do, meaning:
h
Do not be sad
about what they used to do.

x: The interpretation of the statement then is:
h
Do not be sad
or humble about anything that your brothers have done to you in your soul, or in your brother from your mother, or what they used to do to you before today.
He says: When Joseph loaded his brothers’ camels with provisions, he fulfilled their needs, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So when he had provided them with their provisions

, he said: When he had fulfilled their need and given them their measure. And his saying: He put the water-drawing vessel in his brother’s saddlebag, means: He put the vessel with which he measures food in his brother’s saddlebag. The saqaya is the drinking place, which is the vessel from which the king drank and measured food. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Affan told us, he said, Abdul Wahid told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: He used to say: The sa’ and the siqaya are the same, it is the vessel from which one drinks. He said, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: The water-skin and the measuring cup are one thing, from which Joseph used to drink. He said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The water-skin is the cup from which Joseph drinks.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He made the water-trough, he said: the king’s drinking place.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The water-trough is in his brother’s saddlebag, which is the king’s vessel from which he used to drink.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: They said, ‘We miss the king’s cup, and whoever brings it will have a camel load,’ and it is the watering place from which the king used to drink, meaning his shuttle.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He made the drinking vessel
, and his statement: the king’s cup, he said: They are one thing, the drinking vessel and the cup, one thing, from which Joseph drinks.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding his statement:
h
He placed the drinking vessel in his brother’s saddlebag
, that it is the vessel from which the king used to drink.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
He placed the drinking cup in his brother’s saddlebag

, he said: The drinking cup is the measure, and it was a golden cup, according to what they mention. His saying: In his brother’s baggage, means: In the belongings of his brother, the son of his mother and father, who is Benjamin. And so said the people of interpretation.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: In his brother’s saddlebag, meaning: in his brother’s belongings. And his saying:
h
Then a caller called out
, meaning:
h
Then a caller called out
. It was said: I know the teacher. O caravan, and the caravan with its loads, you are indeed thieves. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: When he had equipped them with their provisions, he put the water-trough in his brother’s saddlebag, and the brother did not notice. So when they had set out, a crier announced before the caravan had set out: You are indeed thieves. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Then he prepared their provisions, honoured them, gave them and fulfilled them, and loaded one camel after another for them, and loaded a camel for his brother in his name as he had loaded it for them. Then he ordered the king’s watering place, which was the cup, and they claimed that it was made of silver, to be placed in the saddlebag of his brother Benjamin. Then he gave them time until they had set out and reached the Surat Yusuf 12:70 So when he had furnished them with their provisions, he put the drinking cup in his brother’s saddlebag. Then a crier proclaimed, “O caravan, you are indeed thieves.” village, then he ordered them to be caught up with and held back, then a crier called out: O caravan, you are thieves. Stop. Then his messenger came to them and said to them, as they recall: Did we not honour your hospitality, give you your full measure, treat you well, and do to you what we did not do to others, and bring you into our homes and dwellings? Or something like that. They said: Yes, but what is that? He said: We have lost the king’s watering place, and we do not accuse anyone but you of it. They said: By God, you know that we did not come to cause corruption on earth, nor were we thieves. And his saying: O donkey, we have previously explained the meaning of donkey, which is a plural that has no singular form.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The caravan of the sons of Jacob was made up of donkeys.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: O donkey, he said: They were donkeys.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, a man told me, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: O caravan, indeed you are thieves, he said: The caravan was donkeys.

x: God Almighty said: They said, as they turned to them, ‘What are you missing?’

God Almighty says: The sons of Jacob said, when they were called: O caravan, you are thieves, and they turned to the crier and those present, saying to them: What are you missing? What are you missing? “They said: We are missing
h
the king’s cup
,” meaning: So the people said to them: We are missing the king’s drinking place. There are different readings of this. It was mentioned on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he read it:
h
The king’s measure
, without the waw, as if he was directing it to the measure with which food is measured.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Raja
m: that he read it: The king’s voice.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Yaʿmar
m: that he read it: Sawg Al-Malik with a ghayn, as if he directed it to the fact that it is a source of their saying: Sagha yasughu Sawghan. As for what the regions read:
h
the king’s measure

, which is the reading that I do not permit reading other than it, due to the consensus of the evidence on it. The measure is the vessel that Joseph used to measure food with. And the interpreters said the same.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding this word:
h
The king’s cup
, he said: It is like a shuttle. He said: And Abbas had something similar in the pre-Islamic era from which he would drink.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The king’s cup
, he said: It was made of silver like a shuttlecock. And Abbas had one of them in the pre-Islamic era.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: They said, ‘We are missing
h
the king’s cup
,’ he said: It was made of silver.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: that he read: The King’s cup, he said: It was his vessel from which he drank, and it was as tall as it was.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Suwaid bin Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Awana, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
The king’s measure
, he said: the Persian shuttle.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: h
The king’s cup

, he said: It is the Persian shuttle whose two ends meet, from which the non-Arabs used to drink. He said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
The king’s cup
, he said: The king’s vessel from which he used to drink.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Yahya told us
m: - meaning Ibn Abbad - he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
h
The king’s cup
is a silver shuttle from which they drink. And Abbas had one in the pre-Islamic era.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
The king’s cup
is the king’s vessel from which he drinks.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Saeed bin Mansour told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The king’s measure
, he said: The Persian shuttle whose two ends meet.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The cup, from which Joseph used to drink.

c: Muhammad bin Muammar Al-Bahrani told us, he said, Abd Al-Samad bin Abd Al-Warith told us, he said, Sadaqah bin Ibad told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
The king’s cup
, he said: It was made of copper. And his saying: And for whoever brings it, there is
h
a camel’s load
of food, he says: And for whoever brings the measure, there is
h
a camel’s load
of food, as:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever brings it shall have a camel’s load
, meaning:
h
a camel’s load

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
A camel’s load
, he said: A donkey’s load, and it is a language.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said, and Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
A camel’s load
, he said: A donkey’s dream, and it is a language.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said,
m: his statement:
h
A camel’s load
, he said: A donkey’s load. And his saying: And I am a guarantor of it, means: I am a guarantor of giving him a camel load of food if he brings me
h
the king’s measure
. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And I am responsible for it
, he said: I am a guarantor.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his saying:
h
And I am responsible for it
, the leader is the muezzin who said: O caravan.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr and Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: It was conveyed to me on the authority of Mujahid, then he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, on the authority of Warqa’ ibn Iyas, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr:
m: h
And I am responsible for it
, he said, guarantor.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
And I am responsible for it
, meaning I am responsible for it.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And I am responsible for it
, he said: I am a guarantor.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak:
m: h
And I am responsible for it
, he said: a guarantor.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And I am responsible for it
, he said: a guarantor.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: The Messenger said to them: Whoever brings it to us will have a camel load, and I will be responsible for that until I deliver it to him. And from the leader who means the guarantor, the poet said: I do not command peace in it, but I am the leader of myself The root of the word za’im in Arabic is the one who is in charge of the people’s affairs. The same applies to the guarantor and the bearer. That is why it is said: The chief of the people is their leader and their manager. It is said: He claimed leadership and leadership. From this comes the saying of Layla al-Akhiliya: Even if the banner appears, I will see him under the banner on Thursday, a leader.

evidence.text: It was mentioned on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he read it: The king’s measure, without the waw, as if he was directing it to the measure with which food is measured.
It was narrated on the authority of Abu Raja that he read it: The king’s voice.
It was narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Yaʿmar that he read it: Sawg Al-Malik with a ghayn, as if he directed it to the fact that it is a source of their saying: Sagha yasughu Sawghan.
As for what the regions read: the king’s measure, which is the reading that I do not permit reading other than it, due to the consensus of the evidence on it.

x: God Almighty says: Joseph's brothers said: By God, meaning: By God. This taa in Tala God is a waw that was changed to a taa, as was done in the Torah, which is from wariyyat, and the Turath, which is from warath, and the At-Takhmah, which is from Al-Wakhama. The waw in all of these was changed to a taa. The waw in all of these Rahoof are names, but it is not like that in Tala God, because it is a waw of an oath. It was made a taa because of the frequency with which the Arabs used to say By God, so it was made specific in this word by being changed to a taa. Whoever says that in the name of God and says Tala God, does not say Tala Ar-Rahman or Tala Ar-Raheem, nor with any of the names of God, nor with anything that is sworn by, and it is only said in Tala God alone. And his saying:
h
You have certainly known that we did not come to spread corruption on earth
, means: You have certainly known that we did not come to disobey God on your land.
This is what a group of interpreters used to say.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas,
m: regarding his statement: They said, ‘By God, you have certainly known that we did not come to cause corruption on earth,’ he said: We did not come to disobey on earth.

x: What was the knowledge of the one to whom it was said: You know that we did not come to cause corruption on earth, that they did not come for that, so that those who said that considered it permissible to say it?

They considered it permissible to say that because, as mentioned, they returned the merchandise that they found in their bags, so they said: If we were thieves, we would not have returned to you the merchandise that we found in our bags.

It was said: They had known on their way and their journey that they would not wrong anyone, nor would they take what was not theirs, so they said that when it was said to them: You are indeed thieves.
God Almighty said: “They said: ‘Then what is his recompense, if you are liars?’”

God Almighty says: The companions of Joseph said to his brothers: What is the reward for theft if you are lying in your statement: We did not come to cause corruption in the land, nor were we thieves? They said: His recompense is whoever has it found in his baggage, that is his recompense. God Almighty says: The brothers of Joseph said: The reward for theft is whoever has it found in his baggage, that is his recompense. He says: The reward for whoever has it found in his baggage is that he hands over his theft to the one from whom he stole it so that he may enslave him. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers. He says: This is how We deal with whoever is unjust and does what he has no right to do, such as taking someone else's money by stealing. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: So his recompense is his, meaning: he was saved by it, Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers, meaning: thus do We deal with those who steal from us.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said:
m: We were informed about his statement: They said, ‘Then what is his penalty, if you are liars?’ They told Joseph what was ruled in their country, that whoever stole was to take a slave, so they said: His penalty is whoever is found in his saddlebag, that is his penalty.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: “They said, ‘Then what is his punishment, if you are lying? ’ They said, ‘His punishment is that whoever finds it in his saddlebag, that is his punishment. ’ You take it, and it is yours.”

x: The meaning of the statement is: They said: The reward for the theft is what is in his baggage, as if it was said: His reward is the enslavement of what is in his baggage, then enslavement was omitted, since its meaning was known. Then the statement began and it was said: It is his recompense, thus do We recompense the wrongdoers. It may have another meaning: that it means they said: the reward of the theft, in whose saddlebag the theft is found, so the thief is punished, so his first punishment is raised by the predicate sentence after it, and it is raised by the pronoun from its mention in he, and he is the subject of his second punishment. And there is a third possibility: that it is from a reward, and it is raised by the pronoun from his mention in the ha’ in in his saddle, and the first reward is raised by the pronoun from his mention in found, and the answer to the reward is the fa’ in so he is, and the second reward is raised by he is, so the meaning of the statement then is: They said the reward for theft, whoever finds the theft in his saddle, it is his reward, he is enslaved and enslaved.

God Almighty says: So Joseph searched their vessels and their saddlebags, seeking thereby the king’s cup. He began his search with the vessels of his brothers from his father, and he began to search them vessel by vessel before the vessel of his brother from his father and mother, for he delayed his search, then he searched the last of them, his brother’s vessel, and he extracted the cup from his brother’s vessel. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So he began with their vessels before his brother’s vessel

, he mentioned to us that he would not look into a vessel except that he would seek forgiveness from God, out of remorse for what he had accused them of, until his brother remained, and he was the youngest of the people. He said: I do not think that this one took anything! They said: Yes, so he checked it! Behold, they knew where they had put their water-skin, then he took it out from his brother’s vessel.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Then he took it out of his brother’s vessel. He said: Whenever he opened a piece of luggage, he would seek forgiveness, repenting for what he had done, until he reached the boy’s luggage and said: I do not think this one took anything! They said: Yes, so he cleaned it!

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: So he started with their containers before his brother’s container. When the boy’s saddle was left, he said: This boy would not have taken it! They said: By God, he will not leave until you look into his saddlebag. Let us go, and you are content. So he put his hand in and took it out of his saddlebag. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that he said: When the Messenger said to them: And whoever brings him shall have a camel-load, and I shall be responsible for him, they said: We do not know him among us or with us. He said: You will not leave until I search your belongings, and I will excuse myself from demanding them from you! So he began with their containers, one by one, searching them and looking at what was in them, until he passed by his brother’s container and searched it, and took him out of it, then he took him by the neck and went back with him to Joseph. God says:
h
Thus did We plan for Joseph

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: It was mentioned to us that whenever he searched for the belongings of one of them, he would seek forgiveness from his Lord out of guilt, for he knew where what he was looking for was! Until when his brother remained, and he knew that what he was looking for was in him, he said: I do not think this boy will take it, and I do not care if I do not search for his belongings! His brothers said: It is better for you and for us that we also investigate his belongings. So when he opened his belongings, he extracted what he was looking for from them, and God said:
h
Thus did We plan for Joseph
. The Arab scholars differed regarding the letter ha and the letter alif in his saying:
h
Then he extracted it from his brother’s vessel

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is from the masculine form of the word sa’a. He said and made it feminine, and he said: And for whoever brings it there is a camel load, because he meant the sa’a. He said: And the sa’a is masculine, and some of them make the sa’a feminine, and here he meant the water-carrier, and it is feminine. He said: They are two names for one thing, like the garment and the blanket, masculine and feminine for one thing. Some grammarians of Kufa said about his statement:
h
Then he extracted it from his brother’s vessel

, he went to the feminization of: theft. He said: Even if the saa’ is in the meaning of the saa’, then perhaps this feminization is from that. He said: If you wish, you can make it for the feminization of the water-carrying vessel. He said: The saa’ is masculine, and the saa’ is feminine and masculine. So whoever feminizes it says: three saa’s, like three houses, and whoever masculines it says saa’s, like doors.
Surat Yusuf 12:76 So he began with their vessels before his brother's vessel, then he extracted them from his brother's vessel.
h
Thus did We plan for Joseph
. It was not for him to take his brother into the king's religion except that God should will.
h
We raise by degrees whom We will

, and above every possessor of knowledge is one Knowing. Another of them said: The word sa’a was made feminine when it was made feminine because it was intended to mean a drink, and it was made masculine when it was made masculine because it was intended to mean a sa’a. He said: This is like the tray and the table, the spearhead and its two supports, and what is similar to that, of the things in which two names come together, one of which is masculine and the other feminine. And His saying:
h
Thus did We plan for Joseph

, meaning: This is how We did for Joseph, so that he might rescue his brother from his father’s and mother’s brothers, by their acknowledgment that he could take him from them and detain him in his hands, and stand between him and them.

This is because they said, when it was said to them: What is his penalty if you are liars?: The penalty of one who steals the cup, that whoever finds it in his bag is enslaved by it. And this was their ruling in their religion. So God planned for Joseph, as He has described to us, until He took his brother from them, so he became with him by their ruling and God’s action for him. And his saying:
h
It was not for him to take his brother under the king’s law

, unless God willed it, means: Joseph would not have taken his brother under the rule of the king of Egypt, his judgment, and his obedience to them, because it was not from the rule of that king and his judgment that anyone should be enslaved by stealing. So it was not for Joseph to take his brother under the rule of the king of his land, unless God willed it by His plot that He plotted against him, until the one in whose vessel the measure was found, his brothers and companions, submitted to their judgment against him, and their souls were content with submission.
And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan told us, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He would not have taken his brother under the king’s law
, except for an act that God plotted against him, and Joseph resorted to it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told me, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Thus did We plan for Joseph
, God planned it for him, so it was a cause for Joseph.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So that he may take his brother according to the king’s religion, unless God wills, he said: Except for an act that God plotted against him, and Joseph was afflicted with it. He said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement:
h
Thus did We plot against Joseph
, he said: We did.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Thus did We plan for Joseph
, meaning: We did for Joseph.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Thus did We plan for Joseph
, meaning: We did it for Joseph.

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his statement:
h
He would not have taken his brother under the king’s religion
Some of them said: He would not have taken his brother under the king’s authority.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He would not have taken his brother under the king’s religion
, meaning: under the king’s authority.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding his statement:
h
He would not have taken his brother under the king’s religion
, meaning: under the king’s authority.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: in His judgment and ruling.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It was not for him to take his brother under the king’s law except that God willed
, he said: It was not in the king’s judgment that he should enslave a man for theft.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: In the religion of the king, he said: That was not in the religion of the king, he said: His rule.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih Muhammad ibn Laith al-Marwazi told us, on the authority of a man whom he named, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of Abu Mawdud al-Madani, he said:
m: I heard Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi say: “They said, ‘His recompense is that whoever finds it in his baggage, that is his recompense. ’” “
h
Thus did We plan for Joseph

. He would not have seized his brother by virtue of the king’s law.” He said: The king’s law is not used to seize the one who stole at all, but God planned for his brother until they said what they said, so He seized them based on what they said, and not by virtue of the king’s law.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said:
m: It reached him regarding his statement:
h
It was not for him to take his brother under the king’s debt
, he said: The king’s ruling was that whoever stole would be doubled in damages.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: He would not take his brother in the religion of the king, meaning: in the ruling of the king.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: He would not have taken his brother by the king’s religion, meaning: unjustly, but God plotted for Joseph to take his brother to him.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement,
h
It was not for him to seize his brother under the king’s law

, he said: It is not under the king’s law that a thief should be seized for his theft. He said: And the ruling among the prophets, Jacob and his sons, was that a thief should be seized for his theft as a slave who could be enslaved.

x: These sayings, even though the words of those who said them differed in the meaning of the king’s religion, are close in meaning, because whoever takes it under the king’s authority treats it according to his work, so he takes it with his consent and not otherwise, and that is from him a judgment upon him, and his judgment upon him is his judgment. The origin of religion is obedience. I have explained this in other places with evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here.
And his saying: Except that God wills, as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Except if God wills, but we made it up for him, that they said: Then his reward is.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Except that God wills, except for a reason that God plotted against him, so Joseph fell ill with it. And his saying:
h
We raise by degrees whom We will
, there is a difference in the reading of that.

x: Some of them read it:
h
We raise by degrees whom We will

, adding degrees to whom, meaning We raise the statuses of whom We will, raising his statuses and ranks in this world with knowledge over others, just as We raised Joseph’s status in this and his status in this world over the statuses and ranks of his brothers.
Others read it as:
h
We raise by degrees whom We will

, with the nunation of degrees, meaning: We raise whom We will by ranks and degrees in knowledge over others, just as We raised Joseph. So whom in this reading is in the accusative case, and in the first reading it is in the genitive case. We have explained this in Surat Al-An’am. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, his statement,
h
We raise by degrees whom We will
, refers to Joseph and his brothers, who were given knowledge, so We raised Joseph above them in knowledge. And His statement:
h
And above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowledgeable

, God Almighty says: And above every scholar is one more knowledgeable than him, until that ends with God. What He meant by that is that Joseph was the most knowledgeable of his brothers, and that above Joseph is one more knowledgeable than Joseph, until that ends with God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Abu Amir Al-Aqdi told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdul-A’la Al-Tha’labi, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: that he narrated a hadith and a man in his presence said: And above every possessor of knowledge is one who is All-Knowing. Ibn Abbas said: What you said is bad! Indeed, God is All-Knowing, and He is above every scholar.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas was told a hadith, and a man in his presence said: Praise be to God, And above every possessor of knowledge is the All-Knower! Ibn Abbas said: The All-Knower is God, and He is above every scholar.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: We were with Ibn Abbas, and he narrated a hadith, and a man was amazed and said: Praise be to God, Above every possessor of knowledge is the All-Knower! Ibn Abbas said: What you said is bad: God is the All-Knower, and He is above every possessor of knowledge.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Amr bin Muhammad told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowledgeable
, he said: This one is more knowledgeable than that one, and this one is more knowledgeable than that one, and God is above every scholar.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Saeed bin Mansour told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Abdul-A’la, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And above every possessor of knowledge is one who is All-Knowing, he said: God is the All-Knowing, All-Aware, above every scholar. Surat Yusuf 12:76 So he began with their vessels before his brother's vessel, then he extracted them from his brother's vessel.
h
Thus did We plan for Joseph
. It was not for him to take his brother into the king's religion except that God should will.
h
We raise by degrees whom We will
, and above every possessor of knowledge is one Knowing.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ubayd God told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowledgeable
, he said: God is above every scholar.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b, he said:
m: A man asked Ali about a matter, and he said something about it. The man said: It is not like this! Rather it is such and such. Ali said: You were right and wrong, And above every possessor of knowledge is one more All-Knowing.

c: Yaqub and Ibn Wakee’ told me, they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowledgeable
, he said: God’s knowledge is above everyone.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Nadr, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowledgeable
, he said: God Almighty.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Ya’la bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr:
m: h
And above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowledgeable
, he said: God is more knowledgeable than anyone.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ibn Shabrama, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowledgeable
, he said: There is no scholar except that there is another scholar above him, until knowledge ends with God.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Asim told us, he said, Juwairiya told us, on the authority of Bashir Al-Hujaimi, he said:
m: I heard Al-Hasan reciting this verse one day:
h
And above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowledgeable

, then he stopped and said: By God, no scholar has ever spent the evening on the face of the earth except that there is one above him who is more knowledgeable than him, until knowledge returns to the one who taught him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Ali told us, on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of Ibn Shabrama, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowledgeable
, he said: Above every scholar is another more knowledgeable, until knowledge ends with God.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowledgeable
, until knowledge ends with God, from Him it began, and the scholars learned, and to Him it returns. And in Abdullah’s reading: And above every scholar is one more knowledgeable.

x: If someone were to say to us: How was it permissible for Joseph to put the water-drawer in his brother’s saddlebag, then steal from innocent people, and say: O caravan, you are indeed thieves? It was said: His saying: O caravan, you are indeed thieves, is only report from God about a muezzin who called him, not report about Joseph. It is possible that the muezzin called him by that because he had lost the cup and did not know what Joseph had done. It is possible that the muezzin called him by that because of Joseph’s command, and he considered it permissible to order him to call them by that, because he knew that they had stolen in some cases, so he ordered the muezzin to call them by describing them as thieves, and Joseph meant that theft, not that they stole the cup.

Some of the people of interpretation said: That was a mistake on the part of Joseph, so God punished him by the people’s response to him: If he steals, a brother of his stole before, and we have already mentioned the narration about that previously.

evidence.text: And his saying: We raise by degrees whom We will, there is a difference in the reading of that.

Some of them read it: We raise by degrees whom We will, adding degrees to whom, meaning We raise the statuses of whom We will, raising his statuses and ranks in this world with knowledge over others, just as We raised Joseph’s status in this and his status in this world over the statuses and ranks of his brothers.
Others read it as: We raise by degrees whom We will, with the nunation of degrees, meaning: We raise whom We will by ranks and degrees in knowledge over others, just as We raised Joseph.
So whom in this reading is in the accusative case, and in the first reading it is in the genitive case.

x: God Almighty says: “They said:
h
If he steals
, a brother of his stole before,” meaning his brother from his father and mother, who is Joseph, as:

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his statement:
h
If he steals
, a brother of his stole before, is about Yusuf.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If he steals
, a brother of his stole before, he said: He means Joseph.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: A brother of his had stolen before, he said: Yusuf.

x: The interpreters differed about the theft that they described Joseph with.
Some of them said: It was an idol of his maternal grandfather, which he broke and threw on the road.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Amr Al-Basri told us, Al-Fayd bin Al-Fadl told us, Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
If he steals
, a brother of his stole before him. He said: Joseph stole an idol that belonged to his maternal grandfather, broke it and threw it in the road, and his brothers used to criticize him for that.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: A brother of his had stolen before, he mentioned that he had stolen an idol belonging to his maternal grandfather, so they taunted him for that.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If he steals

, a brother of his stole before, they meant by that to criticize the Prophet of God, Joseph. And the theft that they criticized him for was an idol that belonged to his maternal grandfather, so he took it. The Prophet of God only wanted good by that, so they criticized him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If he steals
, a brother of his stole before, he said: Joseph’s mother had ordered Joseph to steal an idol that belonged to his uncle and that he worshipped, and she was a Muslim.

x: Others said about this:

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said,
m: I heard my father say: The sons of Jacob were eating, when Joseph saw a vein and hid it, so they taunted him for that:
h
If he steals
, a brother of his stole before.

x: Others said about this: Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid Abu al-Hajjaj who said: The first affliction that befell Joseph, as far as I have heard, was that his paternal aunt, the daughter of Ishaq, was the eldest son of Ishaq, and she was the one to whom Ishaq’s belt was entrusted. They used to inherit it from their elders, and he was one of her two sisters who was in charge of her. He had a hand in it that was not disputed, and he could do with it as he wished. When Joseph was born to Jacob, his aunt had taken him into her care, so he was with her and to her. No one loved anything as much as she loved him. When he grew up and reached some years, and Jacob’s soul fell for him, he came to her and said: O my sister, hand Joseph over to me, for by God I cannot let him be absent from me for an hour!

She said: By God I will not leave him, by God I cannot let him be absent from me for an hour! He said: By God I will not leave him! She said: Leave him with me for a few days so that I may look at him and calm down, perhaps that will console me about him, or something like that. When Jacob left her, she took Isaac's belt and tied it around Joseph from under his clothes. Then she said: I have lost Isaac's belt, so see who took it and who took it? So she looked. Then she said: Search the people of the house! So they searched them and found it with Joseph. She said: By God, it is mine, and I can do with it as I wish. He said: Jacob came to her and she told him the story. He said to her: You and that, if he did that, then it is yours, I cannot do anything else. So she held him back, but he could not do anything to him until she died. He said: He is the one about whom Joseph's brothers said when he did to his brother what he did when he captured him:
h
If he steals
, a brother of his stole before.
Surat Yusuf 12:77 They said,
h
If he steals
, a brother of his has stolen before. But Joseph kept it secret within himself and did not disclose it to them. He said,
h
You are in a worse position

, and God is most knowing of what you describe. Ibn Hamid said: Ibn Ishaq said: When the sons of Jacob saw what Joseph’s brothers had done and did not suspect that he had stolen, they said - regretfully, because it had entered their hearts, rebuking him -
h
If he steals
, a brother of his stole before. When Joseph heard it, he said:
h
You are in a worse position
, secretly to himself, and did not reveal it to them,
h
and God knows best what you describe
. And his saying: “
h
So Joseph kept it secret within himself and did not reveal it to them
. He said, ‘
h
You are in a worse position

, and God is most knowing of what you describe.’” He means by his saying: So he kept it secret, so he concealed it. He said: So conceal it, so he made it feminine, because he meant by it the word, which is: You are the worst place,
h
and God knows best what you describe

If it had come in the masculine form, it would have been permissible, as it was said: That is from the report of the unseen, That is from the report of the towns. He referred to the word, but it was not mentioned previously. The Arabs often do this if the intended meaning is understood by the listeners of the speech.

i: This is similar to the saying of Hatim al-Ta’i:
x: Amawi, wealth is of no use to a young man if he chokes one day and his chest becomes tight.

He means: And the chest became constricted with the soul, so he used a metaphor for it and did not mention it, since in his saying: When it chokes one day, there was an indication to the listener of his words of what he meant by his saying: And it became constricted with it. And from this is the saying of God: Then indeed, your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted and then strove and were patient - indeed, your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful, so he said: after it, and before that there was no mention of a feminine noun. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So Joseph kept it secret within himself and did not reveal it to them
. As for what he kept secret within himself, it was his saying:
h
You are in a worse position
, and God is most knowing of what you describe.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So Joseph kept it secret within himself and did not reveal it to them
. He said, ‘
h
You are in a worse position
, and God is most knowing of what you describe.’” He said: This is the statement.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And Joseph kept it secret within himself and did not reveal it to them
, meaning: He kept it secret within himself, saying:
h
You are in the worst position
, and God is most knowing of what you describe. And his saying:
h
And God knows best what you describe
, means: And God knows best what you are lying about in what you describe his brother Benjamin with. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You are in the worst position
h
and God knows best what you describe
, they say: Joseph says it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And God knows best what you describe
, meaning: what you deny.

x: The meaning of the statement then is: So Joseph kept it to himself and did not reveal it to them. He said: You are worse in status with God than those whom you described as thieves and more wicked in position, because of your previous actions, and God is acting on your lies, even if many of the people present were ignorant of it. He mentioned that when the cup was found in the bag of Joseph’s brother, the people blamed each other, as: Ibn Wakee' narrated, Amr narrated, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: When the stolen goods were extracted from the boy's saddlebag, their backs were cut off and they said: O sons of Rachel, you will continue to be a scourge upon us! When did you take this cup? Benjamin said: Rather, it is the sons of Rachel who will continue to be a scourge upon you. You took my brother and destroyed him in the wilderness! This cup was placed in my saddlebag, as you put the dirhams in your saddlebags!

They said: Do not mention the dirhams lest they be seized with them! When they entered upon Joseph, he called for the cup, pricked it, then brought it close to his ear and said: This cup tells me that you were twelve men, and that you took a brother of yours and sold him. When Benjamin heard that, he stood up and prostrated himself before Joseph, then said: O king, ask this cup of yours about my brother, is he alive? So he pricked it, then said: He is alive, and you will see him. He said: Do with me as you wish, for if he knows about me, he will rescue me. He said: So Joseph entered and wept, then he performed ablution, then he came out. Then Benjamin said: O king, I want you to strike this cup of yours so that it may tell you the truth. Ask him: Who stole it and put it in my bag? So he struck it, and he said: This cup of mine is angry, and he said: How can you ask me about my companion, when you have seen who I was with?

He said: When the sons of Jacob became angry, they could not be tolerated. Reuben became angry and said: O king, by God, you must leave us alone or I will cry out such a cry that there will not remain a pregnant woman in Egypt except that she will miscarry what is in her womb! And every hair on Reuben's body stood up and came out of his clothes. Then Joseph said to his son: Go to Reuben and touch him. And when one of the sons of Jacob became angry and the other touched him, his anger went away. So the boy passed by him and touched him, and his anger went away. Then Reuben said: Who is this? There is seed of Jacob's seed in this country! Joseph said: Who is Jacob? Then Reuben became angry and said: O king, do not mention Jacob, for he is the beloved of God, the son of the sacrifice of God, the son of the friend of God! Joseph said: Then you, if you are truthful.
