God Almighty says: The brothers of Joseph said to Joseph: O noble one, O king, he has an old father, who is obsessed with loving him, meaning Jacob, so take one of us in his place, meaning: so take one of us instead of Benjamin, and leave him alone, indeed we see you among the doers of good, meaning: we see you among the doers of good in your actions.
Muhammad bin Ishaq said about this:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: We see you among the doers of good, we see that this is goodness from you if you do it.

x: God Almighty says: Joseph said to his brothers: God forbid, I seek refuge in God. The Arabs do the same with every source that is placed in the place of yafʿal and yafʿal, as they put it in the accusative case, like when they say: hamdan li-llah and shukran lahu, meaning: I praise God and thank Him. The Arabs say in this regard: God forbid and God forbid, and they add the feminine ha, just as they say: “How beautiful is the meaning of this statement: God forbid, God forbid, God forbid.” And they say: O God, I seek refuge in You, as if it were said: I seek refuge in You, seeking refuge, or I call upon You, seeking refuge.
“We should not take except from the one with whom we find our property,” he says: I seek refuge in God from taking an innocent person with a sick person, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: “He said, ‘God forbid that we should take anything except from the one with whom we found our property. If we did, we would be wrongdoers.’” He said: If we took anything other than the one with whom we found our property, then we would be doing what we should not do and transgressing against people. Ibn Wakee' narrated, he said, Amr narrated, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi: "They said, 'O Aziz, indeed he has an old father, so take one of us in his place. Indeed, we see you are of the doers of good.' He said, 'God forbid that we should take anyone except the one with whom we found our property. Indeed, in that case we would be wrongdoers.'" Joseph said, "When you come to your father, greet him with our greetings and say to him, 'The King of Egypt is praying that you will not die until you see your son Joseph, so that he may know that there are righteous people like him in the land of Egypt.'"

x: God Almighty means: When they despaired of him, when they despaired of him releasing Joseph from Benjamin, taking one of them in his place, and answering them to what they asked of him.
His saying: They despaired, is derived from: The man despaired of such-and-such, he despairs, like:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: When they despaired of him, they despaired of him, and they saw his severity in his matter. His saying: They are secretly engaged, means that they produce for each other, and no one else mixes with them. And the rescue, the group of productive people, is called by it the individual and the group, as it is said: a just man, and men of justice, and false people, and breakfast. It is a source from the saying of the one who says: I saved so-and-so, I saved him in secret, making it a description and an attribute. And from the evidence that this is as we mentioned, is the saying of God And We brought him near for a secret conversation, so He described the individual with it. And He said in this place:
h
They were saved in secret

, so He described the group with it, and the plural of rescue is rescue, as Labid said: And the angels of awakening witnessed my high heels and the buttocks of kings as witnesses A group of men may be called a whisper, as God Almighty said: And when they whispered, and He said: There is no whispering of three, and they are the people who whisper. And whispering can also be a source, as God said: The whispering is only from Satan, from which you say: I whispered, I whispered, so in this place it is the whispering itself, and from it the poet said: Bani Bada is a secret counselor for men, so be a secret counselor for your secret In this verse, Najwa and Naji have one meaning, which is munajat, and he combined the two languages. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of his saying:
h
They were saved in secret
, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: So when they despaired of him, they conferred privately, and Simeon conferred with them, and he had taken him as a pledge, and they conferred privately among themselves, whispering to each other.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
They were saved in secret
, they were saved alone in secret.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: They were alone in secret, meaning: they were alone with each other, then they said: What do you think? And his saying: Their leader, the scholars differed regarding the meaning of that.

x: Some of them said: He meant their elder in intelligence and knowledge, not in age, and he was Simeon. They said: Reuben was older than him in birth.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
Their eldest said
, he said: He is Simeon who stayed behind, and older than him - or: older than them - in birth, is Reuben.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Their elder said, Simeon who stayed behind, and older than him in birth was Reuben.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Their eldest said
, he said: Simeon who stayed behind, and the eldest of them in birth was Reuben.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant their oldest, who was Robel.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Their elder said, and he was Reuben, the brother of Joseph, and he was his maternal cousin, and he was the one who forbade them from killing him.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Their leader said, he said: Rubil, and he was the one who advised them not to kill him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Their eldest said

, in knowledge, Indeed, your father has taken a covenant from you in the name of God, ‘Before you neglected Joseph, I will never leave the land,’ the verse. So Reuben stayed in Egypt, and the nine came to Jacob and told him the report, so he wept and said, O my sons, you do not go once without diminishing one! You went once and diminished Joseph, and you went a second time and diminished Simeon, and you have gone now and diminished Reuben!

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: So when they despaired of him, they secretly went away. He said: What do you think? Then Reuben said, as he was told to me, and he was the leader of the al-Nas 114:Did you not know that your father took a covenant from you in the name of God that you would bring him back to me unless you were surrounded? And before that, you neglected Joseph, the verse.

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of those who said: Their elder said, he meant Rubil, because they all agreed that he was the eldest of them in age. The Arabs do not understand when they are addressed, when it is said to them: So-and-so is the elder of the people, in an absolute sense without a conjunction, except in one of two meanings: either in leadership and supremacy over them, or in age. As for intellect, if they wanted that, they connected it and said: He is their elder in intellect. But if it is stated in an absolute sense without a conjunction, then nothing is understood except what I mentioned. The commentators said: Even though Simeon had the knowledge and intelligence that God had given him, he did not have leadership and prestige over his brothers. It is known from this that he meant by his saying:
h
Their eldest said
. If this is the case, then there remains only the other aspect, which is old age.
All those we mentioned said: Reuben was the oldest of the people, so the statement we have chosen is correct. And His statement:
h
Did you not know that your father had taken a covenant from you in the name of God

? He says: Did you not know, O people, that your father Jacob had taken from you the covenants and pledges of God: We will bring him to Him all together unless you are surrounded, “and before what you neglected regarding Joseph,” and before this action of yours, your neglect of Joseph. He says: Did you not know before this your neglect of Joseph? And if the interpretation of the speech is diverted to what we have said, then ma would then be in the accusative case. It may be possible that his saying, And before that, you neglected Joseph, is a subject predicate, and his saying,
h
Did you not know that your father had taken a covenant from you in the name of God
? is a finite predicate, so ma would then be in the nominative case, as if it were said: And before this, your neglect of Joseph, so ma would be raised by before.
This may be ma which is a connection in the speech, so the interpretation of the speech would be: And before this, you neglected Joseph.
And his saying: I will not leave the land in which I am, which is Egypt, and I will not leave it, until my father gives me permission to leave it, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: I will not leave the land, which I am in today, until my father gives me permission, to leave it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Shimon said:
m: I will not leave the land
h
until my father gives me permission or God judges for me
, and He is the best of judges. And his saying:
h
Or God decides

, or my Lord decides for me to leave it, and leave my brother Benjamin, otherwise I will not leave, and He is the best of judges, he says: And God is the best of judges, and the most just of those who decide between people. Abu Saleh used to say about this:

c: Al-Husayn bin Yazid Al-Subaie told me, he said, Abd Al-Salam bin Harb told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until my father gives me permission or God judges for me
, he said: By the sword. It is as if Abu Saleh directed the interpretation of his saying:
h
Or God decides
, to:
h
Or God decides
for me to fight the one who prevented me from returning with my brother Benjamin to his father Jacob, so I fight him.

x: God Almighty says, informing about what Reuben said to his brothers, when Joseph took his brother by the measure that he had taken from his vessel: Return, my brothers, to your father Jacob and say to him: O our father, your son Benjamin has stolen. The reading of this letter with the opening of the seen and the ra and the softening: Your son stole.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Your son stole: with a damma on the seen and a shaddah on the ra, in the manner of what the doer is not named, meaning: he stole, and we only testified to what we knew.

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: We did not say that he stole except on the basis of our apparent knowledge that this was the case, because the king’s cup was struck in its container and not in the containers of others.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Return to your father, for I would not return until his order came to me, and say, ‘O our father, your son has stolen, and we only testified to what we knew,’ meaning: The theft was found in his bag, and we were watching, we had no knowledge of the unseen,
h
and we were not guardians of the unseen

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: We did not testify before Joseph that a thief would be caught for his theft, except for what we knew.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: Jacob, peace be upon him, said to them: This man does not know that a thief will be caught for his theft except on the basis of your word! They said: We only testify to what we know, we do not testify that a thief will be caught for his theft except on the basis of what we know. He said: The ruling among the prophets, Jacob and his sons was that a thief would be caught for his theft as a slave and enslaved. And his saying:
h
And we were not guardians of the unseen

, meaning: We did not think that your son would become our affair, but rather we said: And we will guard our brother, from what we had the means to guard him from. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Husayn bin Al-Harith Abu Ammar Al-Marwazi told us, he said, Al-Fadl bin Musa told us, on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Waqid, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
And We were not guardians of the unseen
, he said: We did not know that your son was stealing.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We were not guardians of the unseen
, we did not know that he would steal.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And We were not guardians of the unseen
, we did not know that he would steal.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And We were not guardians of the unseen
, he said: We did not know that he would steal.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid and Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And we were not guardians of the unseen
, he said: We did not think nor did we feel that he would steal.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And We were not guardians of the unseen
, he said: We did not see that he would steal.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And We were not guardians of the unseen
, he said: We did not think that your son would steal.

x: The more correct of the two interpretations in our view regarding his statement: And we testified only to what we knew, is the statement of those who said: And we testified that your son stole only to what we knew from seeing the measure in his container, because it follows his statement: Indeed, your son stole, so it is more likely to be report about their testimony to that than report about something separate. He mentioned that: Al-Ghaib in the Himyarite language means the night itself. Surat Yusuf 12:81 Go back to your father and say, "O our father, indeed your son has stolen. And we only testified to what we knew,
h
and we were not guardians of the unseen

evidence.text: The reading of this letter with the opening of the seen and the ra and the softening: Your son stole.

x: Even if you accuse us, do not believe us in what we say about your son stealing:
h
And ask the town in which we were

, which is Egypt, he says: Ask whoever is in it from its people, and the caravan in which we came, which is the caravan in which we were, from which we came with it, about the report of your son and the truth of what we told you about his theft, for you will tell the truth of that, and indeed we are truthful, in what we told you about his report. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And ask the town in which we were
, which is Egypt.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jarj, Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
And ask the town in which we were
, he said: They mean Egypt.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Reuben knew from his return what he said to his brothers, that they were people who were accused by their father, because of what they had done to Joseph. And their saying to him: Ask the town where we were and the caravan where we came, they knew what we knew and witnessed what we witnessed, if you do not believe us, and indeed, we are truthful.

x: There is something omitted in the speech, which is: So Benjamin's brothers returned to their father and Reuben remained behind, so they told him the story, and when they told him that he had stolen, He said, 'Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something,' meaning: Rather, your souls have made something attractive to you that you intended and desired, so have patience in a most beautiful way, meaning: So my patience over what befell me of the loss of my son, is a most beautiful patience in which there is no impatience or complaint, perhaps God will bring me all of my children and return them to me, He is the All-Knowing, of my loneliness, and of their loss and my grief over them, and the truth of what they say of his lie, the Wise, in His management of His creation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something, so patience is most fitting, he says: it has been made beautiful, and his statement:
h
Perhaps God will bring them all to me
, he says: Joseph and his brother Reuben.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: When they brought that to Jacob, meaning Reuben was telling them, he accused them and thought that it was like what they did to Joseph, then he said: “Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something, so patience is most fitting.
h
Perhaps God will bring them all to me
,” meaning Joseph, his brother, and Reuben.

x: God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
And he turned away from them

, and Jacob turned away from them, and said, ‘Oh, my grief for Joseph,’ meaning: Oh, my sorrow for him. It is said: Regret is the most intense sadness and remorse. It is said: I regretted something, I am very sorry about it. God Almighty says: And the eyes of Jacob turned white from grief, and he was suppressing it. He says: He was suppressing his grief, meaning that he was filled with it, holding it back and not revealing it. Changing the passive participle to the active participle, as in his saying: and those who restrain anger, and we have explained its meaning with its evidence in the past. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said what we said in the interpretation of his saying: And he said, ‘Oh, my grief over Joseph’:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And he turned away from them
, he turned away from them, and his grief was complete and reached its peak when his brother Joseph joined him, and his grief over Joseph was stirred up in him, so he said: Oh, my grief over Joseph!
h
And his eyes turned white from grief
, while he was suppressing it.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And he turned away from them and said
, ‘Oh, my grief over Joseph,’ meaning: Oh, my sorrow over Joseph.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Oh, my grief over Joseph, oh, my sorrow.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Oh, my grief over Joseph, oh, his grief.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Oh, my grief over Joseph, oh, how sad he was.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Oh, my grief over Joseph, oh, my grief.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Aqatada,
m: his saying: Oh, my grief over Joseph, meaning: we grieved him.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Oh, my grief over Joseph, he said: Oh, my sorrow over Joseph.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad bin Hameed Al-Maamari told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: And he said, ‘Oh, my grief over Joseph.’

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Hujaira, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Oh, my grief for Joseph, he said: Oh, my sorrow for Joseph.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Marzuq, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Oh, my sorrow, oh, my grief.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Hisham told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: Oh my sorrow, oh my grief, for Joseph.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Sufyan al-Asfari, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: No one other than this nation was given the right to seek refuge in God. Do you not hear the words of Jacob: Oh, my grief over Joseph?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: something similar.

x: Mention of those who said what we said in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And his eyes turned white from grief
, and he was suppressing it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He is suppressing his grief, he said: suppressing his sorrow.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Surat Yusuf 12:
m: h
And he turned away from them and said

, "Oh, my grief over Joseph!" And his eyes had turned white from grief, and he was suppressing [his grief]. Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: He is suppressing his grief, he said: suppressing his sorrow.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So he is suppressing his grief, he said: sadness.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So he is suppressing means depressed.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Then he is suppressing his grief
, he said: suppressing his grief.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: Then he is Kazeem, he said: Kazeem is the one who is suppressed.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: Kazim, he said: Depressed.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And his eyes turned white from grief
, and he was suppressing it, meaning: His grief resounded in his heart, and he did not speak evil.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then he is suppressing his grief
, he said: suppressing his grief, so he did not say anything wrong.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Al-Hussein bin Al-Hasan told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And his eyes turned white from grief
, and he was suppressing it, he said: He was suppressing his grief, so he only said good things.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Zari’, on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani:
m: So he is filled with grief, he said: distressed.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: He is suppressing anger, he said: from anger.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And his eyes turned white from grief
, and he was suppressing grief, he said: The suppressing grief is the one who does not speak, grief reached him to the point that he did not speak to them.

x: He, the Most High, meant that the sons of Jacob - who had returned to him from Egypt - said to him, when he said: Oh, my grief over Joseph - By God,
h
you will not cease to remember Joseph
. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: She ceased to love him, she ceased to love him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: she ceases to love him, meaning she ceases to love him.

x: This is what Al-Hasan said in his hadith, and it is a mistake. Rather, it is: She is losing her love for him, and she is still remembering Joseph.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: They said, ‘By God, you do not cease to remember Joseph.’ He said: You do not cease to love him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: You cease to love Him, you cease to love Him. He said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: By God,
h
you will not cease to remember Joseph
, he said:
h
You will not cease to remember Joseph

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, they said:
m: By God,
h
you will not cease to remember Joseph
, he said:
h
You will not cease to remember Joseph
. He said: You will not cease to love him.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You will not cease to remember Joseph
, he said:
h
You will not cease to remember Joseph

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
You will not cease to remember Joseph
, he said:
h
You will not cease to remember Joseph

. It is said: I have not ceased to say that, and I have not ceased in language, afta’ and afta’a fata’ and fatu’an. It was also narrated: I have not ceased to say it, and from it is the saying of Aws bin Hajar: It did not stop until its dust was like a canopy on a windy day. And his other saying: And the horses kept returning and claiming, and some of them followed and cut off Meaning: It still does not stop. And the letter la was deleted from his saying: tafta’a and it is intended in the speech, because if what follows an oath is a piece of report, it is not accompanied by denial, and the lam with which oaths are answered is not dropped, and that is like the saying of the speaker: By God, I will come to you. And if what follows it is denied, it is met with ma or la. So when its location was known, it was deleted from the speech, so that the listener would know the meaning of the speech, and from that is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: I said, By God, I will not leave even if they cut off my head and limbs. So I deleted la from his saying: I will stop sitting for the reason I mentioned, as the other said: No, by my father, Dahmaa will not remain dear to her people as long as the flint is ignited. He wants: Still. And his saying:
h
Until you become a coward

, means: until you become weak in body and insane in mind. The origin of the word haradh is corruption of the body and mind due to sadness or love. From this comes the saying of Al-Arji: I am a man who has love in him, so he urged me on until I became weak and sick. He means by his saying: He incited me, he melted me and left me incited. It is said from it: a man who incited, a woman who incited, people who incited, and two men who incited, in the same form for the masculine and feminine, and in the dual and plural. Some Arabs say for the male haridh and for the female haridhah. So if it is described with this word, it is dual and plural, and masculine and feminine. Haridh is singular in all cases and the femininity does not enter into it, because it is a source. So if it is made to an agent based on the assumption of nouns, then what is required of nouns from dual, plural, masculine and feminine is required of it.

x: Some of them mentioned hearing: A man who is inciting, if he is in pain, and he recited a verse about that: The horses asked for him for a whole day, and if he had trained him, he would have become an instigator. He mentioned that it includes the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: I see the man with the horses becoming an instigator like the instigation of a sick young camel in the country And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
Until you are exhausted
, meaning the effort of illness, worn out.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Until you become a hotbed, he said: Before death.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Until you become a heathen, he said: Heathen is what is before death.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told me, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Until it becomes dry, until it wears out or becomes old.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Until you become old, he said: old.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Until you become old. He said: Old. He said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said: Al-Haradh is an old thing.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: until it becomes rotten, he said: The rotten thing is the worn-out, perishable thing. He said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abu Muadh, on the authority of Ubaid bin Sulayman, on the authority of al-Dahhak: Until it becomes worn out, worn out means worn out. Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj said, I heard Abu Muadh say, Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said regarding His statement, until it becomes rotten, it means worn out and gone.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Until it becomes worn out, meaning worn out.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: When Jacob mentioned Joseph, they said - meaning his sons who were present at that time, out of ignorance and injustice - By God, you will not cease to mention Joseph until you become ill, meaning: you will become corrupt and have no mind,
h
or you will be among those who perish

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until you become infirm or are among those who perish
, he said: Infirm is the one who has been returned to the worst of age until he is no longer sane, or is perishing, so he is perishing before that. And his saying:
h
Or you will be among those who perish
, means:
h
Or you will be among those who perish
by death. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Or you will be among those who perish
, he said: Death.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: or you will be among the lost, among the dead.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: or you will be among the lost, he said: the dead.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Or you are among those who perish, he said: Or you die.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Or you will be among the lost, he said: among the dead.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Or Surat Yusuf 12:85 They said, "By God, you will not cease to mention Joseph until you become ill or are among those who perish." you will be among the lost, he said: the dead.

x: God Almighty says: Jacob said to those of his sons who said to him: By God, you will not cease to remember Joseph until you become ill or are among those who perish. I do not complain to you about my sorrow and grief, but I complain about that to God. What he means by his saying:
h
I only complain of my distress
, is that I only complain of my worries and sadness to God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
I only complain of my distress
, Ibn Abbas said: My distress means my concern.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Jacob said, with knowledge of God: I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God,
h
and I know from God that which you do not know
, when he saw their rudeness, harshness, and bad words towards him: I did not complain of that to you,
h
and I know from God that which you do not know

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God, he said: My need and my grief to God.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Hudha bin Khalifa told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: the same. It was said: Bath is the most severe form of sadness, and in my opinion it is from Bath al-Hadith, but what is meant by it is: I only complain about my situation that I am in of worry, and I broadcast my talk and sadness to God.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: I only complain of my sorrow, he said: My grief.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya bin Saeed told me, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
I only complain of my distress
and my grief, he said: My need. As for his saying:
h
And I know from God what you do not know
, Ibn Abbas used to say about that, according to what was reported from him, what:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And I know from God that which you do not know
, he said: I know that Joseph’s vision is true, and that I will prostrate to him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God,
h
and I know from God that which you do not know

. He said: When they told him about the king’s supplication, Jacob’s soul felt a sense of loss and he said: There is no friend on earth except a prophet! So he was hopeful and said: Perhaps it is Joseph.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God, the verse. He mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, Jacob, was never afflicted with a calamity except that his good opinion of God came back to him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Isa bin Yazid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: It was said: How much did Jacob grieve over his son? He said: He grieved seventy bereaved women! He said: What was his reward? He said: The reward of a hundred martyrs. He said: He never had a bad opinion of God for an hour of the night or day.

c: Ibn Hamid told us
m: another time. He said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Muadh, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the same. Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, on the authority of Al-Mubarak bin Mujahid, on the authority of a man from Al-Azd, on the authority of Talhah bin Masraf Al-Ayami, who said: There are three things that you should not mention and avoid mentioning them: Do not complain about your illness, do not complain about your affliction, and do not praise yourself. He said: And I was informed that Jacob bin Ishaq had a neighbor who came to him and said to him: O Jacob, why do I see you so broken and wasted, and you have not reached the age that your father reached? He said: What God has afflicted me with of worrying about Joseph and mentioning him has broken me and wasted me! So God revealed to him: O Jacob, do you complain about me to My creation? He said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive me! He said: Then I have forgiven you. And after that, whenever he was asked, he would say: I only complain of my sorrow and grief to God,
h
and I know from God that which you do not know
. Surat Yusuf 12:86 He said, "I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God,
h
and I know from God that which you do not know

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Muammil bin Ismail told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, who said:
m: It has reached me that Jacob grew old until his eyebrows fell over his cheeks, and he used to raise them with a rag. A man said to him: What has brought you to what I see? He said: The length of time and the abundance of sorrows! So God revealed to him: O Jacob, do you complain about Me? He said: A sin, so forgive it.

c: Amr ibn Ali told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Laith ibn Abi Salim, who said:
m: Gabriel entered the prison upon Joseph, and recognized him. He said: O king, handsome in face, pleasant in scent, and generous to his Lord, will you not tell me about Jacob? Is he alive? He said: Yes. He said: O king, handsome in face, pleasant in scent, and generous to his Lord, what is the extent of his grief? He said: The grief of seventy bereaved women. He said: O king, handsome in face, pleasant in scent, and generous to his Lord, is there any reward for that? He said: The reward of a hundred martyrs. Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Layth ibn Abi Salim, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: I was told that Gabriel came to Joseph, peace be upon them, while he was in Egypt, in the form of a man. When Joseph saw him, he recognized him, so he went to him and said: O king, whose fragrance is pleasant, whose clothing is pure, and whose adornment is honorable towards his Lord, do you have any knowledge of Jacob? He said: Yes! He said: O king, whose clothing is pure, and whose adornment is honorable towards his Lord, how is he? He said: He has lost his sight. He said: O king, whose clothing is pure, and whose adornment is honorable towards his Lord, what has taken his sight? He said: Grief over you. He said: O king, whose fragrance is pleasant, whose clothing is pure, and whose adornment is honorable towards his Lord, what was he given for that? He said: The reward of seventy martyrs.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abu Shuraih said:
m: I heard someone narrate that Joseph asked Gabriel: How much did Jacob grieve? He said: The grief of seventy bereaved women. He said: What was his reward? He said: The reward of seventy martyrs. He said, Ibn Wahb told us, Nafi’ ibn Yazid told me, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abi Ja’far, who said: Gabriel entered upon Joseph in the well or in the prison, and Joseph said to him: O Gabriel, how great is my father’s grief? He said: The grief of seventy bereaved women. He said: What is his reward from God? He said: The reward of a hundred martyrs.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq told us, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, Abdul Samad bin Maqal told me,
m: I heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: Gabriel came to Joseph with the good report while he was in prison. He said: Do you recognize me, O truthful one? He said: I see a pure form and a good soul that does not resemble the souls of sinners. He said: I am the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds, and I am the trustworthy spirit. He said: What brought you into the entrance of the sinners, while you are the best of the good, the head of those brought near, and the trustworthy one of the Lord of the Worlds? He said: Did you not know, O Joseph, that God purifies the houses through the purity of the prophets, and that the land they enter is the purest of lands, and that God has purified the prison and what is around it through you, O most pure of the pure and son of the purified? It is only purified through the virtue of your purity and the purity of your righteous and sincere fathers! He said: How can I be called the truthful, and you count me among the sincere, while I have been brought into the entrance of the sinners, and named among the misguided and corrupt? He said: Your heart was not tempted, and you did not obey your mistress in disobeying your Lord, and for that reason God named you among the truthful, and counted you among the sincere, and joined you with your righteous fathers. He said: Do you have knowledge of Jacob, O faithful spirit? He said: Yes, God granted him beautiful patience, and tested him with grief over you, and he was suppressing it. He said: What is the extent of his grief? He said: The grief of seventy bereaved women. He said: What is his reward, O Gabriel? He said: The amount of a hundred martyrs. Ibn Humayd narrated that Jarir narrated on the authority of Layth on the authority of Thabit al-Bunani who said: Gabriel entered upon Joseph in prison and Joseph recognized him. He said: So he came to him and greeted him and said: O king of good fragrance, pure clothing, and generous to his Lord, do you have any knowledge of Jacob? He said: Yes. He said: O king of good fragrance, pure clothing, and generous to his Lord, do you know what he did? He said: His eyes turned white. He said: O king of good fragrance, pure clothing, and generous to his Lord, what is that? He said: From grief over you. He said: O king of good fragrance, pure clothing, and generous to his Lord, what is the extent of his grief? He said: The grief of seventy bereaved women! He said: O king of good fragrance, pure clothing, and generous to his Lord, does he have any reward for that? He said: Yes, the reward of a hundred martyrs. Ibn Wakee' narrated, Amr narrated, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: Gabriel came to Joseph while he was in prison and greeted him. He came to him in the form of a man with a handsome face, a pleasant scent, and fine clothes. Joseph said to him: O king with a handsome face, honorable in the sight of his Lord, and a pleasant scent, tell me how Jacob is? He said: He is deeply grieved over you. He said: How much of his grief? He said: The grief of seventy bereaved women. He said: How much of his reward? He said: The reward of seventy or a hundred martyrs. Joseph said: Then to whom will he turn after me? He said: To your brother Benjamin. He said: Will I ever meet him? He said: Yes. So Joseph wept when he met his father after him, then he said: I do not care what I encounter, for God has shown it to me. He said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Zaid, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Gabriel came to Joseph while he was in prison and greeted him. Joseph said to him: O king, generous to his Lord, pleasant in scent, and pure in clothing, do you know about Jacob? He said: Yes, how intense his grief is! He said: O king, generous to his Lord, pleasant in scent, and pure in clothing, what is his reward? He said: The reward of seventy martyrs. He said: Do you think I will meet him? He said: Yes. Joseph was pleased.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: When Jacob entered upon the king and his eyebrows had fallen over his eyes, the king said: What is this? He said: Years and sorrows, or: worries and sorrows. Then his Lord said: O Jacob, why do you complain about Me to My creation? Have I not done to you and done?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Ziyad, on the authority of Muslim bin Yasar,
m: tracing it back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He who is sad will not be patient. Then he recited: I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God.

c: Amr bin Abdul Hamid Al-Amili told me, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: From the time Joseph left Jacob until the day he returned, there were eighty years, and sadness did not leave his heart. He cried until he lost his sight. Al-Hasan said: By God, there was no creature on the earth that day more honorable to God than Jacob, peace be upon him.

x: God Almighty says, when Jacob desired Joseph, he said to his sons: O my sons, go, to the place from which you came and left your two brothers there, and find out about Joseph, meaning: seek out Joseph and find out about his story. The origin of the word taḥsās is the verb taḥsās from ḥ “And his brother, meaning Benjamin,
h
and do not despair of relief from God

, meaning: Do not despair that God will relieve us of the grief we are in over Joseph and his brother with relief from Him. So He will show them, Indeed, no one despairs of relief from God, meaning: no one despairs of His relief and mercy, and loses hope in Him, except the disbelieving people, meaning: the people who deny His ability to create whatever He wills. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: O my sons, go and inquire about Joseph and his brother, in Egypt,
h
and do not despair of relief from God
, he said: From God’s relief that Joseph is returned.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not despair of the mercy of God
, meaning: of the mercy of God.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Then Jacob said to his sons, while he had good expectations of his Lord, despite the sadness he was in: O my sons, go to the country from which you came, and inquire about Joseph and his brother
h
and do not despair of relief from God
, meaning of His relief, Indeed, no one despairs of relief from God except the disbelieving people.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And do not despair of the mercy of God
, he said: of the mercy of God.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not despair of relief from God
, he said: From God’s relief, He will relieve you of the distress you are in.

x: There is something omitted in the speech, and mentioning what is apparent is sufficient for what was omitted, and that is: So they went out, returning to Egypt until they reached it and entered upon Joseph, And when they entered upon him, they said, O noble one, distress has afflicted us and our family, meaning the severity of drought and famine, and we have brought a poor merchandise, as:

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: They went out to Egypt and returned to it, with a small amount of merchandise, meaning, it was not enough to reach what they used to trade for, unless they were given more than they could afford. They had seen what had happened to their father, and the successive calamities that had befallen him in his children and his eyesight, until they came to Joseph. When they entered upon him, they said, O Exalted One, hoping that he would have mercy on them regarding their brother, distress has touched us and our family. What he meant by his saying:
h
And we brought mixed merchandise is dirhams

, or a price that is not permissible in the price of food except for someone who exceeds it. The origin of izjaa is the market by pushing, as Al-Nabigha Al-Dhubyani said: The wind blew from the direction of Dhi Arl, driving the night away from its shores. It means: you shop and pay, and from it the saying of A’sha Bani Tha’laba: The giver of the hundred camels and her slave Awdha, who gives birth to her children Hatem said: Let him weep for the guest of the cannon, and for the widow who is driven away by the night, another widow. It means that she drives it in her hands despite its weakness and inability to walk. Therefore, it was said: With a weak commodity, because it is not a commodity, but rather it is permissible to permit it based on the situation of those who take it.

x: The interpreters differed in explaining the interpretation of this, even though the meanings of their explanation were close.
Mentioning the sayings of the people of interpretation on this:

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: With a defective merchandise, he said: Poor, counterfeit merchandise, it is not spent until some of it is put away.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad Al-Anqazi told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And we came with a defective merchandise, he said: The defective merchandise, which is not spent until some of it is put away.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And we brought a mixed merchandise
, he said: mixed, the deception, the rope, and the thing.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malikah, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas, and he was asked about his statement: And we came with a merchandise that was torn, he said: The tattered goods, the rope, the tether, and the thing.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malikah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And we brought mixed merchandise
, he said: The merchandise is dirhams, and mixed merchandise is worthless.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: It is unsold and of no use.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, he said, Abu Hasin told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah,
m: And we came with defective merchandise, Saeed said: incomplete, and Ikrimah said: poor dirhams.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: and Ikrimah, the same.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: and Ikrimah: And we came with defective merchandise. One of them said: incomplete, and the other said: poor. And he said: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, who said: He was fat and woolly.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Ali bin Asim told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, he said:
m: A man asked Abdullah bin Al-Harith, while I was with him, about his saying:
h
And we brought mixed merchandise
, he said: Little, the goods of the Bedouins, wool and butter.

c: Ishaq bin Ziyad Al-Qattan Abu Yaqub Al-Basri told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Balkhi told us, he said, Marwan bin Muawiyah Al-Fazari told us, on the authority of Marwan bin Amr Al-Azdi, on the authority of Abu Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And we brought a mixed merchandise
, he said: pine nuts and green seeds.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Yazid bin Al-Walid, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And we brought a mixed merchandise
, he said, little. Do you not hear his statement: So he loaded our camels, and they read like that.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he said:
m: Except for a few, because they are in the Mushaf of Abdullah:
h
And our camels were loaded
, meaning his saying: Mizja’ah.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-Qa’qa’ bin Yazid, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Few. Didn’t you hear his saying:
h
And our camels were loaded

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: and al-Hasan: a cheap commodity. Saeed said: the bad, and al-Hasan said: the little.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Idris told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, he said:
m: The goods of the Bedouins are butter and wool.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Atiyah, he said:
m: Dirhams are not worth anything.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Mizja’ah, he said: Little.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Mizja’ah, he said: Little.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. He said, Qubaysah bin Uqbah told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith: And we came with mixed merchandise, he said: Something of wool, and something of ghee. He said, Amr bin Awn told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: Few.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Mizja’ah, he said: Little.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. He said, Al-Hussein told us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Incomplete. Saeed bin Jubair said: So ask. He said, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: And we came with defective merchandise, he said: poor.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: It is unsold and not spent.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: Unsold.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abda told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, Ad-Dahhak said:
m: It is unsold, of no use.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: with a defective commodity, meaning: unsold and useless.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: And we came with defective merchandise, he said: incomplete, and Ikrimah said: there is an exaggeration in it. He said, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The bad dirhams that are not permissible except with a decrease. Surat Yusuf 12:88 So when they entered upon him, they said, "O Exalted One, distress has seized us and our family, and we have brought mixed merchandise,
h
so give us full measure and be charitable to us

. Indeed, God rewards the charitable." He said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The despicable dirhams, which are not permissible except with a decrease.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Dirhams are permissible.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: And we came with a small merchandise, meaning: a small amount.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And we brought mixed merchandise
, he said: Mixed merchandise is little.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And we came with a small amount of merchandise, meaning: it was small and did not amount to what we used to buy from you, unless you exceeded us in it. And his saying: “
h
Then give us full measure
... with it, and give us with it what you used to give us before at a good price and in full, permissible dirhams that are not returned,” as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
Then give us full measure
, meaning: Give us what you used to give us before, for our merchandise is in short supply.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Then give us full measure
, he said: Just as you used to give us good dirhams. And His statement:
h
And be charitable to us

, the Almighty says: They said: And be generous to us with something between the price of good and bad horses, so do not reduce the price of your food for the bad price of our merchandise. Indeed, God rewards the charitable, meaning: God rewards those who are generous to those in need with their money. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And he gave us charity, he said: He gave us between good and bad.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
So give us full measure and be charitable to us

, do not reduce the price for us because of the return of our dirhams. They differed about charity. Was it permissible for the prophets before our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, or was it forbidden?

x: Some of them said: It was not permissible for any of the prophets, peace be upon them.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: No prophet ever asked for charity, but they said: We have come with mixed merchandise, so give us full measure
h
and give us charity
, do not reduce the price.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah
m: that: Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Qasim told us, he said, it is narrated on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah that he was asked: Was charity forbidden to any of the prophets before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Did you not hear his saying: “
h
So give us full measure and be charitable to us

. Indeed, God rewards the charitable”? Al-Harith said: Al-Qasim said: Ibn Uyaynah believes that they did not say that unless charity was permissible for them, and they were prophets, for charity was only forbidden to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to them.

x: Others said: What he meant by his saying:
h
And be charitable to us is that he be charitable to us by returning our brother to us
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And give us charity
, he said: Return our brother to us.

x: This statement that we have mentioned on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, even if it is a statement that has merit, is not the preferred statement in interpreting his statement:
h
And give us charity

, because charity in the common usage of the Arabs is only giving a man in need some of his possessions seeking reward from God for it, even though every good deed is charity. So directing the interpretation of God’s words to the most common meaning in the words of the one in whose tongue the Qur’an was revealed is more appropriate and more appropriate. Mujahid said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Qasim told us, he said, Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Aswad, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid when he was asked: Is it disliked for a man to say in his supplication: O God, give me charity? He said: Yes, charity is only for those who seek reward.

x: It was mentioned that when Joseph, peace be upon him, was told by his brothers: “O noble one, hardship has touched us and our family, and we have brought poor merchandise, so give us full measure and be charitable to us.
Indeed, God rewards the charitable,” he was overcome by tenderness, and he revealed to them what he had been concealing from them about his affair, such as:

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: It was mentioned to me that when they spoke to him with these words, he was overcome by his soul, so his tears streamed down his cheeks as he wept. Then he revealed to them what he had concealed from them, and said: Do you know what you did to Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant? He did not mean by mentioning his brother what he had done to him when he took him, but to differentiate between him and his brother, since they did to Joseph what they did.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: So when they entered upon him, they said, ‘O Exalted One, distress has afflicted us and our family,’ the verse. He said: So he took pity on them at that time, and said to them: Do you know what you did with Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?

x: The interpretation of the statement is: Do you remember what you did to Joseph and his brother, when you separated them, and did what you did while you were ignorant? Meaning: In your state of ignorance of the consequences of what you were doing to Joseph, and what his affair and your affair would lead to.

God Almighty says: When Joseph said that to them, Joseph's brothers said to him: Are you really Joseph? He said: Yes, I am Joseph. "And this is my brother. God has conferred favor upon us," by bringing us together after you had separated us. Indeed, he who fears God and is patient, meaning: he who fears God and watches Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins, and is patient, meaning: and restrains himself and restrains himself from what God has forbidden him to say or do when a calamity befalls him from God, for indeed, God does not allow the reward of those who do good to be lost, meaning: God does not invalidate the reward of his goodness and the recompense of his obedience to Him in what He has commanded and forbidden. There is a difference in the reading of his saying:
h
Are you indeed Joseph
? The majority of the people in the countries read it as: Aa’naka You are you, as a question.
He mentioned that this is in the reading of Abi bin Kaab: Or are you Joseph?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Muhaisin
m: that he read: Indeed, you are Joseph, as a statement, not as a question.

x: The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is the reading of those who read it with a question, due to the consensus of the evidence from the reciters on it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: When he said that to them, meaning his saying:
h
Do you know what you did with Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant
, he removed the cover and they recognized him and said:
h
Are you indeed Joseph
? The verse.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us,
m: he told me who heard Abdullah bin Idris mention, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, his saying: Indeed, whoever fears God and is patient, he said: whoever fears disobeying God and is patient in prison.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: Are you indeed Joseph?
The majority of the people in the countries read it as: Aa’naka You are you, as a question.
He mentioned that this is in the reading of Abi bin Kaab: Or are you Joseph?
Abu Jaafar said: The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is the reading of those who read it with a question, due to the consensus of the evidence from the reciters on it.

x: God Almighty says: Joseph’s brothers said to him: By God, God has favored you over us, and has given you preference in knowledge, patience, and virtue, and indeed we were sinners, meaning: We were not in what we did to you, in separating you from your father and your brother, and other things we did to you, except sinful, except sinful, meaning: mistaken. It is said: So-and-so made a mistake, he made a mistake, he made a mistake, he made mistakes, and from that is the saying of Umayyah ibn al-Askar: And the immigrants we have covered for him, by God, have made mistakes and have favored others. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: When Joseph said to them: I am Joseph and this is my brother, they apologized to him and said: By God, God has favored you over us, and we were indeed wrong, in what we did to you.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: By God, God has preferred you over us, and that was after He made themselves known to them. He said: May God make you a forbearing man.

x: God Almighty says: Joseph said to his brothers: No reproach, meaning: There is no change upon you, nor will there be any corruption of the sanctity and brotherhood between me and you, but you have my pardon and forgiveness. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There is no blame upon you
, he said, There is no blame upon them for their actions.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us,
m: his saying:
h
There is no reproach upon you today
, he said: Sufyan said: There is no reproach upon you.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: h
There is no blame upon you
today, meaning:
h
There is no blame upon you
today in my view for what you did.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: They apologized to Joseph, and he said:
h
There is no blame upon you
today, meaning: I will not mention your sin to you. And his saying:
h
God will forgive you

, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful, this is a supplication from Joseph for his brothers, that God forgives them their sins for what they committed and committed of injustice. He says: God has pardoned you for your sin and injustice, and covered it up for you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful, meaning: God is the Most Merciful of the merciful for whoever repents from his sin and returns to His obedience by repenting from his disobedience, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: God forgives you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful, when they confessed their sin.

x: It was mentioned that when Joseph, peace be upon him, introduced himself to his brothers, he asked them about their father and they said: His sight has been taken away by grief! Then he gave them his shirt and said to them: Go with this shirt of mine.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Joseph said to them: What did my father do after I left? They said: When my uncle Benjamin passed away from grief. He said: “Take this shirt of mine and throw it over my father’s face, and he will regain his sight. Then bring me all your family.” And his saying:
h
He will come seeing
, meaning: He will be considered seeing. And bring me your entire family, meaning: And bring me all of your family.

x: God Almighty says: And when the caravan of the sons of Jacob departed from Joseph, heading to Jacob, their father Jacob said: Indeed, I smell the fragrance of Joseph. It was mentioned that the wind asked permission from its Lord to bring Jacob the fragrance of Joseph before the bearer of good report came to him, so He gave it permission, and it brought it to him.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abu Shuraih told me, on the authority of Abu Ayoub al-Hawzani,
m: he told him: The wind asked permission to bring Jacob the scent of Joseph when he sent the shirt to his father before the bearer of good report came to him, so it did. Jacob said: Indeed, I smell the scent of Joseph, unless you think it is false.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when the caravan departed

, their father said, ‘Indeed, I sense the fragrance of Joseph, unless you think it is false.’ He said: A wind blew and brought the fragrance of Joseph from a distance of eight nights, so he said: Indeed, I sense the fragrance of Joseph, unless you think it is false.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And when the caravan departed
, he said: A wind blew and brought the scent of Joseph’s shirt from a distance of eight nights.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Dhirar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Hudhayl, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas say: Jacob smelled the scent of Joseph while he was eight nights’ journey away from him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, they said: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Hudhayl, he said:
m: I was next to Ibn Abbas and he was asked: How far did Jacob smell the scent of his shirt? He said: From a distance of seven or eight nights. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Jarir narrated, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Hudhayl, he said: My companions said to me: You go to Ibn Abbas, so ask him for us. He said: I said: I will not ask him about anything, but I will sit behind the throne, and the people of Kufa will come to him and ask about their needs and my needs, and I heard him say: Jacob smelled the scent of Joseph’s shirt from a distance of eight nights. Ibn Abi Al-Hudhayl said: I said: That is like the location of Basra in Kufa.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Ali bin Asim told us, on the authority of Dhirar bin Murrah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Al-Hudhayl, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas say: Jacob smelled the scent of Joseph’s shirt from a distance of eight nights. He said: I said to myself: This is like the location of Basra in Kufa. Abu Kuraib narrated, he said: Wakee’ narrated, and Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: My father narrated, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Indeed, I smell the fragrance of Joseph, he said: He smelled the fragrance of Joseph’s shirt from a distance of eight nights. He said: I said to him: That is like the distance between Basra and Kufa. And the wording is from the hadith of Abu Kuraib.

c: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad told us, he said, Asim and Ali told us, they said, Shuʿbah told us, he said, Abu Sinan told me, he said,
m: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse: Indeed, I sense the fragrance of Joseph, he said: He sensed his fragrance from a distance between Basra and Kufa.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam Al-Asqalani told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, he said, Abu Sinan told us.
m: He said: I heard Abdullah bin Abi Al-Hudhayl narrating, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. He said, Abu Naim told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Al-Hudhayl. He said: We were with Ibn Abbas and he said: I smell the scent of Joseph. He said: He smelled the scent of his shirt from a distance of eight nights.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi al-Hudhayl, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas say:
h
And when the caravan departed

, he said: When the caravan set out, a wind blew and brought Jacob the scent of Joseph’s shirt, so he said: Indeed, I smell the scent of Joseph, unless you think it false, he said: So he smelled his scent from a distance of eight nights.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: It was mentioned to us that there were eighty farsakhs between them on that day, Joseph in Surat Yusuf 12:94
h
And when the caravan departed
, their father said, "Indeed, I sense the fragrance of Joseph, unless you do not think me to be mistaken." the land of Egypt, and Jacob in the land of Canaan, and a long time had passed since that.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
