m: regarding his statement: Indeed, I smell the scent of Joseph, he said: It has reached us that there was a distance of eighty farsakhs between them on that day. And he said: Indeed, I smell the scent of Joseph, and he had been separated from him for seventy-seven years before that.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, I smell the scent of Joseph, he said: He smelled the scent of the shirt from a distance of eight days. He said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
And when the caravan departed

, he said: When the caravan departed, a wind blew and carried the scent of Joseph’s shirt to Jacob, and he said: Indeed, I smell the scent of Joseph, he said: And he smelled the scent of his shirt from a distance of eight days.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: When the caravan departed from Egypt, Jacob smelled the scent of Joseph, so he said to those of his children who were with him: I smell the scent of Joseph, if only you would not deny it. As for his saying: If you were not to refute, he means: If you were not to scold me, to make me helpless, to blame me, and to call me a liar. And from it the poet said: My friend, stop blaming and refuting me, for what has passed of my affair will not be returned. It is said: Time ruined someone, meaning it corrupted him. From this is the saying of Ibn Muqbil: Let time do what it wants, for if it is tasked with destroying people, it will destroy them.

x: The interpreters differed about its meaning.
Some of them said: It means: If you did not make me foolish.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: If only you would not be fooled, he said: you would be foolish.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same. And he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
If only you would not be refuted
, he said: you would be foolish.

c: Al-Muthanna and Ali bin Dawud told me, they said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
Had you not been refuted
, he said: you would be ignorant.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Had it not been that you would be refuted
, he said: Had it not been that you would be foolish.

c: Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us,
m: they both said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: Had it not been that you would refute, he said: Had it not been that you would be foolish.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas - and Salim, on the authority of Saeed -
h
If only you would not refute
m: one of them said: You are foolish, and the other said: You are lying.
b.via: Saeed - If only you would not refute

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ata’:
m: h
If only you would not be refuted
, he said: If only you would not lie, if only you would be foolish.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: You are foolish.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
If only you would not be refuted
, he said: If only you would not be foolish.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Had it not been that you would be refuted
, he said: Had it not been that you would be foolish.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi al-Hudhayl, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas say:
h
If only you would not be refuted
, he said: you would be foolish.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Had it not been that you would be refuted
, he said: His mind was gone.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: You refute, he said: His mind has gone.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Had it not been that you would be refuted
, he said: His mind had gone.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
If only you would not be refuted
, he said: If only you would not say: Your mind is gone.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: If you did not refute me, he said: If you did not weaken me.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Had it not been that you would be refuted
, he said: The one who has no mind, that is the one who is executed. He says: He does not have a mind.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: If you were not lying.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Suwaid bin Amr Al-Kalbi told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed:
m: If you were not to be refuted, he said: You would lie. He said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: If it were not for the fact that you would grow old and lie. He said, Muhammad bin Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:

c: It was reported to me on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: You are lying. He said, Abda and Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: If you were not lying.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
If only you would not be refuted
, that you would lie.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abdul-Malik, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If only you would not refute
, he said: You would be foolish, or you would lie.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Had you not been refuted
, he said: you would lie.

x: Others said: It means: you grow old.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
If only you would not be refuted
, he said: If only you would not become old.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaid God told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan.
m: He said: You grow old.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abu Al-Ashhab told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
If only you would not be refuted
, he said: you would become old.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ashhab,
m: and others, on the authority of Al-Hasan, similarly.

x: We have explained that the root of refutation is corruption. Since that is the case, weakness, old age, lying, loss of reason, and all meanings of corruption are included in refutation, because the root of all of that is corruption. Corruption in the body is old age, loss of reason, and weakness, and in action is lying and false blame.
Oh, you who criticize me, blame has come and gone. Love has been long and you have prolonged the refutation.
Meaning: blame. It has become clear, since the matter was as we described, that the statements made by those we mentioned regarding His statement:
h
Had it not been that you would be refuted

, despite the differences in their expressions regarding its interpretation, are close in meaning, and all of them are possible according to the apparent meaning of the revelation, since there was no evidence in the verse that some of that was meant by it and not some of it.

God Almighty says: Those to whom Jacob spoke from his sons said: Indeed, I smell the fragrance of Joseph, unless you deny it. By God, O man, you are in your old mistake and error because of your love for Joseph and your remembrance of him. You do not forget him nor are you comforted by him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, you are in your old error, meaning: your old mistake.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They said, ‘By God, you are indeed in your old error,’ meaning: from the love of Joseph, you will not forget him or console yourself with him. They said harsh words to their father, which they should not have said to their father, nor to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: They said, ‘By God, you are indeed in your old error.’ He said: Concerning the matter of Joseph.

c: Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan said:
m: By God, you are in your old error, he said: From your love for Joseph.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us.
m: He said, Amr told us, on the authority of Sufyan, something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: They said, ‘By God, you are indeed in your old error.’ He said: In your old love.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: They said, ‘By God, you are indeed in your old error,’ meaning: You are among those who mentioned Joseph in the falsehood that you are upon.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: By God, you are indeed in your old error, he said: They mean his old grief over Joseph, and in your old error, in your old mistake.

x: God Almighty says: When Jacob, the bearer of good tidings, came from his son Joseph, and he was the bearer of good tidings of Joseph’s message, and that was a messenger, as mentioned, Joseph was the one who sent him the message. The messenger, as mentioned, and the herald, was Judah, son of Jacob, Joseph’s brother on his father’s side.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So when the bearer of good tidings came
h
he threw it on his face
. He says: The bearer of good tidings is the messenger.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: When the bearer of good report came, he said: the postman.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Muhammad bin Yazid Al-Wasiti told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: When the bearer of good report came, he said: the postman. He said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
So when the bearer of good tidings came
, he said: Judah, son of Jacob.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The bearer of good tidings, he said: Judah bin Ya’qub.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Judah bin Ya’qub. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: He is Judah bin Ya’qub.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: When the bearer of good tidings came, he said: Judah bin Ya’qub, he was the bearer of good tidings.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: When the bearer of good tidings came, he said: He is Judah bin Jacob. Sufyan said: Ibn Masoud used to recite: And the bearer of good tidings came from before the caravan.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: When the bearer of good tidings came, he said: The messenger, and he is Judah bin Ya’qub. He said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: Joseph said: “Go with this shirt of mine and throw it over my father’s face, and he will regain his sight. Then bring me all your family.” Judah said: I went with the shirt stained with blood to Jacob and told him that Joseph had been eaten by a wolf. Today I will go with the shirt and tell him that he is alive, and I will make him happy as I made him sad. So he was the bearer of good tidings.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: When the bearer of good report came, he said: the postman.

x: Some of the Arab scholars from Kufa used to say: An in his statement: Fal-ma anta ja’ al-Basheer and its omission have the same meaning. He used to say: This is in lama and hatta in particular. It is mentioned that the Arabs sometimes include it in them and sometimes omit it, as God the Most High said: And when our messengers came, and He said in another place: And when our messengers came, and he said: It is a relative clause and has no place in these two places.
It is said: Hatta kana kana or Hatta an kana kana And his saying:
h
He threw it on his face
, means: The bearer of good tidings threw Joseph’s shirt on Jacob’s face, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: When the bearer of good report came, he threw the shirt over his face. And His statement: So he regained his sight, meaning: He returned and regained sight with his eyes, after he had become blind. “He said: Did I not tell you that I know from God that which you do not know?” God Almighty says: Jacob said to those of his sons who were with him at that time: Did I not tell you, O my sons, that I know from God that He will return Joseph to me and reunite me with him? And you did not know of that what I knew, because Joseph’s vision was true, and God had decreed that I and you should prostrate before Him, so I was certain of His decree.

x: God Almighty said: “They said, ‘O our father, ask forgiveness for us for our sins. Indeed, we were sinners.’”

God Almighty says: The sons of Jacob who had separated him from Joseph said: O our father, ask your Lord to pardon us and cover for us our sins that we committed in you and in Joseph, so that He will not punish us for them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, we were sinners, in what we did to him, for we have confessed our sins. He said, ‘I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord,’ God Almighty says: Jacob said: I will ask my Lord to pardon you for your sins that you committed in me and in Joseph. Then the scholars differed about the time when Jacob delayed the supplication for his sons to seek forgiveness for their sins.
Some of them said: Postpone it until dawn.
Who said that?

c: Abu Al-Sa'ib told me, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said,
m: I heard Abd Al-Rahman bin Ishaq mentioning on the authority of Muharrib bin Dithar who said: My uncle used to come to the mosque and he heard a man saying: O God, You called upon me and I answered, and You commanded me and I obeyed, and this is magic, so forgive me. He said: So he listened to the voice and it was from the house of Abdullah bin Mas'ud. So he asked Abdullah about that and he said: Jacob delayed his sons until magic by saying: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muharrib ibn Dithar, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masoud:
m: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, he said: He delayed them until dawn. He said, Abu Sufyan Al-Himyari told us, on the authority of Al-Awam, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi, regarding Jacob’s saying to his sons: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, he said: He delayed them until dawn. He said, Amr told us, on the authority of Khallad al-Saffar, on the authority of Amr bin Qais: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, he said: in the night prayer.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, he said: He delayed that until dawn.

x: Others said: He postponed it until Friday night.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman Abu Ayyub al-Dimashqi told us, he said, al-Walid told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’ and Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, he said: until Friday night comes, and this is what my brother Jacob said to his sons.

c: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Tirmidhi told us, he said, Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi told us, he said, al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’ and Ikrimah,
m: the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: My brother Jacob said: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, meaning: until Friday night comes. And His saying: He is the Forgiving, the Most Merciful, means: My Lord is the One who covers the sins of those who repent to Him for their sins, the Most Merciful, towards them, so that He does not punish them after they repent from them.

x: God Almighty says: So when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents into his care and said, ‘Enter Egypt, if God wills, in safety.’

God Almighty says: When Jacob, his sons, and their families entered upon Joseph, he took his parents into his care, meaning he took his parents into his care, and said to them: Enter Egypt, God willing, in safety.

How did Joseph say to them: Enter Egypt, God willing, in safety, after they had entered it, and God Almighty informed us about them that when they entered it to Joseph and he had taken his parents to him, he said this to them?
The people of interpretation differed on that.

Some of them said: Jacob entered upon Joseph with his son, and Joseph sheltered his parents with him before entering Egypt. They said: This is because Joseph met his father as an honor to him before he entered Egypt, so he sheltered him with him, then he said to him and those with him: Enter Egypt, God willing, in safety, before entering it.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: So they brought their families and children to him, and when they reached Egypt, Joseph spoke to the king who was above him, so he and the kings went out to meet them, and when they reached Egypt, he said: Enter Egypt, God willing, in safety. “And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents into his care.”

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Jaafar bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of Farqad Al-Sabkhi, he said:
m: When the shirt was thrown over his face, he regained his sight and said: Bring me all your family, so Jacob and Joseph’s brothers carried him. When he approached, he informed Joseph that he had approached him, so he went out to meet him. He said: The people of Egypt rode with him, and they were honoring him. When one of them approached the other, and Jacob was walking leaning on a man from his sons called Judah, he said: Jacob looked at the horses and the people and said: O Judah, is this the Pharaoh of Egypt? He said: No, this is your son! He said: When each of them approached the other, Joseph tried to greet him first, but he was prevented from doing so, and Jacob was more deserving of it and better than him, so he said: Peace be upon you, O Remover of my sorrows, this is what he said: O Remover of my sorrows.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj said:
m: It reached me that Joseph and the king went out with four thousand to meet Jacob and his sons. He said, and I was told by someone who heard Jaʿfar bin Sulayman narrating on the authority of Farqad al-Sabkhi, who said: Yusuf went out to meet Jacob, and the people of Egypt rode with Yusuf. Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith, similar to the hadith of al-Harith, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz.

x: Others said: Rather, his saying, God willing, is an exception to Jacob’s saying to his sons, I ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. He said: It is from the word mukhdhir which means to bring forward. They said: Rather, the meaning of the statement is: He said: I ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, God willing. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. So when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to him and said: Enter Egypt, and he raised his parents.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: h
I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord
, God willing, while you are safe, and between that is what he explained about presenting the Qur’an.

x: meaning Ibn Jurayj: And between that is what he explained about the presentation of the Qur’an, that between His saying:
h
I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord
, and His saying: God willing, there is some speech that has entered, and its place, according to him, is that it follows His saying:
h
I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord

The correct statement regarding this matter, according to us, is what al-Suddi said, which is that Joseph said this to his parents and those with them of their children and their families before they entered Egypt when he met them, because that is how it appears in the revelation, so there is no evidence that indicates the correctness of what Ibn Jurayj said, and there is no reason to advance something from the Book of God from its place or delay it from its place except with a clear argument. It was said: What he meant by his saying:
h
He took his parents to him was his father and his maternal aunt
Those who said this statement said: Joseph’s mother had died before, and what was with Jacob at that time was his maternal aunt, his mother’s sister, whom he married after his mother.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: So when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself, he said: his father and his maternal aunt.

x: Others said: Rather, it was his father and mother.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: So when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself, he said: his father and his mother.

x: The more correct of the two statements on this matter is what Ibn Ishaq said, because that is what is most common in people’s usage and familiarity with each other regarding two parents, unless what is said is correct, that Joseph’s mother had died before that for a reason that must be accepted, in which case it must be accepted for her. And his saying: And he said, ‘Enter Egypt, if God wills, in safety,’ from the drought and famine you were experiencing in your desert.
His saying:
h
And he raised his parents to the throne
, means: to the bed, as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And he raised his parents to the throne
, he said: the bed.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Muhammad bin Yazid Al-Wasiti told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: The Throne is the bed. He said, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
And he raised his parents to the throne
, he said: the bed.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid - and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And he raised his parents to the throne
, he said: his bed.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: On the Throne, he said: On the bed.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And he raised his parents to the throne
, he said: He raised his parents to the bed.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan said:
m: h
And he raised his parents to the throne
, he said: On the bed.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And raised his parents to the throne
, he said: His seat.

c: Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me, he said, Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, he said,
m: I asked Zayd ibn Aslam about the statement of God:
h
And raised his parents to the throne

, and I said: Have you been informed that she is his maternal aunt? He said: Some of the people of knowledge said that, they say that his mother died before that, and that this is his maternal aunt. And his saying:
h
And they fell down before him in prostration
, means: Jacob, his son, and his mother fell down before Joseph in prostration.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And they fell down before him in prostration
, meaning: He raised his parents onto the bed and prostrated before him, and his brothers prostrated before him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: He - meaning Jacob - carried his family until they came to Joseph. When Jacob’s sons gathered to him, they entered upon Joseph. When they saw him, they fell down in prostration to him, and that was the greeting of the kings at that time, his father, his mother, and his Surat Yusuf 12:100
h
And he raised his parents to the throne
h
and they fell down before him in prostration
, and he said, "
h
O my father

, this is the interpretation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it come true. And He has been gracious to me when He brought me out of prison and brought you from the desert after Satan had sown discord between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Kind to whom He wills. Indeed, He is the All-Wise." The All-Knowing, the All-Wise brothers.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And they fell down before him in prostration

. This was a greeting before you, with which they would greet one another. Then God gave this nation peace, the greeting of the people of Paradise, as an honor from God, the Blessed and Exalted, which He hastened for them, and a blessing from Him.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And they fell down before him in prostration
. He said: The greeting of the people on that day was for some of them to prostrate to one another.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ishaq told us, Sufyan said:
m: And they fell down prostrating before him, he said: It was a greeting among them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
And they fell down before him in prostration
, his parents and his brothers. That was their greeting, as people do today.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
And they fell down before him in prostration
, he said: a greeting between them.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they fell down before him in prostration

, he said, he said: That prostration is for his honor, just as the angels prostrated to Adam for his honor, it is not a prostration of worship. What was meant by the statement that prostration was a greeting between them was that it was done by them to people, not as an act of worship from one another. What indicates that this was not part of the morals of the people in ancient times before Islam, other than as an act of worship from one another, is the statement of A’sha of Banu Tha’labah: When he came to us in the middle of the night, we prostrated to him and raised Ammar. And His saying: “
h
O my father
, this is the interpretation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it come true,” He, the Most High, says: Joseph said to his father:
h
O my father

, this prostration that you, my mother, and my brothers prostrated to me, is the interpretation of my vision of before, meaning: what my vision that I had seen had come to, and it was his vision that he had seen before his brothers did what they did to him: that eleven stars and the sun and the moon were prostrating to him, my Lord has made it come true, meaning: my Lord has fulfilled it, because its interpretation came to be correct. Scholars have differed about the amount of time between Joseph’s vision and its interpretation.

x: Some of them said: The duration of that was forty years.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, he said, Abu Uthman told us, on the authority of Salman Al-Farsi, he said:
m: There were forty years between Joseph’s vision and his seeing its interpretation.

c: Yaqub bin Burhan and Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, they said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Sulayman al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, he said, Uthman said:
m: There were forty years between Joseph’s vision and when he saw its interpretation. He said: Then he mentioned.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Salman, who said:
m: There were forty years between Joseph’s vision and its interpretation.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad, he said:
m: He saw the interpretation of his dream after forty years. He said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Salman, the same.

c: Abu Al-Saib told me, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Dhirar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad:
m: That he heard some people disputing about a dream that one of them had seen while he was praying. When he finished, he asked them about it, but they concealed it from him. So he said: Indeed, the interpretation of Joseph’s dream came after forty years.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Dhirar bin Murrah Abi Sinan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad, he said:
m: There were forty years between Joseph’s vision and its interpretation.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil and Jarir told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, he said:
m: Abdullah Ibn Shaddad heard some people disputing about a dream, so he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Abu Al-Sa’ib on the authority of Ibn Fadil.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Salman, who said:
m: He saw the interpretation of his dream after forty years.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad, he said:
m: Joseph’s vision occurred after forty years, and the end of the vision ends there. He said, Muadh bin Muadh told us, Sulayman al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Salman, who said: There were forty years between Joseph’s vision and when he saw its interpretation. He said, Abdul Wahhab bin Ata’ told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Salman, who said: There were forty years between Joseph’s vision and its interpretation. He said, Saeed bin Suleiman told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Suleiman al-Taimi, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Salman, who said: There were forty years between Joseph’s vision and his seeing its interpretation. He said, Amr bin Muhammad Al-Anqazi told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad, he said: There were forty years between Joseph’s vision and its interpretation.

x: Others said: It lasted for eighty years.
Who said that?

c: Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab Al-Thaqafi told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: It was eighty years from the time Joseph left Jacob until they met, and sadness did not leave his heart, and his tears ran down his cheeks, and there was not on the face of the earth that day a servant more beloved to God than Jacob.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar Jisr ibn Farqad, he said:
m: There were eighty years between the time Jacob lost Joseph until the day he was returned to him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hassan bin Ali told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Ayyad, he said:
m: I heard that there were eighty years between Joseph’s separation from Jacob’s stone until they met.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Dawud bin Mihran told us, he said, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: Joseph was thrown into the well when he was seventeen years old, and between that and his meeting with Jacob there were eighty years, and he lived after that for twenty-three years, and he died when he was one hundred and twenty years old. He said, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, something similar, except that he said: eighty-three years. He said, Dawud bin Mihran told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Joseph was thrown into the well when he was seventeen years old, and he was in slavery and in prison as a king for eighty years, then God Almighty reunited him, and he lived after that for twenty-three years.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Mubarak bin Fadala told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: Joseph was thrown into the well when he was seventeen years old, and he was absent from his father for eighty years. Then he lived after God reunited him and he saw the interpretation of his dream for twenty-three years, and he died when he was one hundred and twenty years old.

c: Mujahid told us, Yazid told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: Joseph was absent from his father in the well and in prison until they met for eighty years, and Jacob’s eyes never dried, and there was no one on earth more honorable to God than Jacob.

x: Others said: It lasted eighteen years.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: It was mentioned to me, and God knows best, that Joseph’s absence from Jacob was eighteen years. He said: The People of the Book claim that it was forty years or thereabouts, and that Jacob remained with Joseph after he came to him in Egypt for seventeen years, then God took him to Himself. And His saying:
h
And He was kind to me when He brought me out of prison and brought you from the desert

, the Most High says, informing about what Joseph said: And God was kind to me in bringing me out of the prison in which I was confined, and in bringing you from the desert. And that is because the dwelling of Jacob and his son, as mentioned, was in the desert of Palestine, likewise:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: The home of Jacob and his son, according to what some scholars have told me, was in the Arabats, the land of Palestine, the borders of the Levant. Some say: in Al-Awlaj, on the side of the valley. He was a Bedouin, he had camels and sheep.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, an old man of ours told us:
m: Jacob was in the desert of Palestine.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Aqtada:
m: h
And He was kind to me when He brought me out of prison and brought you from the desert
. Jacob and his sons were in the land of Canaan, people of livestock and the wilderness.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: And he brought you from the Bedouins, he said: They were people of the desert and livestock. Bedouins, a noun derived from the saying: So-and-so went to the desert, if he went to the desert, he went to the desert. He mentioned that Jacob entered Egypt with his sons, their families, and their children on the day they entered it, and they were less than a hundred. They left it on the day they left it, and they were more than six hundred thousand. Surat Yusuf 12:100
h
And he raised his parents to the throne
h
and they fell down before him in prostration
, and he said, "
h
O my father

, this is the interpretation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it come true. And He has been gracious to me when He brought me out of prison and brought you from the desert after Satan had sown discord between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Kind to whom He wills. Indeed, He is the All-Wise." The All-Knowing, the All-Wise The novel mentioned that:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zaid bin Al-Habbab and Amr bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad, who said:
m: The family of Jacob gathered with Joseph in Egypt, and they were eighty-six people, young and old, male and female. And they left Egypt on the day that Pharaoh expelled them, and they were more than six hundred thousand. He said, Amr told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The people of Joseph left Egypt, and they were six hundred and seventy thousand, and Pharaoh said: Indeed, these are a small group.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Israel and Al-Masoudi, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said:
m: The Children of Israel entered Egypt and they were sixty-three people. And they left it and they were six hundred thousand. Israel said in his hadith: six hundred thousand and seventy thousand.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Masruq, he said:
m: The people of Joseph entered Egypt, and they were three hundred and ninety, including men and women. His saying:
h
After Satan has caused discord between me and my brothers

, means: after he has corrupted what is between me and them, and some of us have become ignorant of others. It is said: The devil sowed discord between so-and-so and so-and-so, he sows discord and discord. And his saying: Indeed, my Lord is Kind to whomever He wills, he says: Indeed, my Lord is Kind and does what He wills, and from His kindness and doing is that He brought me out of prison and brought my family from the Bedouins, after what had been between me and them of separation from home, and after what I had been in of slavery and bondage, like that which:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, my Lord is Kind to whomever He wills, He was kind to Joseph and did for him until He brought him out of prison, and brought his family from the desert, and removed from his heart the instigation of Satan and his incitement against his brothers. And His saying: He is the All-Knowing, of the interests of His creation and other things. The beginnings and consequences of things are not hidden from Him. The All-Wise, in His management.

x: God Almighty says: Joseph said, after God had gathered his parents and brothers for him, and had extended to him from the world what He had extended of honor, and had established him on the earth, longing to meet his righteous fathers: My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom, meaning: of the kingdom of Egypt, and taught me of the interpretation of dreams, meaning of the expression of the vision, enumerating God’s blessings upon him, and thanking Him for them, Creator of the heavens and the earth, meaning: O Creator of the heavens and the earth, O Creator and Maker of them, You are my protector in this world and the Hereafter, meaning: You are my protector in my world against those who oppose me and wish me harm with Your support, and You nourish me in it with Your favor, and You make me gentle in the Hereafter with Your grace and mercy, Let me die as a Muslim, meaning: Take me to You as a Muslim, And join me with the righteous, meaning: And join me with the righteous of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac and those before them of Your prophets and messengers. . It was said: None of the prophets wished for death before Joseph.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom and taught me of the interpretation of dreams, the verse. Ibn Abbas used to say: The first prophet to ask God for death was Joseph.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Hussein narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: His statement, My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom, the verse, he said: He longed to meet his Lord, and he wanted to join Him and his fathers, so he asked God to take him and join him with them. And no prophet ever asked for death except Joseph, who said, My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom and taught me of the interpretation of dreams, the verse. Ibn Jurayj said: In some of the Qur’an, there are some prophets who said: Take me.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Let me die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous

, when he had gathered his affairs and satisfied his eyes, and he was on that day immersed in the vegetation of the world, its kingdom and its freshness, so he longed for the righteous before him. Ibn Abbas used to say: No prophet ever wished for death before Joseph.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Aruba, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: When Joseph’s affairs were gathered together and blessings were bestowed upon him, he asked to meet his Lord and said: “My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom and taught me of the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.” Qatada said: No one ever wished for death, prophet or otherwise, except Joseph.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said, more than one person told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: That when the Prophet Joseph, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reunited with his father and brothers, and he was at that time the king of Egypt, he longed for God and for his righteous fathers, Abraham and Isaac, so he said: “My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom and taught me of the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my protector in this world and in the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Khalid, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you taught me the interpretation of dreams
, he said: the phrase.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Let me die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous

, meaning: Let me die in obedience to You, and forgive me when You let me die. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that he said: Joseph said, when he saw what he saw of God’s honor and favor upon him and his family, when God reunited him and returned him to his father, and united him with him in what he was in of kingship and joy: “O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it come true,” until His saying: Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise. Then Joseph was frightened and remembered that what he was in of this world was perishing and going away, so he said: “My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom and taught me of the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my protector in this world and in the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.” He mentioned that the sons of Jacob who did what they did to Joseph, their father asked forgiveness for them, so God repented to them and pardoned them, and forgave them their sin.

x: Who said that? Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Hussein narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Salih Al-Mari, on the authority of Yazid Al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: When God, the Blessed and Exalted, reunited Jacob and made his eyes happy, He left his sons alone, and some of them said to one another: Do you not know what you did, what the old man suffered from you, and what Joseph suffered from you? They said: Yes. He said: Does their forgiveness of you deceive you, so what will you do with your Lord? So their affair was settled so that they went to the old man and sat before him, and Joseph was sitting beside his father. They said: O our father, we have come to you regarding a matter like which we have never come to you regarding before, and a matter has befallen us like which has never befallen us, until they stirred him up, and the prophets are the most merciful of creation.

He said: What is the matter with you, my sons? They said: Do you not know what happened from us to you, and what happened from us to our brother Joseph? He said: Yes. They said: Have you not forgiven? They said: Yes. They said: Your pardon will not avail us at all if God has not pardoned us. He said: What do you want, my sons? They said: We want you to supplicate to God for us, and when the revelation comes to you from God that He has pardoned what we have done, our eyes will be comforted and our hearts will be reassured, otherwise we will never have comfort in this world. He said: So the old man stood up and faced the Qiblah, and Joseph stood behind his father, and they stood behind them, humbled and submissive. He said: So he supplicated and Joseph responded, but they did not respond for twenty years. Salih al-Muri said: He frightened them. He said: Then when it was the beginning of the twenty, Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended to Jacob, peace be upon him, and said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, has sent me to you to give you good report that He has answered your supplication regarding your son, and that He has pardoned what they have done, and that He has honored their covenants on prophethood after you.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Jaafar bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of Abu Imran Al-Joni, he said:
m: By God, if the killing of Joseph had happened, God would have thrown them all into Hell, but God, may He be glorified and exalted, held back Joseph’s soul so that He might convey His command to him, and out of mercy for them. Then he says: By God, God did not tell us their story to reproach them for that, for they are prophets from the people of Paradise, but God told us their story so that His servant would not despair. He mentioned that Jacob died before Joseph, and he made a will to Joseph, and ordered him to bury him next to the grave of his father Isaac.

x: Who said that? Ibn Wakee' narrated, Amr narrated, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: When death approached Jacob, he instructed Joseph to bury him near Abraham and Isaac. When he died, myrrh was breathed into him and he was carried to Ash-Sham. He said: When they reached that place, Esau, Jacob's brother, came and said: He defeated me in the call, but by God, he will not defeat me in the grave. But he refused to let them bury him. When they were delayed, Hisham bin Dan bin Jacob - and Hisham was deaf - said to some of his brothers: Why is my grandfather not being buried? They said: This is your uncle preventing him. He said: Show him to me, where is he? When he saw him, Hisham raised his hand and struck Esau's head with it, and suddenly his eyes fell on Jacob's thigh, so they were buried in one grave.

God Almighty says: This report that I have told you, of the report of Joseph and his father Jacob and his brothers and the rest of what is in this Surah, is from the report of the unseen, meaning: from the report of the unseen that you have not seen or witnessed, but We reveal it to you and make it known to you so that we may strengthen your heart and encourage your heart, and you may be patient with the harm that befell you from your people for the sake of God, and you may know that those before you from the Messengers of God, when they were patient with what befell them in it, and took to forgiveness, and enjoined what is right, and turned away from the ignorant, they won victory, and were supported with triumph, and were empowered in the land, and they defeated those who intended from their enemies and the enemies of God’s religion. God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: O Muhammad, take a lead in them, and narrate their traces.
h
And you were not with them

when they decided on their plan while they were plotting.” He says: And you were not present with Joseph’s brothers when they decided on their plan while they were plotting. He says: And you were not present with Joseph’s brothers when they decided on their plan while they were plotting. He says: “And you were not present with Joseph’s brothers when they agreed ... when they were plotting.” He says: And you were not present with Joseph when they were plotting. He says: And you were not present with Joseph when they were plotting. He says: And you were plotting.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you were not with them
, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: I was not with them while they were throwing him into the bottom of the well, and they were plotting, meaning: against Joseph.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And you were not with them
when they decided on their plan and they were plotting, the verse. He said: They are the sons of Jacob.

x: God Almighty says: How many are the polytheists among your people, O Muhammad. Even if you were keen for them to believe in you, confirm you, and follow what you brought them from your Lord, they would not believe you or follow you.

God Almighty says to Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him: What do you ask, O Muhammad, of those who deny your prophethood and refuse to believe in you and acknowledge what you have brought them from your Lord, for what you call them to of sincere worship of your Lord, abandoning the worship of idols and obeying the Most Merciful, of reward? Meaning: of reward and recompense from them, but your reward and the reward of your work is with God. He says: What do you ask of them for that as a reward, so that they say to you: You only want by calling us to follow you that we give you our wealth since you asked us for that. And since you do not ask them for that, it is right for them to know that you are calling them to what you are calling them to, following the command of your Lord, and advising them, and that they should not deceive you. And His saying:
h
It is only a reminder to the worlds

, God Almighty says: What is this with which your Lord sent you, O Muhammad, of prophecy and message, except a reminder, meaning: Except an admonition and reminder to the worlds, so that they may learn from it and remember it.

God Almighty says: And how many are the signs in the heavens and the earth for God, and a lesson and an argument, such as the sun, the moon, the stars, and other signs of the heavens, and the mountains, the seas, the plants, the trees, and other signs of the earth, they pass by them, meaning: they see them and pass by them, turning away from them, not considering them, nor thinking about them and what they indicate of the oneness of their Lord, and that divinity is only appropriate for the One, the Compeller, who created them and created everything, and managed them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, and in the Mushaf of Abdullah it is: they walk by it, the heavens and the earth are two great signs.

x: God Almighty says: Most of these people - whom God Almighty described in His words: And how many a sign is there in the heavens and the earth which they pass by while they are turning away from it - do not acknowledge God as their Creator and Provider and the Creator of everything, except that they are polytheists in their worship of idols and statues, and their taking lords besides Him, and their claim that He has a son. God is exalted above what they say. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Imran bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And most of them do not believe in God, the verse. He said: Of their faith, when it is said to them: Who created the heaven? Who created the earth? Who created the mountains? They say: God, and they are polytheists.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him
, he said: You ask them: Who created them? And who created the heavens and the earth? They say: God. So that is their belief in God, while they worship other than Him.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer and Ikrimah:
m: And most of them do not believe in God, the verse. They said: They know that He is their Lord and that He created them, and they associate others with Him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer and Ikrimah,
m: something similar. He said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Nadr, on the authority of Ikrimah:
h
And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him

. He said: From their faith, when it is said to them: Who created the heavens? They say: God. And when it is asked: Who created them? They say: God. And they associate others with Him after that. He said, Abu Naim told us, on the authority of Al-Fadl bin Yazid Al-Thamali, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: It is the saying of God: And if you ask them, Who created the heavens and the earth? they will surely say, God. So if they are asked about God and His description, they describe Him with descriptions other than His, and attribute to Him a son, and associate others with Him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh,
m: on his saying:
h
And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him
, their belief is their saying: God is our Creator, He provides for us, and He causes us to die.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him
. So their belief is their saying: God is our Creator, He provides for us, and He causes us to die.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him

. Their belief is their saying: God is our Creator, He provides for us, and He causes us to die. So this is belief along with their association with others by worshipping others besides Him. He said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him
. He said: Their belief is their saying: God is our Creator, He provides for us, and He causes us to die.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hani’ bin Saeed and Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: They say: God is our Lord, and He provides for us, and they are still associating partners with Him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Their faith is their saying: God is our Creator, He provides for us, and He causes us to die. He said, Al-Husayn told us, Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah, Mujahid, and Aamer: that they said about this verse:
h
And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him
. He said: There is no one who does not know that God created him and created the heavens and the earth, so this is their belief, and they disbelieve in everything other than that.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And most of them do not believe in God Surat Yusuf 12
h
And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him

. except while they associate others with Him, regarding their belief in this. You will not meet anyone among them except that he informs you that God is his Lord, and He is the One who created him and provided for him, and he is an associate in his worship.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And most of them do not believe in God, the verse, he said: Do not ask any of the polytheists: Who is your Lord? except that he will say: My Lord is God, and he is associating partners with God in that.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told us, he said, my uncle told me, he said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him

, meaning the Christians. He says: And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, ‘God,’ “And if you ask them who created them, they will surely say, ‘God,’” and if you ask them: Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? they will surely say, God. And yet they associate others with Him and worship other than Him, and prostrate to rivals besides Him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: They used to associate others with Him in their Talbiyah.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ata’:
m: And most of them do not believe in God, the verse, he said: They know that God is their Lord, and they associate others with Him after that.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him
, he said: They know that God is their Creator and Provider, and they associate others with Him.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: I heard Ibn Zayd say: And most of them do not believe in God, the verse, he said: No one worships other than Him with God except that he believes in God, and knows that God is his Lord, and that God is his Creator and Provider, and he associates others with Him. Do you not see how Abraham said: Have you seen what you used to worship, you and your forefathers of old? Indeed, they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds. He knew that they worship the Lord of the worlds along with what they worship. He said: No one associates others with Him except that he believes in Him. Do you not see how the Arabs used to respond, saying: Here I am, O God, here I am, here I am, You have no partner, except a partner who is Yours, You own him and what he owns? The polytheists used to say this.

x: God Almighty says: Are these people who do not acknowledge that God is their Lord except while they are associating others with Him in their worship of Him, safe from
h
a covering of the punishment of God

coming upon them, covering them with God’s punishment and torment for their associating partners with God, or the Resurrection coming upon them suddenly while they are persisting in their associating partners with God and disbelieving in their Lord, so God Almighty will make them dwell in His Fire forever, and they will not know of its coming and occurrence. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: That there will come upon them an overwhelming punishment from God, he said: It will overwhelm them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
A covering of the punishment of God
, he said: It covers them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do they then feel secure that there will not come to them an overwhelming punishment from God
? meaning: a punishment from the punishment of God.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
A covering of the punishment of God
. He said, A covering is a calamity that will cover them from the punishment of God.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad: This is the call to which I call, and the method which I am on, of calling to the Oneness of God, and sincere worship of Him without deities and idols, and ending with His obedience, and abandoning His disobedience, my way, my method and my call, I call to God alone with no partner for Him, with insight, with that and certainty of knowledge from me, and he who follows me, believes in me, and has faith in me also calls to it with insight, and glory be to God, God Almighty says to him: And say, in glorification of God, and in glorification of Him from having a partner in His kingdom, or a deity other than Him in His authority: and I am not of the polytheists, meaning: I am innocent of the people of polytheism with Him, I am not of them and they are not of me. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas,
m: regarding his statement: “Say, ‘This is my way. I invite to God with insight.’” He said: This is my call.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: “Say, ‘This is my way. I invite to God with insight.’” He said: This is my way, this is my command, my way, and my method. I invite to God with insight, I and whoever follows me, he said: And it is the right of God upon whoever follows him to call to what he called to, and to remind with the Qur’an and preaching, and to forbid the disobedience of God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas,
m: regarding his statement: Say, ‘This is my way,’ meaning, this is my call.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: Say, ‘This is my way.’ He said: This is my call.

x: God Almighty says: And We did not send, O Muhammad, before you, except men, not women nor angels, to whom We revealed, Our signs, calling to obey Us and to worship Us alone, from the people of the towns, meaning: from the people of the cities, not the people of the deserts, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed from the people of the towns
, because they were more knowledgeable and patient than the people of the pillar. And His statement:
h
Have they not traveled through the land

, God Almighty says: Have these polytheists who belie you, O Muhammad, and reject your prophethood, and deny what you brought them of the Oneness of God, and sincere obedience and worship of Him, not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them, when they rejected Our messengers? Did We not inflict Our punishment upon them, destroying them with it, and save from it Our messengers and followers, so that they might reflect on that and take heed?

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said:
m: His statement:
h
And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed
, he said: They said:
h
God has not sent down anything to any human being
, he said: And His statement:
h
And most of the people are not believers, even if you desire it. And you do not ask them for any payment for it
, and His statement:
h
And how many a sign is there in the heavens and the earth that they pass by
, and His statement:
h
Do they then feel secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming punishment from God
, and His statement:
h
Have they not traveled through the land and seen
, who We have destroyed? He said: So about all of that he said to the Quraysh 106:Did they not travel through the land and see their traces, and take heed and reflect? And His statement:
h
And the home of the Hereafter is better

, the Most High says: This is what We did in this world with the people of Our authority and obedience, that when Our punishment descends upon the people of Our disobedience and polytheism, We save them from it, and what is in the home of the Hereafter is better for them. And he left out mentioning what we mentioned, being content with the indication of his saying:
h
And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God

, upon it, and the home was added to the Hereafter, which is the Hereafter, due to the difference in their wording, as it was said: Indeed, this is the certain truth, and as it was said: I came to you in the year of the first, and the night of the first, and the night of the first, and on Thursday, and as the poet said: You praise Faq'as and criticize Abs. By God, your mother is from a hybrid. Even if the land of Abs could overpower you, you would know humiliation with certainty. Meaning: knowing him with certainty.

x: The interpretation of the words is: The Hereafter is better for those who fear God, by performing His duties and avoiding His sins. And His statement:
h
Do you not understand

? He says: Do these polytheists not understand the truth of what we say to them and inform them of, about the evil consequences of disbelief and the fate of what will become of its people, along with what they have witnessed, seen and heard of what happened to the nations before them who disbelieved and denied the messengers of their Lord?

God Almighty says: And We did not send before you, except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns, so they called upon those to whom We sent, but they denied them and rejected what they brought from God,
h
until when the messengers despaired

, those to whom We sent them of them that they would believe in God and believe them in what they brought them from God, and those to whom We sent from the nations who denied thought that the messengers whom We sent had denied them in what they had told them from God, of His promise to them of victory over them, Our victory came to them. This is what a group of interpreters say.
Who said that?

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib bin Janadah told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied

, he said: When the messengers despaired that their people would respond to them, and their people thought that the messengers had denied them, victory came to them in that regard, so We save whom We will.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah Al-Dharee’ told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar, except that he said in his hadith, he said: The messengers despaired, and he did not say: When they despaired.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
Until when the messengers despaired
that their people would submit, and the people of the messengers thought that the messengers had lied, then Our victory came to them.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Imran bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Until when the messengers despaired
of their people and thought that they had been denied, he said:
h
Until when the messengers despaired
of their people and their people thought that the messengers had been denied, Our victory came to them.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Imran al-Salami, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Until the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied
, he said: The messengers despaired of their people believing them, and their people thought that the messengers had denied them.

c: Amr bin Abdul Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Imran bin Al-Harith Al-Salami, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until when the messengers despaired
, he said: The messengers despaired of their people responding to them,
h
and they thought that they had been denied
, he said: Their people thought that they had come to them with lies.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said,
m: I heard Hasin, on the authority of Imran bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
Until when the messengers despaired
of their people responding to them, and their people thought that they had been denied, Our victory came to them.

c: Abu Hasin Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Yunus told me, he said, Abthar told us, he said, Hasin told us, on the authority of Imran bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding this verse:
h
Until when the messengers despaired
, he said: The messengers despaired of their people believing, and their people thought that the messengers had lied to them in what they had promised and lied, Our victory came to them.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Imran ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: h
Until the messengers despaired of their people
’s victory, and thought that they had been denied, their people thought that they had been denied.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hisin told us, on the authority of Imran bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until when the messengers despaired

, he said: from their people that they would believe in them, and that they would respond to him, and their people thought that the messengers had denied them, Our victory came to them, meaning the messengers.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Imran bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab bin Ata’ told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Ibad Al-Qurashi, on the authority of Abdul-Rahman bin Muawiyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And they thought that they had been lied to, light, and its interpretation according to him is: And the people thought that the messengers had been lied to.

c: Abu Bakr told us, he said, Talq bin Ghannam told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: h
Until when the messengers despaired
of their people believing them, and their people thought that their messengers had lied to them, Our victory came to them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
Until when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied
, meaning: the messengers despaired that their people would follow them, and their people thought that the messengers had been denied, so God gave victory to the messengers and sent the punishment.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until when the messengers despaired of their people obeying them and following them
, and their people thought that their messengers had denied them, “Our victory came to them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad bin Fadil told me, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Imran bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Until the messengers despaired of their people

, and thought that they had been denied, he said: So nothing delayed them except those who thought that they had been denied. He said, Adam Al-Asqalani told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, he said, Husayn bin Abd Al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Imran bin Al-Harith, he said, I heard Ibn Abbas say: And they thought that they had been lied to, light, and Ibn Abbas said: The people thought that the messengers had lied to them, light.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until the messengers despaired of their people
, and their people thought that the messengers had denied them. He said, Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of Khasif, who said, I asked Saeed bin Jubair about his statement:
h
