Until the messengers despaired
, of their people, and the disbelievers thought that they were the ones who had lied.

c: Yaqub and Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told me, they said: Ismail bin Aliyah told us, he said: Kalthum bin Jabr told us, on the authority of Saʿd bin Jubayr,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until the messengers despaired of their people believing
, and their people thought that the messengers had lied to them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Arim Abu Al-Nu’man told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, he said, Shu’aib told us, he said, Ibrahim bin Abi Harrah Al-Jazari told me, he said:
m: A young man from Quraysh asked Saeed bin Jubayr and said to him: O Abu Abdullah, how do you recite this letter, for whenever I come to it I wish that I had not recited this surah:
h
Until when the messengers despaired
of their people and thought that they had been denied, he said: Yes,
h
until when the messengers despaired

of their people believing them, and the ones to whom they were sent thought that the messengers had been denied. He said: Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim said: I have never seen a man called to knowledge who hesitates like today. If I traveled to Yemen in this way, it would be little.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Al-Hajjaj told us, Rabia bin Kulthum told us, my father told me:
m: Muslim bin Yasar asked Saeed bin Jubair and said: O Abu Abdullah, a verse has reached me very deeply: Until when the messengers despair and think that they have been denied, this is death, that the messengers think that they have been denied, or think that they have been denied, lightened. He said: So Saeed bin Jubair said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman,
h
until when the messengers despaired

of their people responding to them, and their people think that the messengers have denied them, Our victory has come to them, so We save whom We will, but Our punishment cannot be repelled from the criminal people, he said: So Muslim went to Saeed and embraced him and said: May God relieve you as You relieved me.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Yahya bin Abbad told us, Wahib told us, Abu Al-Mu’alla Al-Attar told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbad:
m: h
Until the messengers despaired of their people

’s faith, and their people thought that the messengers had denied them what they were telling them and conveying to them. He said: The messengers despaired of their people’s faith, and their people thought that the messengers had denied them what they were telling them and conveying to them. He said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
Until when the messengers despaired
, that their people would believe them, and their people thought that the messengers had lied, the messengers came with Our victory.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Surat Yusuf 12:
m: 110 Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, there came to them Our victory, and whomever We willed was saved. And Our punishment cannot be repelled from the criminal people. Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding this verse:
h
Until when the messengers despaired

of their people, and their people thought that the messengers had been denied. He said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Kalthoum bin Jabr, who said, Saeed bin Jubair said to me: One of your masters asked me about this verse, so I said: The messengers despaired of their people, and their people thought that the messengers had lied.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement: Until, when the messengers gave up hope and thought that they had been denied, he said: The messengers gave up hope that their people would believe in them, and their polytheist people thought that the messengers had denied what God had promised them of His victory over them, and they had broken their promise. And he recited: Our victory came to them, he said: Victory came to the messengers at that time. He said: My father used to recite it: They were denied.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab bin Ata’ told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Abu al-Mutawakkil, on the authority of Ayoub bin Abi Safwan, on the authority of Abdullah bin al-Harith, that he said:
m: h
Until the messengers despaired
of the faith of their people, and thought that they had been denied, and the people thought that they had been denied in what they had brought them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: Their people thought that their messengers had lied to them about what they had promised them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of Jahsh bin Ziyad Al-Dhabi, on the authority of Tamim bin Hudlam, he said:
m: I heard Abdullah bin Masoud say about this verse:
h
Until when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied
, he said: The messengers despaired of their people believing in them, and their people thought when the matter was delayed that they had been denied, with the alleviation.

c: Abu Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Muʿalla, on the authority of Saʿid bin Jubayr,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until the messengers despaired
, he said: The messengers despaired of their people’s victory, and the people of the messengers thought that the messengers had lied to them.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Amr bin Thabit told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
Until the messengers despaired

of being believed, and their people thought that the messengers had lied to them. He said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
Until the messengers despaired of their people believing
them, and their people thought that the messengers had lied to them.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak regarding his statement:
h
Until when the messengers despaired
, meaning: they despaired of their people responding to them and believing in them, and they thought, meaning: the people of the messengers thought that the messengers had denied them the promise.

x: The reading is based on this interpretation that we mentioned in his statement: They lied with a damma on the kaf and a light dhal. This is also the reading of some of the readers of the people of Medina and most of the readers of the people of Kufa. We have chosen this interpretation and reading because it follows His statement: “And We sent not before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns. So have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them?” This was evidence that the despair of the messengers was due to the faith of their people who were destroyed, and that what is implied in His statement:
h
And they thought that they had been denied
, is only from mentioning those before them from the perished nations. This was also made clearer by God’s following in the context of the report about the messengers and their nations His statement:
h
Then We saved whom We willed
, since those who were destroyed were those who thought that the messengers had denied them, so they denied them, thinking that they had been denied.
Some of those who read this reading went to an interpretation other than the one we chose, and they directed its meaning to:
h
until the messengers despaired
of the faith of their people, and the messengers thought that they had been lied to in what they were promised of victory.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, he said, Uthman bin Omar told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas read:
h
Until the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied

, he said: They were human beings who were weak and despaired. He said, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abi Malekah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who recited:
h
And they thought that they had been denied

, lightly. Ibn Jurayj said: I say as he says: They broke their promise. Abdullah said: Ibn Abbas told me: They were human beings. And Ibn Abbas recited: “Until the Messenger and those who believed with him say: When is the help of God? Unquestionably, the help of God is near.” Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abi Malekah said: He meant by it that they were weak and thought that they had broken their promise.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: that he read:
h
Until the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied

, in a lightened form. Abdullah said: It is what you hate. He said, Abu Amer told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq: That a man asked Abdullah bin Masoud:
h
Until the messengers despaired

and thought that they had been lied to, he said: It is what you hate, lightened. He said, Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saʿid bin Jubayr: that he said regarding this verse:
h
Until when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied
, I said: They were denied, he said: Yes, were they not human beings?

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied
, he said: They were human beings who thought.

x: This is an interpretation and a statement. Any other interpretation is more correct in my opinion, and any statement contrary to it is more similar to the attributes of the prophets. And if it is permissible for the messengers to doubt God’s promise to them and to doubt the truth of His report, while they have witnessed from God’s proofs and evidence what the one to whom they were sent did not witness, and they are excused for that, then the one to whom they were sent is more deserving of an excuse for that than they are. And that is a statement that if someone said it, its matter would not be hidden. This interpretation, which we mentioned recently, was mentioned by Ibn Abbas to Aisha, and she denied it most strongly, according to what was mentioned to us. He mentioned the narration about her, may God be pleased with her.

i: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad narrated, he said: Uthman bin Umar narrated, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, he said: Ibn Abbas recited:
x: Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, and he said: They were human beings, they became weak and despaired.

Ibn Abi Malekah said: So I mentioned that to Urwah, and he said: Aisha said: God forbid, God and His Messenger never told him anything except that he knew that it would happen before he died, but the trials of the messengers continued until the prophets thought that those who followed them had denied them. So she would recite it: They had been denied, and she would make it heavy.

i: He said, Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abi Malekah informed me: Ibn Abbas recited:
x: h
And they thought that they had been denied
, lightly.

Abdullah said: Then Ibn Abbas said to me: They were human beings, and Ibn Abbas recited: “Until the Messenger and those who believed with him say: When is the help of God? Unquestionably, the help of God is near.” Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abi Malekah said: It goes to the point that they were weak and thought that they had broken their promise.
Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abi Malekah said:

c: Urwah informed me on the authority of Aishah
m: that she contradicted that and refused it, and said: God did not promise Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, anything except that He knew that it would happen until he died, but the trials of the messengers continued until they thought that those who were with them from the believers had denied them. Ibn Abi Malekah said in the hadith of Urwah: Aishah used to recite it:
h
And they thought that they had been denied
, heavy, for denial. He said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Hashimi told us, he said:

c: Ibrahim ibn Saad told us, he said: Salih ibn Kaysan told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, he said:
m: I said to her: His statement:
h
Until when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied

, he said: Aisha said: They were certain that they had been denied. I said: They had been denied. She said: God forbid, the messengers did not think about their Lord, they were only the followers of the messengers, when the revelation was commissioned on their behalf and the affliction became severe upon them, the messengers thought that their followers had denied them, Our victory came to them.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, she said:
m: h
Until the messengers despaired

of those among their people who had denied them that they would believe them, and the messengers thought that those among their people who had believed had denied them, then the victory of God came to them at that time.

x: This is what was narrated about that from Aisha, except that she used to read: they lied, with emphasis and a damma on the kaf, meaning what we mentioned about her: that the messengers thought that their followers who had believed in them had lied to them and had turned away from their religion, because they were impatient for victory. We have shown that what we choose from reading and interpretation in this regard is different from it in this letter in particular.
Others who read his statement: They denied, with a damma on the kaf and a shaddah on the dhal, said: The meaning of that is:
h
until when the messengers despaired

of their people believing in them and confirming them, and the messengers thought, meaning: and were certain, that their nations had denied them, the messengers came to our aid. They said: Suspicion, in this, means knowledge, from the Surat Yusuf 12:110 Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, there came to them Our victory, and whomever We willed was saved.

i: And Our punishment cannot be repelled from the criminal people. saying of the poet:
x: They thought that two thousand knights were wearing their robes in the Persian coat of arms.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan - and this is the statement of Qatada:
m: h
until when the messengers despaired
of the faith of their people, and thought that they had been lied to, that is: they were certain that there was no report among their people and no faith, Our victory came to them.
b.via: Al-Hasan - and this is the statement of Qatada

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Until when the messengers despaired
, he said: from their people, and they thought that they had been lied to, he said: and they knew that they had been lied to, Our victory came to them.

x: This is the reading that was recited by most of the readers of Medina, Basra, and the Levant. I mean by emphasizing the dhal from khadhdhbu and adding a damma to its kaf. This interpretation that Al-Hasan and Qatada went to in that, if it is read with a shaddah on the dhal and a damma on the kaf, is contrary to what we mentioned from the sayings of all those we have mentioned from the companions, because none of them directed suspicion in this place to the meaning of knowledge and certainty, even though suspicion was used by the Arabs in place of knowledge in what was knowledge acquired through report or other than through observation and witnessing. As for what was knowledge acquired through witnessing and witnessing, suspicion is not used in it. You hardly say: I think I am alive, and I think I am a human, meaning: I know that I am a human, and I know that I am alive. And the messengers whom their nations denied, there is no doubt that they were witnesses to their nations, and heard of their denial of them, so it is said about them: they thought that their nations denied them.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid
m: regarding this matter that he said something that is contrary to all the sayings of the past ones whose names we have mentioned and whose sayings we have mentioned, and an interpretation that is different from their interpretation, and a reading that is different from the reading of all of them, which is that, according to what was narrated on his authority, he used to read: And they thought that they had lied, with the kaf and dhal open and the dhal softened. He mentioned the narration about it:

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said, Abu Ubaid told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: that he read it: They lied, with the kaf open and with a light pronunciation. He interpreted it as: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: The messengers despaired of their people being punished, and their people thought that the messengers had lied. Our victory has come to them, he said: The messengers have come with Our victory. Mujahid said: He said in: Al-Mu’min: But when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in what they had of knowledge, he said: Their saying: We are more knowledgeable than them and will not be punished, and His statement: And that which they used to ridicule overtook them, he said: The truth that their messengers brought overtook them.

x: This is a reading that I do not permit reading, because the proof from the readings of the regions is unanimously agreed upon to the contrary. If reading this way were permissible, it would allow for a way of interpretation, which is better than what Mujahid interpreted, which is:
h
until when the messengers despaired

of God’s punishment of their people who denied them, and the messengers thought that their people had lied and fabricated against God by their disbelief in them, and the thought would then be directed to the meaning of knowledge, according to what Al-Hasan and Qatadah interpreted. As for his saying:
h
Then We will save whom We will

, the readings differed in its reading. The majority of the people of Medina, Mecca and Iraq read it as: Fanji Man Nasha We will save whomever We will, with two nuns pronounced lightly, meaning: “We will save whomever We will of Our messengers and those who believe in Us, except for the disbelievers who denied Our messengers.

When the messengers come, We will help them.” Those who read it in this way argued that it was written in the Qur’an with one nun, and its rule is that it should be with two nuns, because one of the two nuns is a letter from the root of the word from anja yanji, and the other nun comes to indicate the future from the action of a group informing about themselves, because they are two letters, I mean the two nuns, of the same type, the second of which is hidden from being shown in speech, so it was deleted from the script, and the confirmed one was sufficient from the deleted one, as is done with the two letters, one of which is assimilated into the other. Some Kufians read it with this meaning, except that they assimilated the second nun and stressed the jim. Another of them read it with emphasis on the jim and the ya’ in the accusative case, meaning he did that to him, from: Najeetuhu anjihu.
Some Meccans read it as: Fanaja man nasha with the opening of the nun and the emphasis, from: Najaa yanjuu.

The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is the reading of those who read: Fanji man nasha with two noons, because this is the reading that is followed in the regions. And whoever differs from it from those who read it with some of the aspects that we mentioned, then his reading is unique from what the evidence is unanimously upon from the readings. And it is not permissible to differ from what was widely read in the readings of the regions.
The interpretation of the statement is: Then We save the messengers and whomever We will of Our believing servants when Our victory comes, as:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Then We save whomever We will, so We save the messengers and whomever We will, “And Our punishment cannot be averted from the criminal people, and that is because God, the Blessed and Exalted, sent the messengers, so they called their people, and informed them that whoever obeyed would be saved, and whoever disobeyed would be punished and led astray. And His statement:
h
And Our punishment will not be averted from the criminal people

, meaning: And Our punishment and Our wrath will not be averted from those whom We afflicted among the disbelievers, from us and from the people who committed crimes and disbelieved in God, and disobeyed His messengers and what they brought to them from Him.

evidence.text: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Arim Abu Al-Nu’man told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, he said, Shu’aib told us, he said, Ibrahim bin Abi Harrah Al-Jazari told me, he said: A young man from Quraysh asked Saeed bin Jubayr and said to him: O Abu Abdullah, how do you recite this letter, for whenever I come to it I wish that I had not recited this surah: Until when the messengers despaired of their people and thought that they had been denied, he said: Yes, until when the messengers despaired of their people believing them, and the ones to whom they were sent thought that the messengers had been denied.
He said: My father used to recite it: They were denied.
Abu Jaafar said: The reading is based on this interpretation that we mentioned in his statement: They lied with a damma on the kaf and a light dhal.
This is also the reading of some of the readers of the people of Medina and most of the readers of the people of Kufa.

Some of those who read this reading went to an interpretation other than the one we chose, and they directed its meaning to: until the messengers despaired of the faith of their people, and the messengers thought that they had been lied to in what they were promised of victory.
So she would recite it: They had been denied, and she would make it heavy.
Ibn Abi Malekah said in the hadith of Urwah: Aishah used to recite it: And they thought that they had been denied, heavy, for denial.
Abu Jaafar said: This is the reading that was recited by most of the readers of Medina, Basra, and the Levant.

This interpretation that Al-Hasan and Qatada went to in that, if it is read with a shaddah on the dhal and a damma on the kaf, is contrary to what we mentioned from the sayings of all those we have mentioned from the companions, because none of them directed suspicion in this place to the meaning of knowledge and certainty, even though suspicion was used by the Arabs in place of knowledge in what was knowledge acquired through report or other than through observation and witnessing.

It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding this matter that he said something that is contrary to all the sayings of the past ones whose names we have mentioned and whose sayings we have mentioned, and an interpretation that is different from their interpretation, and a reading that is different from the reading of all of them, which is that, according to what was narrated on his authority, he used to read: And they thought that they had lied, with the kaf and dhal open and the dhal softened.

Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said, Abu Ubaid told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, that he read it: They lied, with the kaf open and with a light pronunciation.
Abu Jaʿfar said: This is a reading that I do not permit reading, because the proof from the readings of the regions is unanimously agreed upon to the contrary.
As for his saying: Then We will save whom We will, the readings differed in its reading.

The majority of the people of Medina, Mecca and Iraq read it as: Fanji Man Nasha We will save whomever We will, with two nuns pronounced lightly, meaning: “We will save whomever We will of Our messengers and those who believe in Us, except for the disbelievers who denied Our messengers.

Those who read it in this way argued that it was written in the Qur’an with one nun, and its rule is that it should be with two nuns, because one of the two nuns is a letter from the root of the word from anja yanji, and the other nun comes to indicate the future from the action of a group informing about themselves, because they are two letters, I mean the two nuns, of the same type, the second of which is hidden from being shown in speech, so it was deleted from the script, and the confirmed one was sufficient from the deleted one, as is done with the two letters, one of which is assimilated into the other.
Some Kufians read it with this meaning, except that they assimilated the second nun and stressed the jim.
Another of them read it with emphasis on the jim and the ya’ in the accusative case, meaning he did that to him, from: Najeetuhu anjihu.
Some Meccans read it as: Fanaja man nasha with the opening of the nun and the emphasis, from: Najaa yanjuu.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is the reading of those who read: Fanji man nasha with two noons, because this is the reading that is followed in the regions.
And whoever differs from it from those who read it with some of the aspects that we mentioned, then his reading is unique from what the evidence is unanimously upon from the readings.
And it is not permissible to differ from what was widely read in the readings of the regions.

x: God Almighty says: There was in the stories of Joseph and his brothers a lesson for the people of wisdom and intellects to take heed from, and an admonition to be exalted by. And that is because after Joseph was thrown into the well to perish, then he was sold as a slave for a low price, and after the long imprisonment and confinement, He made him king of Egypt, empowered him in the land, and raised him above those of his brothers who sought to harm him, and reunited him with his parents and brothers by His power, after a long period, and brought them to Him from the distant, distant plain, so He, the Most High, said to the polytheists of Quraysh, from the people of His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: There was indeed for you, O people, in their stories a lesson if you would take heed, that the One who did that to Joseph and his brothers, it is not difficult for Him to do the same to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so He brought him out from among you, then made him victorious over you, empowered him in the country, and supported him with soldiers and men from among the followers and companions, even if hardships befell him, and days, nights, ages and times came against him.
Mujahid used to say: The meaning of this is: There was a lesson in their stories for Joseph and his brothers.
The novel mentioned that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There was certainly in their stories a lesson
, for Joseph and his brothers.

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Shababah told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: A lesson for Joseph and his brothers.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding
, he said: Joseph and his brothers.

x: This statement that Mujahid said, even if it has a possible interpretation, what we have said about it is more appropriate, because it follows the report about our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and about his people from the polytheists, and follows their threat and warning for disbelief in God and in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and is separate from the report of Joseph and his brothers. Despite that, it is a general report about all people of understanding that their stories are a lesson for them, and it is not specific to some of them and not others. So if the matter was as we described in that, then it is more likely to be a report that it is a lesson for others. The narration that we mentioned from Mujahid from the narration of Ibn Jurayj is more likely to be from his statement, because that is in agreement with the statement that we have said about that.
And His saying:
h
It was not a fabricated hadith
, God Almighty says: This statement was not a fabricated hadith, lied about, or guessed, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
It was not a fabricated hadith

, and fabrication is lying. But the confirmation of what is before it, he says: But the confirmation of what is before it of the books of God that He revealed before it to His prophets, such as the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms, he confirms all of that and bears witness to it that all of it is true from God, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: But the confirmation of what was before it, and the Criterion is the confirmation of the books that came before it, and it bears witness to them. And His saying:
h
And the details of everything

, the Most High says: It is also the details of everything that the servants need from the clarification of God’s commands and prohibitions, His lawful and unlawful things, and His obedience and disobedience. And His statement:
h
And guidance and mercy for a people who believe

, God Almighty says: It is a clarification of His command and guidance for those who are ignorant of the path of truth and are blind to it, if they follow it and are guided by it from their misguidance, and mercy, for those who believe in it and act according to what is in it, saving them from the wrath of God and His painful punishment, and inheriting His Paradise in the Hereafter and eternal bliss, for a people who believe, He says: for a people who believe in the Qur’an and what is in it of God’s promise and threat, His command and prohibition, so Surat Yusuf 12:111
h
There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding

. It was not a fabricated statement, but a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of all things and a guidance and mercy for a people who believe. they act according to what is in it of His command and refrain from what is in it of His prohibition.
